I just assembled this and mounted it to a desk today and I am impressed with the build quality and the clamp mount. It seems to hold to the desk very well. However, I ran across two design flaws everyone needs to know about, that made me give this the lowest rating. First, there is absolutely no tilt or swing adjustability on the center monitor mount position. It will rotate between landscape and portrait orientation, but no tilt or side to side adjustment capability at all. And I looked all over the product page and it doesn't mention that shortcoming. Second, the side monitor mounts have full adjustability with hex wrench bolts for loosening or tightening the adjustments. However, the hex adjustment bolt for tightening/loosening the side to side angle is up inside the mounting assembly in such a way that you cannot get to it. I had to tighten it, and I ended up having to completely disassemble that mount to tighten one bolt that is supposed to be user adjustable. Although not a design flaw, the product page does mention an optional grommet mount, but there were no instructions (or possibly even hardware) included for mounting that way.

review_title: Choose carefully if your Monitor/TV is close to the weight cap. before buying this!
review_text: The mount claims to be adequate for up to 30kg/66lbs. When I installed the 40" LCD (42lb.) Television, the mount was under such a tremendous stress, due to the location which demanded that the picoting arm remain fully extended, that it sagged fully 2". Considering that the mounts arm entire reach was approx. 20", that was really cause for concern. The mount would very likely be entirely suited for the television I was installing if the normal position was folded back during general usage. Then extended only for access to the rear, or even used only occasionally while fully extended. As my situation required being installed in a tight corner, and normal use was to be fully stretched out, the safety of the persons using the TV as well as the TV itself if it was to either tear out the of the wall, or the arm bracing itself failed would be a liability. It also should be noted that the included lag bolts were insufficient themselves under higher stressed loads. I did the initial install using larger bolts to begin with because the provided (2) were certainly inadequate. I would say that any monitor or television under 40lbs/18kg would be perfectly safe.

While I was out running errands, I stopped by my parents' house to see if they had any scrap wood around, and I found a decent piece that was about 5 feet tall, less than 6 inches wide, and around 1/2 inch thick. He drilled about 12 screws through the wood and into the wall for stability, which is now more stable than the wall itself! Since I'd seen other reviews suggesting to take the plate off before installing the wall mount, that's where we started. Due to that, he didn't even need (or want) my assistance until it came time to screw the plate-fastened 32" LCD tv to it, and all I did was hold the tv in place while he screwed it in. I must say, I absolutely love the swivel aspect of this mount (which is our first), though I didn't notice how we could angle the tv towards the bed. It's perfect the way it is now, though. I do want to point out that the instructions show which way the plate goes onto the wall (the two screw slots on top with the one screw slot on bottom), though he did it wrong. It's still stable, and he doesn't want to switch it. I doubt we'll run into any issues with it though, mostly because of the wood plank it's attached to. review_title: Replace the Mounting Hardware And see theses tips for Mounting to Studs
review_text: The Wall Mount itself is excellent. Unfortunately, I had to replace all of the mounting hardware with my own. The lag screws are terrible (one broke), the wall anchors don’t work (I replaced with toggle bolts), and the bolts to attach to the TV were too long for my television. So, as for the attaching this to a stud.... The bracket that attaches to the wall connects with two connections at the top and one at the bottom. The two holes at the top are spaced so that both cannot be screwed into a stud. When you place this, measure it out so that one of the top holes and the bottom hole enter the stud - and connect with lag screws. Then use a toggle bolt for the second top connection. This produced a very secure connection for my television.

review_text: UPDATE: I've used it now for a few days under various conditions and have updated my score to reflect how I feel about it. The good: 1. Ok so let's first clarify.. I am not the kind of woman that would spend $400 on a vacuum of any kind, despite my ability to do so. However, I do spend a lot of time researching products, and all kinds of "animals" and "sharks" and everything in between, and I want to be up to date. I spent about a month in fact researching name brands, cordless and corded, of all varieties. Then all of a sudden, in the middle of the night while browsing on my Amazon app (do you sleep with your cell phone?) this little gem came to my attention. First thing that caught my eye was the "extras".. the cute attachment that vacuums drapes! Have you seen any other manufacturer offer this up without costing extra? I haven't... Second thing was the floor attachment had a rotating brush head in it. Red and blue, who would have guessed! Then, to my surprise, the reviews were actually not too bad! The price was perfect, and the time was right. So, finally, after a month of research and half a dozen "Save Until Later" decisions, I added to my cart and hit "Process My Order". It arrived today! No, I have no spare time right now, but I just had to share this one! Right out of the box, a nice quality box I might add, I could see the multitude of add ons. Everything well packed and wrapped in plastic. I was so excited that I grabbed the engine by its handle right through the plastic, and ...oops! I accidentally pulled the trigger and the thing started roaring! Quick thinking, I triggered twice and it turned off. But great thing was, it came with a charge! I could tear off the plastic, pull out the hose section from the box and snap it on, and in seconds I was vacuuming my living room rug, which desperately needed a good vacuum! (I do have another cordless, with a floor attachment, but the B&D product is not meant for floors, take it from me!) No need to hold a trigger here. Just one pull turns it on low, second pull turns it on high, and third pull turns it off. I kept it on high for about 3 minutes to try it out. I glanced at the dust cup and went, WOW! Ok, everyone, this thing actually does have amazing suction on low pile rugs. Not only did it clean the dirt I could see, but it cleaned the dirt I couldn't see. The "grayish" areas of my rug began to turn ivory again! Three minutes of suction, right out of the box, and look at what it picked up. Cat hair and all! (see pics) The attachments (4) are easy to snap on and off, and there is no real brain power needed to figure out how to use it. The wall bracket comes with screws and anchors, which I will deal with later. The AC adapter plugs right into the motorhead without needing the wall bracket, so I can charge the battery anywhere. Oh, and the motorhead has a battery charge indicator so I will know when I need to recharge it! I'm sure there's more to discover, but this is a pretty good starting point, don't you think? Next on my list, charge it in full, and try the drape cleaner! How cat hair manages to get on the top of the drapes still amazes me. I cannot attest to how it will last, and if I had regular carpet I might go with a corded product, but first impressions, I made the right choice and didn't waste $400 of my hard earned money on an animal appliance that probably cost $50 to make. Isn't the best feeling in the world finding a good product at a fair price? Happy to say I feel good about my purchase, and as a dedicated Amazon shopper, that's all that matters! Well, after family, and humanity, and peace on earth! If anything goes wrong, I'll keep you informed.

I'm astounded by some of the previous reviewers who were comparing this to a Dyson favorably. Not only is that misleading, it's bad enough for me to state unequivocally that those people either haven't experienced a Dyson, or are lying. The power of the Proscenic P8 is far more comparable to a Walmart $20 handheld vacuum than a Dyson. Seriously. On the high power setting the suction is weak. And nothing illustrates this better than the small crevice tool. The opening is only 1/4" x 1". Even after funneling all of the suction through that tiny opening it's weak. Compare that to the Dyson crevice tool which has an opening 400% larger and, well... again it is NO comparison. (See photo.) To be clear, I'm really not being that picky. I have two portable Dysons and two plug in units in my home. I also built a workshop and wanted something for the shop, but didn't really want to spend Dyson money. I'd have been happy with something that was a reasonable approximation. But this vacuum is all show - no go. Sure there are a lots of attachments, and the battery is swappable (though EXTREMELY hard to remove), but it doesn't matter if the thing won't get the job done. Especially if it won't do it better than something you can get from Walmart for a fraction of the price. Another area that is vastly inferior to the Dyson is the charging. Although you can technically hang this unit on a wall, it won't charge when you hang it. In fact, you must remove the battery to charge it every time. Meaning that just living with this unit will be a huge pain in the you know what. Generally speaking, avoid this vacuum at all costs.

Please DO NOT waste your time or money on this. All the favorable reviews on here must be from employees or sponsored. Again, do not waste your hard earned money.

I just assembled this and mounted it to a desk today and I am impressed with the build quality and the clamp mount. It seems to hold to the desk very well. However, I ran across two design flaws everyone needs to know about, that made me give this the lowest rating. First, there is absolutely no tilt or swing adjustability on the center monitor mount position. It will rotate between landscape and portrait orientation, but no tilt or side to side adjustment capability at all. And I looked all over the product page and it doesn't mention that shortcoming. Second, the side monitor mounts have full adjustability with hex wrench bolts for loosening or tightening the adjustments. However, the hex adjustment bolt for tightening/loosening the side to side angle is up inside the mounting assembly in such a way that you cannot get to it. I had to tighten it, and I ended up having to completely disassemble that mount to tighten one bolt that is supposed to be user adjustable. Although not a design flaw, the product page does mention an optional grommet mount, but there were no instructions (or possibly even hardware) included for mounting that way.

This monitor stand has become a lifesaver for me. At work, I use 3 monitors and my laptop display since we are paperless. Our company doesn't provide risers so I actually had my monitors stacked on rems of paper to get them to a comfortable level. It took me about 30 minutes to install it. A couple of the pieces I put in backwards so had to take some of it apart and correct it. Once I was finished I was so happy with the product. The 2 side monitors will slide in and out, tilt up and down and turn side to side. You do have to play with the bolts to get it where you can adjust it without a tool but once you find that sweet spot, you are good to go. As other have mentioned in reviews (which were extremely harsh I found), the middle monitor is pretty stationary. I actually didn't notice until I just read the other reviews that it doesn't move. I've had no desire to try to move it. The monitor height goes up and down with the pole that is connected to the desk. If you position your monitors at the correct height, you shouldn't need to tilt them anyway. All together, I'm extremely pleased with my purchase. Others in the office are looking into the same stands as I have also.

Built like a tank is the best thing I can say about this monitor mount. When you have as many computer monitors around your house like I do you find that sometimes you mount the monitor to the wall and throw away the stand just to realize that your wife wants you to put the monitor somewhere else that needs to be put back on the stand that you threw away, that is where this mount comes into play. The mount is made of solid steel except for the plastic cover used to cover the base. The welds are very strong and this mount is built to last a lifetime. All points used for adjusting the monitor mount have easy to use handles that make it simple to adjust. What is really nice about this mount is the fact that now I have the ability to move the monitor into different positions than what I could do with the original stand mount it came with. As for the Vesa mounting holes they lined up perfectly with the 100x100 that my monitor had in it. I love that they included the screws for attaching the monitor to the stand. Mounting brackets is very well built and holds onto my desktop very securely. Once it is tightened down you can move the monitor around with the mount staying in place.

This monitor stand is VERY NICE! The overall quality of this stand is great! Got the package in the mail and didn't realize the stand would be so heavy or thought the stand would be cheap and light because of the price. The stand is very adjustable, you can move the height for eye level or anything below and or above, you can also swivel the monitor vertical if that's something you might want. When mounting the stand to the desk, it tightens very good, so the monitor shouldn't move anywhere no matter the weight. The metal construction of the mount and stand is very good and has some weight to it which shows in the quality of the product. Everything that came in the box was packaged well and came with a minimum of parts that had to be installed. It is almost plug in play, just have to screw in the monitor and the bracket and tighten the bolts down to make sure everything is just right. Once the monitor is in place you can move the monitor all around if you want it closer to you or further away. I will definitely get another one if I get another monitor or need one for another computer. One very nice stand for the money!

review_title: Choose carefully if your Monitor/TV is close to the weight cap. before buying this!
review_text: The mount claims to be adequate for up to 30kg/66lbs. When I installed the 40" LCD (42lb.) Television, the mount was under such a tremendous stress, due to the location which demanded that the picoting arm remain fully extended, that it sagged fully 2". Considering that the mounts arm entire reach was approx. 20", that was really cause for concern. The mount would very likely be entirely suited for the television I was installing if the normal position was folded back during general usage. Then extended only for access to the rear, or even used only occasionally while fully extended. As my situation required being installed in a tight corner, and normal use was to be fully stretched out, the safety of the persons using the TV as well as the TV itself if it was to either tear out the of the wall, or the arm bracing itself failed would be a liability. It also should be noted that the included lag bolts were insufficient themselves under higher stressed loads. I did the initial install using larger bolts to begin with because the provided (2) were certainly inadequate. I would say that any monitor or television under 40lbs/18kg would be perfectly safe.

review_title: Exactly what I was hoping for, and will buy the same brand for the larger tv in the family room
review_text: We ran into a few issues while trying to install this wall mount, mainly because we didn't have a drill (until he went to the store), AND there aren't any studs in our manufactured home (that I know of). While I was out running errands, I stopped by my parents' house to see if they had any scrap wood around, and I found a decent piece that was about 5 feet tall, less than 6 inches wide, and around 1/2 inch thick. He drilled about 12 screws through the wood and into the wall for stability, which is now more stable than the wall itself! Since I'd seen other reviews suggesting to take the plate off before installing the wall mount, that's where we started. Due to that, he didn't even need (or want) my assistance until it came time to screw the plate-fastened 32" LCD tv to it, and all I did was hold the tv in place while he screwed it in. I must say, I absolutely love the swivel aspect of this mount (which is our first), though I didn't notice how we could angle the tv towards the bed. It's perfect the way it is now, though. I do want to point out that the instructions show which way the plate goes onto the wall (the two screw slots on top with the one screw slot on bottom), though he did it wrong. It's still stable, and he doesn't want to switch it. I doubt we'll run into any issues with it though, mostly because of the wood plank it's attached to. Were it screwed into a stud in a regular home, I might argue. Though I received this product at a discount for my honest review, I'd definitely recommend this wall mount, and we'll go with the same brand for the 50" living room tv very soon.

review_title: Replace the Mounting Hardware And see theses tips for Mounting to Studs
review_text: The Wall Mount itself is excellent. Unfortunately, I had to replace all of the mounting hardware with my own. The lag screws are terrible (one broke), the wall anchors don’t work (I replaced with toggle bolts), and the bolts to attach to the TV were too long for my television. So, as for the attaching this to a stud.... The bracket that attaches to the wall connects with two connections at the top and one at the bottom. The two holes at the top are spaced so that both cannot be screwed into a stud. When you place this, measure it out so that one of the top holes and the bottom hole enter the stud - and connect with lag screws. Then use a toggle bolt for the second top connection. This produced a very secure connection for my television.

review_title: If you're handy, should be pretty easy to install
review_text: I used this for our 32" Sony HDTV. Very simply boxed and the instructions are not the most helpful but if you're handy, it's really not that difficult to figure out. The parts are a little tight/stiff when you first get it, but just a little WD40 gets the hinges to move smoothly. Recommend doing this before you begin installation and oil the parts well first. Also, please measure the mount holes in the back of your TV to make sure they are compatible. The holes are located in the following: 75mm x 75mm (3"x3"), 100mm x 100mm(4"x4"), 100mm x 200mm(4"x8"), 200mm x 200mm(8"x8"). Once you mount it to a stud in the wall (I do recommend using your own hardware instead of the ones provided), the entire process takes only a few minutes. Note that this also is much easier for two people doing this but one person can also handle the installation. All in all, for the retailed price point, this is a very good product and I'd consider purchasing another one for my computer monitor. review_title: Shootout with the Wildgame Innovations Crush 20 Lightsout
review_text: I am comparing this camera to the Wildgame Innovations Crush 20 Lightsout. I bought both at the same time for about the same price. Specifications are also close. The Wildgame is 20 megapixel, though, compared to the TEC at 12 megapixel, but TEC has audio and Wildlife does not. I will update this review as I test each unit more. The first TEC.Bean unit had a jammed battery compartment. This was a good test of their customer support at Nova Tech. They responded fast, professional, and solved the issue quick. Set Up Both cameras were easy to setup and learn. Settings Each had settings the other did not have. The TEC has much better timestamp settings. And timestamps geo position, temperature, and lunar phase. I could only get the Wildgame to display date and time. However, the Wildgame has a setting for sensitivity. Quality Wildgame has hands down the best video quality. At night, the TEC is super grainy. The Wildgame is not anywhere close to that level of graininess. In the day, the Wildgame is noticeably sharper. Watertight TEC has been 100% watertight and tested with several rain storms. The Wildgame was wet inside in the same conditions. It was wet enough that I will get it exchanged and hope that it was a failure with that unit. Triggering I feel as if both camera were equal in triggering. Both had false alarms and both seem to trigger late at times or totally miss an event. The Wildgame lets you control sensitivity, though, so at least you can experiment. Conclusions I will keep updating this review as I compare the 2 units. Right now, I like the Wildgame much better. I think video quality at night is the biggest deciding factor. I will, however, move the cameras around my property to see how they perform in different lighting conditions.

It's rugged, it comes in a great case, and the photos it takes are very good. Those are the positives. On the negative side: *When I placed this in a tree in the yard, side by side with another camera of a different make, they both took photos that the other camera missed. But most disconcerting was that the Tec.Bean totally missed a daylight photo of me standing 50 feet away waving! Didn't capture that photo at all. *Night photos, even close ones (15-20') are grainy. The flash doesn't seem to be all that good, and this is close range compared to its 75 foot claim! *For some odd reason the card that comes out of this camera can't be read by my card reader. It's exactly the same card I use in the other brand camera, which can be read. Perplexing. I can hook up the USB between camera and computer and read it that way, so there is a work-around. *Lastly, in spite of what I've heard from other reviewers here, customer support seems very lax. In fact no where in their included paperwork (warranty card and user manual) is there any information on how to contact them. Others here suggested that I email them from their Amazon page, which I did. They did respond, but their answer wasn't helpful, and there has been no further communication from them over the past 4 work-week days. Edit: I received an email from Bella at TEC.BEAN today addressing most of my concerns with the camera. Actually, she addressed them all, but in reality, all of my negative comments are still valid, with the exception of customer support being difficult to get hold of. Once you find out how to email her, then she does provide good communication. And I believe that she truly wants to make things right. She assure me that they will get contact info printed in the included paperwork in the near future. Her fixes for my problems stated above are suggestion that I'd already tried, so those problems remain. I've changed my rating from three to four stars. If they had an option for three and half stars, that's what I'd give.

review_title: Video quality is great! Also has more features than others I have used.
review_text: This one has more features than the others I have used. I have always borrowed these from friends until I decided to buy this one. Video quality is great and it records audio. I set it up using hybrid mode, which takes a photo and then a video. The manual that comes with it does a pretty good job explaining everything this camera can do. You can even hook it up with a power adapter that you have to buy separately. It comes with a strap, a/v cable to hook up to TV, manual, and a USB cable to connect it to you computer to SD card if your computer doesn't have a SD card reader. Setup is a breeze because it has a built in screen, you can change all the settings and see what it sees before switching it to on. Overall this camera is great, durable, and easy to use. It takes 8 AA batteries and an SD card both of which are not included.

review_title: I'd suggest looking at a different trail camera
review_text: I purchased this camera mostly for security monitoring, and it has been so-so at best. Regardless of the settings I have used, I do not get ANY pictures or videos after dark. I've even gone out to test this myself by walking past and standing in its range to no avail. Using a flashlight doesn't even get it to respond. I hope that means I have a dud, but who knows. Also, for my purpose, I wanted to use the picture and video feature that they have - except that I an only get 1 picture and the video is almost always worthless. That is, I'll get a pic in good focus but the subject is more than halfway through the frame, and the video doesn't have any of the subject. The microphone seems rather of a novelty as well. Conversations that happen within 5 feet of the camera are often not picked up, and if they are, they are completely unintelligible. You can hear some slight vocal sounds, but no chance of knowing what was being said. I emailed the manufacturer support email about my issues, but never received a response. I was trying to give them a chance to correct the issues, but it seems that is not going to happen. All that being said, the pictures it does take look good. I do not have a way to test the trigger speed, but I would be surprised if it is better than 1.2s as humans walking often make it fully across the frame without being caught.

review_title: Easy Set Up - Good List of Features
review_text: This is my first Game and Trail Camera. I wanted a camera like this just out of curiosity as to what critters of the four and two legged type might be lurking around my farm. I chose this as it as it has gotten same good reviews here and on YouTube and for the features seemed to be priced right. Pros: Despite this being my first trail camera, it took me only a few minutes to make the settings and get it operational. The 2" LCD screen helped enormously there. Lots of option including time lapse and hybrid which allows you to take time lapse pictures and pictures with the motion detector at the same time The pictures are good quality even when only using the 8 MegaPixel setting. Comes with a nice camo case. CON If there is any con with the camera it is the strap that comes with it. Unlike the well camouflaged camera, it is black. It might as well be a white flag to would be thieves. This is common thing with these trail cameras though. Still, I would recommend finding another means of attaching your camera to make it less visible. Other than the one con, I am very happy with the camera. Good value, seems well made, easy set up, and a good host of features.

review_title: Good concept but far from a quality product
review_text: Used brand new lithium batteries. Saw the percentage go down from 80 to 50 while I was setting it up. Then it shut off. Put brand new regular batteries and it did the same thing. Sending it back because it didn’t have enough juice for me to finish setting it up. The camera doesn’t come with a wall outlet although if you have one that fits then it’s possible to set it up. The options and availability of them are nice and the concept is great! As others have posted, the instructions are a bit different. They mostly tell you how to navigate through the camera but don’t really explain what the settings are for. You have an option to contact manufacturer (via Watsapp 😅) for a free 16gb sd card. I wish the manufacturer luck in getting this product off the ground and working, but in the meantime it’s a small operation where the quality is a hit or miss.

There are so many hunting camera choices on the market and it took me around a month to read all of the comments and reviews and combine them to make a decision which one is the ONE. This camera costs about $25 – 30, more expensive than others, but I needed a good gift for my friend who is a hunter for many years. Don’t get me wrong he has an equipment including couple of cameras, but it is some time past away after he bought them. They are many years old. I think it is time to renovate. I join him sometimes for his hunting adventures. He uses me as a pack mule and I am taking for a hiking trip. 8 AA batteries (I would include it the package for such price ) allow this camera to work independently for number of days 24 hrs a day. It has sensors that reacting on movement(s), it has night vision mode and it creates high quality pictures. It is like being there by yourself but no weapon. My friend is saying you can not have enough of them because there are so many places watch over. The places of activities of the animals is various from year to year (season to season) and using the camera gives a hunter a huge advantage. I will grade it 5 stars but I will update it later if some manufacture issues are found (I hope it will be NONE )

review_title: Cannot Recommend This Camera - Will be Looking for Another Brand
review_text: Worked okay in Winter. But this Spring and Summer, filled the feeder trough with food on multiple occasions. About all I got was a raccoon exiting the scene. Should have been a whole lot of footage. Holes dug around the feeder, food gone... indications that the animals were there for a good period of time - and yes, the time parameters were set correctly to cover the targeted period (7pm to 7am). Of course the camera did get footage of me filling the trough around 9pm and checking the "empty" trough around 6am in the morning. But nothing in between. Camera seems to have no problem picking up on big-fat-old me walking through the field of view. And yes, the batteries (Energizer) have been changed on multiple occasions. Basically, in May I was using the same system settings that worked in Winter (hybrid mode), but this time hardly any animal footage captured. Changed to picture-only mode - raccoon leaving the scene picture and not much else. There were actually more pictures with nothing in them. I have been working with the camera settings since May (now mid-July) - nothing works. It's almost like since the temperature outside at night is 70 to 75 degrees Fahrenheit and the animals are warm-blooded, maybe the IR sensors can't make the distinction that something is there. I'm much bigger than the armadillo, raccoons, bunnies, and bobcat that the camera captured in the Winter, so maybe that is why the camera sees me. As for the Winter videos, they had such a hot spot in the center (about 15 feet away) that you could not see the animal in that area. The pictures that accompanied the Winter videos were not this way. Additionally as noted in many reviews, the broken-English manual is not much help. Seems like the company could at least spend a few bucks to hire an English-speaking tech writer for the English-speaking audience. Not much of a manual so would be cheap to do. This is actually the second Tech Bean camera we got. The first came with a broken USB port, but that was returned and replaced by this one without incident. Anyway, it was fun in the Winter while it lasted even though the videos were too hot to keep. And although I believe this may still be under warranty, I'm tired of wasting time on it, so off to the dumpster it goes. I'll be trying another.

I happen to see this game camera on amazon and decided to purchase it. I am really glad that I did, and I am very impressed with the craftsmanship and quality of the whole system. The camera is small and compact but provides high quality features and functionality. It comes packaged very well with a great set of instructions, a quick start guide, and there is even a card in the package that tells you how to get a free SD card to use with it. The camera will accept up to 32 GB SD card and you can even get a wifi SD card to use in it so that you can download your pictures and videos without opening the camera. The instructions and the cameras onboard menus are extremely easy to use and provides great functionality to the camera. The camera has 1080p ability, and the few test shots I took with it were very clear and in focus. The camera comes with cords to download your pictures or to play them on your tv. It also comes with a strap to help mount the camera to a fixed object. The case has several different tripod mounting screws if you decide to use with a tripod. The case is very well sealed, much like with the type of system you would find on a pelican box with the locking latches. I will definitely be telling all my friends and family about this game camera, it is a great buy without having to break the bank.

review_title: Great pictures. love the hybrid mode
review_text: Update: quit working within 2mo. Will not turn on and batteries are all good. First trail camera. Great pictures. love the hybrid mode. Does everything it is intended to do to include showing me a ten-point buck roaming the farm and a juvenile black bear making the farm his new home. Would not have known otherwise. Friend has a cuddleback camera from Cabelas and it is ridiculous to try and even use when it comes to settings. this is easy to use. Only dislike is that it is slow when it comes to switching between on/off/test mode. Test mode being where you access all settings. It is even slower after you delete all images on the SD card from the camera, it takes a full minute or two to do anything other than say No Image. I use it with a Slate River EZ Aim Game Camera Mount and it works great.

review_title: Good Camera, but old video format
review_text: The camera seems well built, for the price. I chose to use the Lithium AA batteries for longer life. I also selected the Toshiba FlashAir WiFi SD card, allowing photo/video download to a smartphone via WiFi. Some oddities: The camera appears to record video as motion-jpeg (MJPG) in an AVI container (file format). Wow. these are **old** standards (as opposed to H.264 in an MP4 container). With this old video format the Toshiba FlashAir App does not appear to recognize the video files on the SD card (meaning in the App's Photo/Video view only shows photo). The good news is the App also provides a File/Folder view of the SD card, which allows both the photos and videos to be access (viewed and downloaded to the smartphone). The free Android/iOS VLC media player will player MJPG encoded AVI formatted video recorded by the camera. I have also have not been able to delete photos/videos using the Toshiba FlashAir App (does not appear to be an option for deleting). To delete you will need to use the camera's front panel interface. With the camera in the Test mode, press the “Replay” (up arrow) button. Then use the left and right arrows to scroll through the images. To delete an image, press the “DEL” (down arrow) key. You are then presented with the option to delete only this image or to delete ALL images.

This is the only Trail Cam I have used so I can not compare it to others; my review is based on how well the Trail Cam full fills the expectations set by the sales material. 1. THE PRODUCT: Form follows function; yup the design must enhance the function of the product first and then please the eye second. Tec.Bean nailed this with great attention to design detail for every function. Images, the real reason for the product: day light images are excellent and night time IR images are excellent and much better than I expected. The design and build quality are on the same level as Anker and Apple. The only improvement would be to re-label “TEST” mode to “TEST & CONFIGURE”. 2. INSTRUCTION MANUAL: The English version 3.0 is well written, no hint of Chinglish, with good formatting. The only improvements: would be to provide a little more description of the different modes of operation, and to make a PDF version of the latest manual available. As of Dec’17 version 3.0 was not available for download. 3. CUSTOMER SUPPORT: My unit developed a boot failure after about 45 days of ownership and 8 days of operation. They sent me a new replacement unit! Suggested improvement to management - be sure to acknowledge all support requests within 24 hours so we know the email was successful.

review_title: Does not do what I thought it would.
review_text: In general, this is probably a nice unit depending on what you want to use it for. The description says "For hunting and animal observation (also for cold blooded animals or amphibians); for indoor & outdoor security surveillance; for professional wildlife monitoring and researching." I thought having the cold-blooded capability was a bonus. It turns out that the motion detection mode works *only* for cold-blooded animals. Unfortunately, motion detection is the one feature I really need and it doesn't work for at all with a warm-blooded trigger. So disappointing. Will be returned.

This camera is very high quality, it takes amazing pictures! The manual is a little hard to read but don't let that scare you it's a wonderful product! It is a MUST HAVE for anyone that hunts. This camera is built so strong it is tough!! I love that it has a viewing screen on the camera! The mounting of this camera is absolutely easy to install thanks to the awesome straps and looking through the viewing screen! This case products the camera through all weather elements! You won't have to worry about water ruining your memory card, or the camera! Overall, I couldn't be happier this is a phenomenal camera and I love it! I'm thrilled I purchased this and I know you will also love it! The price on this is about perfect!

review_title: Hope you weren't hoping to use this camera soon....
review_text: I am giving this product a provisional 1 star rating because the manual is written in Chingish and is nearly impossible to decipher. Much time is spent touting the features but the grammar is so abysmal that you will end up contacting the company in an effort to figure out how to work the thing. If the company gets back to me....nowhere do they have their contact info in the manual....with some explanations of their terribly written manual, this camera is going back to Amazon. Do not expect to open the box and use this camera !!!1

review_title: Fast trigger speed, crisp photos, a great cam!
review_text: This is a GREAT trail camera for the deer hunter!! The quality is so much better than that of the previous trail cams we have owned! It has a playback feature/screen right on the front of the camera! No more pulling the card and taking it back to the laptop in the car to check the photos. The pictures and video are sharp and clear! No more blurry photos! The trigger speed is QUICK even catching birds in flight! So many great functions that a lot of trail cams do not have. So far, the batteries are still holding up after almost 2 weeks. I can't say that our previous cams lasted more than a few days. This trail cam is well worth every dime!!

I was a little reluctant to purchase this product. I had not heard of TEC.BEAN. I didn't know what to expect. I am here to tell you , I couldn't be happier. It is every thing I was hoping for and more. I purchased this to watch when animals were traveling a certain trail. It takes great pictures and videos. You can delete unwanted pics. Set video and or pictures and the intervals of when the take them or set to motion detection. comes with strap to attach to a tree, to hook up to your computer and see the pics on your monitor. You can also hook to your tv and watch them. It has a time stamp so each pic or video taken you know when it was taken. Color pics during daytime. I would recommend this to anyone. Hunters animal watchers or to monitor homes or about anything you need to monitor. Thanks for such a great product. That is only a few reasons I gave it a 5 star rating.

review_title: Great design and practically can do more than the regular ...
review_text: Great design and practically can do more than the regular camera in the wild or dark, I am amazed by its compact size. Its outside appearance makes it perfectly camouflaged, blends well among the trees in the woods. It has different modes and features, such as, time-lapse, video recording, motion detection . IT also recorded time-stamp, temperature, time, moon-phase, etc. I also can setup a password to protect the options and prevent it from any unexpected change. It runs quietly, and the night picture comes pretty bright, so the IR LED works well. I believe with those features I could hardly find anything is better than this. Overall, it’s a great product.

review_title: A lot of Technology in this Little Cam
review_text: This Little Camera takes beautiful pictures and videos with sound, has a lot of options. Very well constructed, you could probably stand on it without damage. Very easy to hide, I put it in a big bush and could hardly see it at 5 feet and never would see it if you didn't know it was there. Taking me some time to get used to it. So far for me I like the time lapse feature best because you can see everything going on way outside of any motion sensor range, obviously with it using 36 infrared LEDs for a good image at night on time lapse it uses batteries up faster, as does setting it up and trying different functions. I am also going to try and use the LED Screen less now that I am getting a little more used to the functions and see if batteries don't last a bit longer.. Still playing with it though, takes some time to learn, especially if you have never used one and I'm not that Tech-Savy. If I can do it anyone can. I saw someone say Customer service was non-existent. I found them to be the opposite, very helpful. I sent them an Email through Amazon and checked my email a couple hours later, they had already responded. Update: Had camera over 60 days now, I must have thrown my book away with newspapers. I called Tech Support a second time. Again they responded fast, had already emailed me the user manual. Thank You!

review_title: Leery of battery life claims based on internal usage indicator
review_text: Have mouse problem in basement & set this up on tripod with $10 power converter as I've experienced very poor battery life (according to the indicator at least-I did not use lithium, but did use brand new Duracell-After two nights on battery, indicator said battery life was at 45%). Set it to motion detect/video with a desk lamp for illumination (better clarity). Activates with motion, but not all the time.... I think. It could be that there is a pause time after after each video clip before "arming" itself again. Anyway, I had bait there in one clip with a mouse "exploring", next clip..... no bait!

This is a great game camera. I've never had any others, but I like that it doesn't have any red light when it's recording so the bears will hopefully not see it and rip it down. So far so good. Only have seen some small game but we will not only use it for hunting but also for monitoring what it coming around our animals housing. All our animals (rabbits, chickens, goats etc) have secure houses that they are locked in at night and have had a couple encounters with eagles and such trying to get at our birds. Even had a raccoon trying to open the latch on our coop so we put a lock on it. This will help with that and hopefully help us to know whether we will be able to get some big game this year. The picture is clear and it just takes a ad card that we insert into our laptop. This is very fancy and my hubby loves it

I have been looking for a camera like this for awhile now. I am glad I pulled the trigger on this one because it has features that I didn't even know I needed. For example, no lights to alert people of a camera. This is particularly important when you are not uploading to a cloud where data is protected. It saves photos to a SIM card that is inside the unit. Loving the camouflage outside as well, which also helps to not alert people of its presence. I can't wait to see what is on the SIM card! Good quality camera and images on my original tests. Look how hard it is to see even when I am pointing the camera at it.

review_title: but this does not make it a worse camera compared with others
review_text: This is my second trail camera. I bought this because I was impressed with its 9 photos per trigger! Compared with other trail cameras, it does not have an impressively wide angle lense, but this does not make it a worse camera compared with others. It functioned well in rainy and windy days. The battery life is also satisfactory. I got much more pictures with this one than my previous one. The company recommends use a 16gb SD card for best performance. Another thing I appreciate is that the seller offers one-year warranty, so I am pretty confident in its quality.

review_title: A quality camera for all your game tracking needs!!
review_text: TEC.BEAN 12MP 1080P HD Game & Trail Hunting Camera No Glow Infrared Scouting Camera Night Vision up to 75 ft with 36pcs 940nm IR LEDs and Waterproof IP66 I purchased the TEC.BEAN 12MP 1080P HD Game & Trail Hunting Camera from Amazon for my Father to use in the lead up to fall turkey and dear seasons. However, we needed to test it out and know how it works prior to it being used in season. I had some concerns based on previous reviews about the ease of use of the user’s guide. A couple of reviewers had mentioned that the guide was mostly in Chinese and that the English portion was difficult to use and read, at best. This was a real concern for me because while I am IT Professional, Dad is not! I am pleased to say that the guide was easy enough to follow that I could get it up and running with no problem. Before we get to deep into the Camera itself I’d like to mention the case that is included with the camera. It is a very nice and well-designed hard case that will fit right in with your other hunting supplies. The camera itself feels very sturdy and well. The setup process was very easy. Put in the batteries, power it on and follow the onscreen menus. The process was easy to follow and fairly intuitive. Once the initial setup was complete it was easy to position. A couple of call outs: 1) The unit has some heft to it, some ensure you are attaching it to something that will support its weight, and 2) If you find that the lag is causing some shots to be lost point it a little further down the trail. That way the camera activates sooner. Over all I found the TEC.BEAN trail camera to be a quality product that is well made. I look forward to updating this review later after it has been used in the woods for the fall and winter hunting seasons. I Would definitely recommend it!

review_title: Great game cam with lots of options!!
review_text: this game cam has a lot of great features and a good software with many adjustments. i have been using the TEC.BEAN 12MP camera for about a month now and have not had a single issue. the photos are nice and crisp in low light and appear brighter than the naked eye, and the B/W night shots have a nice contrast that any animal can be identified easily. i really like the rugged enclosure and perfectly seals out the elements, it also has many options for mounting including two different tripod mounts. and for me the 12v power input is a huge plus so that batteries are not needed when close to a power source. about the only negative thing i could find is that i wish the test screen would stay on a little longer for setting it up, it seems to time out in less than a minute and it's tough to attach it to a tree and adjust it in that short amount of time. when it times out it goes into a sleep mode then takes a couple seconds to turn the screen back on... but honestly that is very petty and i'm stretching to find a negative point.

review_title: Brilliant design and practically useful in the wild
review_text: Brilliant design and practically useful in the wild, it surely can do more than any regular camera can’t do in woods, trails or even your backyard. I bought this for my father who is retired and likes hiking, birding and everything embracing nature. I believe this little gadget would make him happy and yes it does. It’s not so hard to learn how to set up, so took him only a little while. He is now using it to check what animals are ravaging his backyard; and he plans to bring it for a camping trip soon, it’s a good product !

review_title: An average camera that misses night events
review_text: I had high hopes for this camera after reading all of the reviews here, but unfortunately it performs worse than cheaper cameras when you consider actually capturing passing game. I have yet to capture anything in night mode while my other two trail cameras (different brands) do this just find in the same area. I've tried switch this camera to those locations as well, and it still does not trigger and capture the same game the other cameras do. Also, the HD video does not look like HD 1080 video. The photos it captures are just fine, but video looks like some like a regular SD when compared to other devices.

review_title: I kept wondering why this camera have so much reviews and made me doubt it but no I'm a believer now!
review_text: Love it! Everything is easy to setup, very straight forward, love the HYBRID mode! One of the most customizeable settings out there on the market. At first when looking for a new camera, I kept wondering why this camera have so much reviews and made me doubt it but no I'm a believer now! See the video attached in the review, I ran 720p instead of 1080p. SD format does work in those SD card readers for Androids, have not gotten an iPhone to work, may just be iOS doesn't like it's format or unable to decode it, would suggest bringing along a digital camera if you want to see the image right there and then if you have an iOS.

review_title: Great trail camera at great price
review_text: I’ve used trail camera for many years, mostly Bushnell. They used to give 3 years warranty but not any more! So after my last Bushnell camera is dead, I decided to give this new brand a try. It looks very solid built from outside, and the cover is tightly sealed for water proof purposes. I put in a 64GB SD card, that should be enough photos for the whole hunting season. And the manual claims the battery should be able to last for 6 months! The menu is really intuitive for me to navigate through all the settings. The test photos are much better than my previous trail camera. Let’s see how many game animals it can capture in my backyard!

review_title: Originally dissatisfied, but Nova Tech warrantied their product in great fashion.
review_text: Update: This is my second attempt to update my review, and I no longer remember exact dates. However, the seller contacted me immediately after my original review and expedited me a replacement for my defective camera. I don't think you can ask for more in the way of customer service, so I have revised my original one star review to five stars. I will update again after I have had some time to put the replacement into service. Original Review: I strongly urge you not to purchase this product. I ordered this camera 54 days ago, so my "return window" has closed. Although picture quality was decent, I was not overly impressed with the performance of this camera; it appeared to not capture all activity. I recently walked in front of the camera for about 3 minutes, but only had two photos of myself. One was at approximately 2 1/2 minutes into my movement and the second as I knelt in front of the camera. Today, I opened the camera to find that the small screen will power on but only display solid white (see attached photo). There is no contact information for the manufacturer in the documentation that came with the camera. You can see in my photos that the warranty card is not helpful. At the very least, I hope Amazon will either require more from the manufacturer or no longer offer their product.

review_title: Great product! Would definitely recommend to the average hunter
review_text: This is a high end hunting camera. I haven't seen many that work as well as this. I have strapped it to the tree and it flawlessly takes pictures of the deer that walk past. It will even send me the time stamp and GPS location. The night vision works really well and can brightly see all the animals it takes pictures of. Great product! Would definitely recommend to the average hunter.

This is my first trail camera and it’s worked just fine for me. Great photo quality and videos. The screen display works well. Just wish it stayed on a bit longer so you didn’t have to turn it off and back on again. Only negatives I would say is that the manual was a bit difficult to understand. But not terrible. Looks like Applenproducts can’t read the pictures it takes. So if you have an iPhone you’ll want something else to check out your pictures with in the field. But honestly I like this camera a whole lot.

review_title: UPDATED-Great pictures and videos but issues with viewer
review_text: UPDATED 12/23/2016- customer service reached out to me once they saw my review and did everything they could to make it right. They were helpful and also relayed the issue back to he manufacturer who said this was a known issue. The seller was wonderful to deal with. Original Review: I purchased this item to track the game in the area I hunt. I was pleased with the picture quality and videos that the camera recorded. The main issue that I have is when the temperature dropped below 35F/40F degrees the controls on the camera to use the view screen no longer worked. I needed to remove the SD card and play it through another device. I'm not sure if this was a one off issue or it's consistent for other users with this product. I've already purchased another camera with the same functionality.

My first Game camera, really intuitive controls easy to test and set for both video and pictures. Picture quality day or night at 12mp is great. I cant believe the amount of data I've gotten so far...times...temps....barometric pressure....feeding duration etc. I just love it and realize how important all this info. is in the Harvesting process. Was fine in rain also.

Great for monitoring deer activities, I bought it mainly for hunting. But other than that, there is two big groundhog in my backyard I am try to trap them and get ride of them, this camera took some pictures of the groundhog. I wish this has wifi build in and remind me there is activity on my cell phone. But overall, I like the pictures it captured.

review_title: Works OK, but not 100% dependable UPDATE: Total Junk.
review_text: I have used this camera now for a few months. At times, it does not work, then it does. I have had the competitors brands mostly. What is really confusing is that one minute, this will get the shots good, then seconds later, it goes dead for a period, then back on again. UPDATE: 2-18-18 Camera used inside only, focusing on driveway. NEVER was used outside. It has stopped working. Do not waste your money on this. This was a total waste of money. The little bit that it has worked does not justify the cost of it.

Easy to use, though I don't find the mini screen helpful given my poor eyesight. Night pix are generally over-exposed if there's more than, for example, one deer, within the 5-10' range. I wouldn't buy another one because the battery holder is forever falling out (making the camera stop working): when I open/close the case, when the wind blows enough to move the tree, when my puppy 'kisses' it to show me where it is, etc. It has a nice looking carrying box, but I've never used it.

review_title: Good price for a good camera
review_text: I hate when people write a review 5 minutes after taking it out of the box so I wanted to test it out first. We bought this to use as a security camera in the garage. Luckily, I've only seen pictures of me turning the camera on and off but it seems to do that very well! Plus the picture taking is totally undetectable. I especially like the feature of having a screen on the camera so you can preview where the camera is pointing. It also lets you view and delete photos from that screen so you don't have to bring the SD card back to a computer and forget to put it back in the camera, like other brands. 10/10 would buy again. The reason for 4 stars is because the instructions could be written better. Full and complete sentences, for one, but also an explanation for some of the features would be nice.

review_title: ... first trail camera for the family an we've really enjoyed it. Got at the tail end of our ...
review_text: Our first trail camera for the family an we've really enjoyed it. Got at the tail end of our deer season, the men have liked checking on the deer in our area. Not all are hunted so the kids and other family have really enjoyed seeing what wildlife come to the area, especially at night. We have obviously some cats and other animals popping in and around in my in law's country home! Pictures are good enough to tell what is going on and we like this little peek into the outside world.

What a great device. We are using this as a camera to watch our chicken and Duck house. There have been some missing chickens lately. Before getting this camera it was just a guessing game as to what was happening. We have it set up and have been watching over the coop. The night vision it great. It is very durable. If you take the time sit and read the information it is pretty straight forward on how to set it up and the use of all the features. This was a great purchase for me.

Well I had bought several hunting cameras around $60 before.They worked fine but did not last long. This time I decided to try out a higher-tier camera which is this TEC BEAN cam. review_title: Works best indoors, in daylight, with external power. Otherwise, junk.

If you read the copy on the product page, please explain to me how the sample photos of deer represent any of the "reptiles, cold-blooded or amphibian" that the camera is best for. Please! I bought this to capture images of whatever creature is occasionally getting into things in my back yard. My whole yard is within the range of the camera, so I thought it would be great to use the motion detector mode to capture anything that moved as night. Unfortunately, I live in Florida and the camera doesn't even notice me walking toward the camera so there's no possible chance that it is going to see something smaller (and it has utterly failed to do so). Perhaps it was the heat, but the batteries didn't last a whole week when it was in motion detect mode, even though not even ONE image was captured. I expected more (but I may have missed where the manual said the batteries wouldn't last too long.) On the plus side, when I used a different mode to capture some pictures and video after dark, I was pleased with the quality. It certainly wasn't HDTV clarity, but it was well within my expectations for inexpensive IR photography. The IR video frame rate showed a bug flying by the camera rather smoothly, which I considered a good sign. (smile) My biggest wish would be for a weather-safe way to power the unit from an external source as I'm not confident that the existing adapter and connection would withstand some of our rainstorms.

It has been months and the eight AA batteries are still good, but it has not been used continuously all that time. It works well indoors as a motion detector camera also. review_title: Find out The Pros & Cons Below!
review_text: ABOUT THIS CAMERA: This is a black flash trail camera, otherwise known as a No-Glow camera. BACKGROUND, ABOUT ME, AND MY HISTORY WITH TRAIL CAMERAS: I have several other trail camera brands including Stealth Cam, Moultrie, Covert, Primos, Browning, and TEC.BEAN. Honestly, the day time pictures with all of these brands are adequate for hunting and scouting purposes. What separates a camera in my eyes is trigger time, quality night pictures, recovery time, battery life, strap connecting to the tree, ease of setup, pictures of an object in motion, and durability. I’ve been using trail cams since about 2009. I have included a video and some pictures. WHAT I LIKE: + LCD Screen allows users to see where camera is pointed and you can review pictures/videos on it – unusual to see that in this price range + Easy to follow and program menu + Respectable Trigger time of about 0.8 seconds from my testing + Day pictures are good + Video with audio (5 to 90 second video clips) + Good detection range of about 70' + No glow (i.e. no visible flash) + Pictures/Videos are well illuminated + Photo bursts from 1 to 9 pictures at a time + Security password (optional) + Video file size is small (this means you can take more videos without requiring you to swap SD cards). For reference a 5 second video is 7-10 MB. + It takes 8 AA batteries, so batteries don’t need to be swapped as often as some cameras + It comes with a great case (not a security box but a carrying case) WHAT I DON'T LIKE - Slow video trigger speed of about 1.6 seconds compared to other trail cameras - Slow recovery time of 5-6 seconds (recovery time is the minimum period of time before the next picture or video can be taken) - Night videos are grainy (night pictures are a little grainy at 40' but not as bad) - This camera has a strap with a plastic buckle. I prefer a metal clip which is more convenient when removing and positioning - Whiteout pictures at close range CONCLUSION: In summary, I like this camera for it's pictures. The videos are on the slow side. The trade-off with this camera being a no-glow camera is that pictures are a bit more grainy (typical of many no-glow cameras though some are getting better). I really like the LCD screen. It’s so helpful for knowing where to position the camera. This camera is a respectable camera in this price point, though the Browning cameras for a tad more are really nice. If I can answer any questions, please feel free to leave them below.

You can set up the camera are various time intervals and recording lengths. Motion sensing photo taking will make the battery last long. What I didn't like was the use of 8 AA batteries which is a lot. If you're using this quite often, you'll be replacing batteries quite often as well. I'd like to see built in rechargable or built in replaceable rechargeable batteries (like old school Nokia batteries). It comes with an excellent carry case, a strap (tie around a tree?), an AV cable, and a miniUSB cable. I couldn't get the USB cable working (assuming you can connect to your computer) as the device would get into a booting loop. So in order for me to retrieve the files I had to remove the SD card and so it manually. You also have the option to throw in a WiFi card which you can setup under the menu settings. The user interface is well laid out and easy to navigate. You have the option to change resolution settings, timer settings, PIR settings, and so on. The construction of this camera is good but not great. It appears that the door is seal with rubber gaskets but the battery compartment is not. So under heavy rain or heavy humidity I highly doubt this camera will keep from the elements.

review_title: Great trail camera with many features as well as takes good pictures!
review_text: This is a great trail camera for those who hunt or for those who are trying to track pesky animals that may be getting into their yard or their gardens! I hunt on occasion and it is nice and very useful to have at least one or even a couple of these trail cams set up in the hunting property. Doing so allow you to keep track of what size deer to expect, whether the anticipated hunting area is a good spot or not, and even see what time is prime that the anticipated animals tend to make their appearance. All of this is crucial when hunting and can definitely save one a lot of time and hassle. I have used a number of other trail cams in the past and have had fair luck with them and some what pleased with their functionality. I had one stolen a fair bit of time ago and never got around to replacing it and I saw this one and it seemed to be feature full so I went ahead and ordered it. As soon as I got it in the mail, I opened it up to check it out. It is definitely a tough looking and feeling trail camera, which is good because it has to hold up to different weather and the potential animal knocking it or hitting it. This camera is capable of shooting 12MP, 8MP, 5MP, as well as 2MP pictures depending on your preferences. It can also shoot video at 1080P at 15 fps as well as 720P at 30 fps which will get you some good footage (you are limited to up to 90 seconds of video), though I have always preferred pictures since it gives me what I need information wise and saves some space on the sd card. When the front cover is opened up, you will see the 2 inch lcd screen which will allow you to see what the camera can currently see while setting up the camera, you can view any pictures and videos that were previously taken and saved to the card, and you use it to set up the various settings for use. Settings wise, you can set up a time lapse, multi shot mode, zoom, timer, audio recording, etc. There are loads of features to take advantage of. This camera has a tv out so you can hook it up to a tv or monitor to watch the recorded video or pictures. The strap to mount it to a tree has a plastic clip which feels sturdy, but feel a metal clip would be better for the outdoors conditions. There is a slot on the side to place a lock so that someone can not open and tamper with the camera. The camera takes great pictures and the videos are okay, but like mentioned before, I am not too concerned with videos. Pictures are very good, both those taken during the day as well as those at night. It is fairly sensitive and reacts quickly to movement and the time lapse setting works well as well. I am very pleased with the outcome of this trail camera and look forward to putting it to real use here soon! I would recommend it to anyone. Though the price may be a bit higher than others on the market, this one does have much better functionality than most others do also. I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest review.

I was loaned this Trail & Surveillance Camera to do an independent, honest review. First off, it comes with a few accessories to make it easy to view your HD 1080p videos, with sound, and 12MP photos on your television set, directly from the camera, instead of on the 2" built in viewing screen. Also a USB cable to ease downloading them to a computer is included. It requires an SD Card to use, up to 32GB, which along with the needed 8 AA alkaline batteries are not included. I suggest you use a fast C10 class SD card as I believe the trigger speed is fastest with a speedy card. Battery life lasts through hundreds of videos or thousands of photos. All are crystal clear, full color in daylight and b/w in total darkness. It uses 36 super bright "Black" Infra Red LEDs to light up the night, and your photo/video without spooking the critters. Specs claim up to 75' of lighting which seems accurate. A strap is included for attaching the camera to a tree or pole. There are two built in tripod mount nuts if you wish to use a tripod. There also are slots to use a security cable (not included) , as well as a password setting option to make the camera useless to a thief. The 30 page user's manual is written in decent enough english and walks you through the many functions and settings available. I could list the surprisingly many capabilities and features of this Trail cam but the listing has them clearly stated. All in all, this is a feature rich camera and for the price it is a fabulous choice, plus it comes with a one year warranty should something go wrong. This one had zero issues. It is capable of using the new Wifi SD cards which could be convenient but I did not test that capability. Photo mode can be set to take up to 9 photos per trigger event, and you can set video mode up to 90 seconds in duration. There is a "hybrid" mode which will trigger a photo and then immediately take a video. Nice feature. The camera is enclosed in a tight fitting water resistant case. I am pleased with the capabilities and performance of this camera as I believe you also will be. Thanks for the opportunity to field test this cam. I hope this review is helpful to anyone considering a purchase.

One thing that someone should be careful about is making certain that any direct sun is blocked by a tree or something. I saw a lot of lens flare one some reviewer's photos but my test pictures were sharp and flare-free. Once I found my spot for the camera I did have a little bit of trouble mounting it but I think that it was mostly my fault. After it was set up I tested it by walking in front of it. I even sent my dog to nose around the area by pacing some of his treats on the ground. The test photos and video were exactly the quality that I was hoping for. I especially liked the built-in 2" viewing screen. I was very easy to check out the quality of the photos without having to remove the card and them inserting into a reading device like my tablet. I am still waiting to grab a shot of a big buck or even the bobcats that live near to where I mounted it, but so far they have not be very obliging. I will post those photos when I get them.

review_title: Tickled to death to be provided a product sample and getting turned onto a great little find!!!!!
review_text: I was given the opportunity to have a Product Sample for a product review. Being a trail cam buff I jumped at the opportunity, I keep cams in the woods from spring till winter to monitor game. I own about 15 cameras of several different varieties. I was like a kid at Christmas when I unboxed the Tec Bean camera, from the sharp look of the camo to the well built sturdy construction, ergonomics and compact size of the unit. As I read over the owners manual I was even more excited to get batteries in the unit to check out the numerous feature. I really loved the 2"viewing screen for checking your photos and making sure your cam is spot on the exact location you are wanting to photograph. I told my fiancé if this cam performs has as good as it looks that I was ordering more.....Well it exceeded my expectations with photos, ease of use and operation, with features comparable to $300+ cameras...Day and night video with sound, 1 to 9 shot picture bursts with adjustable digital settings, no more switches that limit your settings. This camera can adjust from seconds to minutes/seconds in photo and video mode with photography type adjustments...2,3 and 4x magnification on the lens and picture quality from 2 to 12 megapixels with the push of a couple buttons. I tested the cam past its suggested range and was overzealous in maximizing my adjustments, because compared to the 2 other brands of cameras I had hooked to the same tree I had to tone down my settings until I went beyond 80 ft with the Tec Bean. It even captured more photos that the other cams missed. I also use a computer program called Hunt and Map which you can plot way points for sign....Well this Cam logs date, time, moon phase, temp and also stamps longitude and latitude and all this in 7 different languages. In 3 weeks of use, moving distance, changing adjustments and comparing photos to 2 other cams I have yet to find its limitations. I even went as far as to not use the high dollar recommended batteries, but went with an off brand battery and after over 1000 photos still have 98% battery life. If you want an unbiased opinion, get as many as these cams as possible, before one of the Big Major Outdoor Companies contracts it, brands it and doubles the price....It is worth every penny and more !!!!!!!

review_title: Good Features, Easy to Use but Camera had Minor Issues
review_text: I rely on game cameras to know what's on my acreage and in the woods around my property. I decided to give the TEC.BEAN camera with its higher resolution, digital zoom and long range a try. The camera takes a load of AA batteries. 8! Even so, it has a smaller footprint than other cameras I've used. It's relatively small and easy to conceal. I tested the camera over several weeks in multiple conditions. Here's what I found. The Good: - Camera is super easy to set up. The prompts in the small LCD screen are clear enough you don't really need to read the instructions - Image quality: good to very good. Crisp color during the day, Sharp black and white at night - Video: sharp clear 1080P video. You can see whatever is moving in the frame, even if it's small - Audio: very few cameras capture audio at all - LCD - very convenient not to have to pull the card in order to see what's on the camera, making it good for spot checking. - Digital zoom. Rare and cool in a game camera. The Not so Good: - The rings for locking the camera are too small to accept a standard padlock. They need to be 10% bigger and the clips that close the case need to be closer to the top and bottom to accommodate the lock hasp. - Reliability. My camera seemed glitchy. The first time I put it in the field I left it for a week and when I came back it had eaten the batteries (all 8 of them) in much less than a week. There was a quite a bit of nighttime video of nothing (see complaint 2 below). Manufacturer tells me that shooting a lot of nighttime video eats the battery but this seemed excessive. - Video was sometimes corrupted. While I got some good video, other's were corrupted and would jump back and forth between time indices failing to correctly display the video. - Too sensitive. While most cameras aren't sensitive enough this one seems to be too sensitive. Small things like grasses moving in the breeze triggered the sensor. - LCD location. The one thing the LCD isn't good for is trying to figure out what's in your view finder while using it. There's basically no way to look at the LCD without obstructing the lens.. Overall I think this camera has potential. I really like the features and the ease of setup. I'm still not sure why it ate the batteries the first time or why I got glitchy video. I'd give the camera more stars if it weren't for these issues. I've reached out to the manufacturer to see about my problems. If they replace the camera and a second test finds that my unit was the issue I'll update the review to reflect it.

review_title: I do not like it at all for two reasons
review_text: I do not like it at all for two reasons. First, IR light source cannot be attenuated, so for small (say, cat-size) animals this camera is semi-useful: at 5 m or closer, the light spot is too bright. But if want to observe elephants, bears and elks at your backyard, at 10 m or so, it is just fine. Most importantly, the camera has a DC 12V input, which is in principle a good idea, since the AA batteries deplete too fast. The problem is that it was not designed by an Einstein: to connect an external DC source to this input, FIRST you have to switch the camera on and close the shell. So you have no way to check whether the camera works, since the access to switches and indicator lights is already closed. Not to mention that date, time, etc., settings are lost. The description says "a battery life up to 8 months" - no way! Probably, if the camera is off. I used it for four weekends, three nights each weekend, and brand new AA batteries got depleted to 33%. Last night I used a 12V external DC source. Even at about 12 m the IR illumination was too bright, and thus the image quality was bad. But the sensor almost did not work: raccoons, opossums and ringtails appeared many times (I feed them with bananas), however only once the camera was triggered for a ringtail at about 3 m.
