review_title: Large drone, fun to fly, cool to film with
review_text: For the price this is a pretty good drone. It does have a couple minor issues, but it's still a great fullsize drone for the money. This thing is big, it is roughly 20 inches by 20 inches in size. One of the biggest drones I have. It's not overly intimidating tho, due to its size. Still flies well even for its size. The controller is also a good size and fits well in your hands. Most Syma drones are all very similar with their flying and controllers. This is my 4th Syma drone. They are all very visually similar and all fly very similar. My small X21 looks and flies pretty much identical to this X8SW. That's pretty good if you're considering jumping up to a larger sized drone. The drone itself comes pretty much complete. To have to attach the propellers, landing gear and camera. You can also attach the prop guards if you so wish. They all attach very easily and remove easily. The first propeller was a little tricky to get on, but after the first one the other 3 were simple once you figure out what way they spin to attach. It comes with 4 yellow and 4 black propellers. You can use all 4 yellow, all 4 black or mix and match the yellow and black. They are labeled A or B and the drone is labeled so you can't really mix them up unless you're not paying attention. The legs just slide in and lock along with the prop guards. The camera slides in underneath and then has a headphone type jack to plug it in and power it. It's all very simple and straight forward to assemble. The drone itself is easy to fly. It's pretty straightforward and easy to control. It has 2 speeds with a quick push down of the right stick. You'll hear a single beep for slow and two beeps for fast. It has decent speed in slow for beginners and decent speed in high for experienced flyers. It's not super fast racing drone speed, but it's ok to get it to move around. It has a good range to it. I had it up quite high and still was able to control it and see video via the factory camera. I would say I was easily up over 200ft high and still had no issues controlling it. There is a couple things about this drone to note. The camera isn't spectacular. The video and photos aren't complete garbage, but they weren't as good as they could be. Syma needs to upgrade the camera. They state it's a HD camera. If it is, it's on the low end of HD cameras. I replaced the factory camera with an aftermarket action camera and mount. I purchased the mount from Amazon. One thing to note, the action camera mount hangs low, so be careful of hard landings. Another thing, the legs sometimes will be in the video or photos. Something you'll have to live with. Another thing is wind, this drone is somewhat on the light side. So any sort breeze will cause this to fly erratically. It's not great in any breezy or windy conditions. The drone does have trimming, but it could be better. That was to be expected tho for the price. This is by no means near what a DJI can handle due to their weight difference and control ability. That's just a given. For what it can do versus the price, it's pretty good to get into the large drone game for beginners. It's still very, very fun. Another thing to note is flips, make sure it is high enough to flip due to the quick drops it will do when coming out of the flip. The drone needs to be at least 30-40ft high. It does drop quite a bit coming out of flips. Kinda caught me off guard. Thankfully I was up pretty high when I attempted them. Overall tho it's a really fun and nice sized drone. It flies really well and is easily controllable. The camera is ok, but could be better, but it works well with or without the Syma FPV app. If you want to get into larger drones but can't see shelling out a large amount, this one is great to begin with. I've enjoyed it so far. Wifi connected easily with my iPhone. Also, pick up a couple extra batteries, you'll only get one with this and it only lasts about 10 mins. I picked up the 3 pack listed on here and now have 4 batteries so I can just swap and go. They are definitely worth it.

He gets a kick out of how close he can get it to me without it touching me, and then zooms off. Then he likes to show me all the embarrassing closeups he’s gotten of me. It’s hilarious. We have to charge it every night because my husband exhausts the battery every single day driving it so much. He told me he's surprised at how long the battery lasts too. He just keeps driving and driving and it takes forever to drain. What I love most about it though is how bright the lights are at night. We don’t have many lights in our neighborhood, so it’s always fun to see the neighbors reaction to these strange hovering lights above their houses. The picture quality is pretty good too. Better than I was expecting. But the best part of buying this drone for my husband was that he finally had to admit that I’m the best wife ever, because now he has the coolest toy at the shop and all the other guys are jealous! Listening to my husband talk about this drone is like listening to my son talk about Minecraft. I don’t understand half of what they’re saying. I just nod in agreeance and try to act shocked. It’s really cute though to see my husband acting like a big kid about his “man toy.” I can’t speak on behalf of the functionality of this drone because I don't know all the technical jargon, but I can tell you that my husband has never been more excited about a remote control vehicle than I've seen him act about this one. He says he loves it, it's the most fun RC experience he's ever had, and he's constantly thanking me for it. For the quality and the price, I can guarantee that there’s no better deal out there. review_title: This is a nice drone for beginners like me
review_text: This is a nice drone for beginners like me. It's larger than the description claims -- it's a full two feet wide, if you measure across the body blade-tip to blade-tip. BTW, getting those blades on was a pain, as I've never done it before. I don't look forward to having to replace one. The controls are quite sensitive, and controlling the drone will require a few hours of practice if you're new to this hobby. It's best used when there's little or no wind. I quickly discovered that a flat, open field was preferable to my hedge- and tree-filled yard. (This is how I discovered that this drone works well as a leaf shredder.) It's easy to lose control given the sensitive controls, because your impulse when there's trouble is to slam the joystick around. A gentle touch is required! Luckily, there's an auto-land button on the controller, which saved my bacon -- and the drone -- several times. I'm still getting the hang of it. I experimented with the camera. No need for a 32-gig card unless you plan on filming long events (and changing the battery pack every 10 or so minutes). The 720 HD camera takes decent-quality photos and video. Have not yet tried the streaming video feature. Speaking of battery life, I would highly recommend getting the three-pack of replacement batteries you'll see suggested. Swapping in a fresh one is a snap. (You'll know when it runs down; the four lights will begin to blink, and eventually the drone will land itself.) Haven't yet tried the app on my smartphone, but FPV sounds interesting. I wonder whether it will enhance the experience, or make it more difficult for this beginner? BTW, there is an error in the user manual on page 10: the illustration says "Long press (hold for 3 seconds) RIGHT stick to enter headless mode", while the paragraph below it tells you to "Press down and hold LEFT stick for 3 seconds to enter headless mode." I haven't tried it yet -- which is it? Bottom line: Nice drone -- I recommend it!

review_title: OMG...Compares admirably well to those $1200 massage chairs!
review_text: OK, I love the kneading and pressing action that those massage chairs have...but I don't have the room (or the $$$) to get one. So I saw the favorable review and decided to order this (long story short, I liked it so much, I ordered a second one as well). Honestly speaking, I can't say how long this thing will hold up, but I've been using it daily for about 20 minutes for the past two weeks, and it seems to be going strong. I use it on my neck, upper back, lower back and even my calves (hence the reason I got a second one). I don't press too hard against it (I don't want to burn out the motor or put too much of a strain on it), but I lean on it enough that I can really feel the kneading action on my muscles. Also, the rotating spheres can be set on regular or heat, and they don't get too hot, just slightly warm (very nice touch). And about every 45 seconds, the rotation reverses. Honestly, I love this thing and cannot believe it's so inexpensive...I will come back and let you know how it's holding up in a few weeks. Pros: -Inexpensive -Heat or no heat -Simple on and off button -Auto reverses -Seems to be able to hold up under the pressure of my weight without straining the motor (motor and gears seem surprisingly strong) Cons: -Since it's portable, it takes a bit of re-positioning to put it in the right spot and not have it slip (but that's really my fault for moving). -Connects to a cable that you plug in, so if you move too much, you may disconnect it (again, my fault for being so fidgety)

I'm on day 2 of using this massager. Press the on/off button once to turn on for regular mode, press twice for the heat mode (lights up red) and press and hold for about 3 seconds to shutoff. The massager i received came intact- no rips or tears in the fabric, all of the functions are currently working as advertised *except* this massager does NOT have a 15 minute auto shutoff function as stated. The instructions recommend not using for more than 30 minutes, I assume to lower the chance to overheat? The massaging 'arms' are a hard plastic that move in a circular motion and switch directions after about every minute. This item comes with a U.S. wall plug and another cord to plug into a cigarette lighter port in the car. I haven't used it in the car yet so I can't say for sure that the cord extends long enough for this and if it's even comfortable to use while in a vehicle. There is a velcro strap on the back of the massager to attach to the head rest of the seat. If the massaging 'arms' feel too hard for you, i would recommend putting extra cushion over the massager, maybe a towel or a blanket. I notice if i put too much pressure on the massager, it noticeably struggles in that the 'arms' move a little slower and the mechanisms sound like they are working harder to move. I haven't had any issues with my long hair getting thru the mesh fabric and getting tangled in the 'arms' yet as someone else stated was an issue, but i will keep an eye on that as it may be possible after the mesh fabric wears down due to normal wear. I haven't had any overheating issues even after using for more than 30 minutes. The heating element seems to take a little bit to heat up and doesn't get very hot. It's not very noticeable to me. I've read a lot of reviews saying this model has a short life. I will update later as to how it's held up (or not).

review_title: At The Price I'm Pretty Satisfied With It
review_text: I'm pretty pleased with this decibel meter. You know, for the price I think it's okay, definitely better than using an application and relying on my iPhone's minuscule speaker to read noise levels I thought. If I was buying a decibel meter for something really super important or scientific I would definitely spend the extra money and buy one of the more robust and feature-filled models though. But, for me just checking how loud the annoying highway is next to my house or how loud my many neighbor's annoying, barking dogs are, well, this fits the bill for my uses. Plus, it's fun to just test everything around you I found. And I believe you'll look way more important and sophisticated with an actual device like this as opposed to just pointing the bottom of your phone at noises, hehe. And while I haven't read the instruction manual thoroughly yet, I was able to get this meter up and running in no time. I'm sure there are still more things I can do to calibrate it precisely like it mentions in the manual though. And even though I feel really comfortable with tech stuff and electronics I still think if you're not that type of person that this shouldn't be too hard to get up and running. As for how long the battery lasts in it I cannot really say. I haven't used it long enough yet to be able to comment on that really. I did switch out the generic battery that came with it though for an Energizer battery. But I don't believe a device like this would have a huge drain on the battery when using it, then again probably best not to quote me on that :P. In the end, I'm happy everything worked and functioned really well for uses and like I expected it would. So, if you don't need one of these meters for anything super important like scientific tests, I'd recommend it for sure. I would also assume it would still work accurately enough as proof of overly loud sound levels if you need if for that reason too, like to show the police or other officials. I hope this was helpful, thanks.

review_title: Easy to Use Accurate Sound Level Meter
review_text: As usual with my Amazon Prime Membership this sound level meter arrived in two days. The meter is powered by a single 9 volt battery, which I was pleasantly surprised to find was included and can be accessed on the back of the unit under a sliding door. The body of the meter is made of plastic, which tapers to the condenser microphone; a metal cylinder covered by a sponge ball. The unit’s overall measurements are approximately 6-1/4” long, 2” wide and 1-1/4” deep, fitting comfortably in the hand. The unit has three toggle control buttons: a single power button that toggles the unit on and off, a hold button to lock and unlock the current sound level reading and a maximum/minimum toggle button that will indicate the highest and lowest sound level readings after the unit is activated. Powering off the unit clears previous readings. On the rear of the unit is a standard camera ¼” x 20 threaded socket for attaching the unit to a tripod. I would like to point out that this “A” weighted sound meter was designed to measure only sound intensity and not frequency, which is a different scale referred to as “C” weighted. To better understand what the readings of this meter actually mean one needs to understand that manufacturers have developed sound level meters with distinctly different response curves naming them “A”, “B”, “C,” “D”, and “Z” weighting, but the “A” & “C” are the most used scales. Most of us are aware that animals have much better hearing than humans. This increased sensitivity is true not only for the intensity of a sound, as a cat can hear sounds that are much quieter than humans can hear, but also for the frequency of a sound as a dog can hear a high-pitched whistle beyond the frequency range that can be heard by humans. So hearing sensitivity must be measured not only in intensity, but also in terms of frequency. This meter is an “A” weighted meter and follows the frequency sensitivity of the human ear at low levels. This is the most commonly used weighting scale, as it also predicts quite well the damage risk of the ear from a noisy environment. Sound level meters set to the A-weighting scale will filter out much of the low-frequency noise they measure, similar to the response of the human ear. Noise measurements made with the A-weighting scale are designated dBA. This would be the meter to use to test the sound level of a noisy environment like an industrial shop, the quietness of the cabin of a car on a test ride or your kid’s room. Bear in mind the OSHA maximum sound limit exposure is 90 dBA for 8 hours. At 115 dBA the exposure is 30 seconds. You might be surprised at the dBA level of restaurants, sporting events and concerts not to mention earbuds. High dBA’s can and do permanently damage hearing. “C” weighted follows the frequency sensitivity of the human ear at very high noise levels. The C-weighting scale is quite flat, and therefore includes much more of the low-frequency range of sounds than the A and B scales. “B” weighting follows the frequency sensitivity of the human ear at moderate levels, used in the past for predicting performance of loudspeakers and stereos, but not industrial noise. This scale is seldom used. Powering up this unit revealed a large, easy to read, non-lighted digital display that immediately begins to indicate the current sound level. I would point out the Amazon description indicates a backlight display; this unit does not have a back lighted display, so it cannot be read in total darkness. Manufacturer’s included instruction sheet specifications indicate the measuring level range to be 40 to 130 dB, but I obtained readings in the 30dB range. The Amazon description indicates 30-130 dBA range, so this appears to be correct. The manufacturer’s specifications also indicate this is an “A” weighted only sound level meter and my tested measurements indicate this to be correct. I compared the readings on this meter to two other sound meters set to the “A” scale and I am satisfied as to this meter’s accuracy and its fit for purpose. It is an accurate, compact, very easy to use, portable sound level meter and I am completely happy with my purchase. I do reserve the right to alter my review at a later date if conditions warrant.

review_title: Very comfortable holster, Holds and secures gun, Perfect for small caliber pistols.
review_text: I used this holder everyday for a month now, and it is as comfortable on day 1 to day 30. The stitching and materials seem well made. I have not washed it yet, but it should not have any problems. I expect that it should last a few years. The holster is perfect for my SW Bodyguard (no laser) with the 6-round mag with finger extension. It does not print what so ever if you have the butt angle slightly rearward of the calf, and wear levi 505 or 550 jeans. The gun stayed secured, even when running, purposely shaking my leg, jumping-jacks, etc. The holster itself is VERY comfortable, and the upper retention strap helps keep the gun secured in place. The upper strap does sometimes fall, but usually very little and over the course of a whole day of walking/running/ doing errands. It takes 5 second to restrap (quietly) in the bathroom stall, and if you need to, 30 second to pull it back up through your pants fabric. To be clear, even if the top strap works it way down at the end of the day, my gun never felt unsecure or shifted position on my leg. I should note that there are micro perforations on the inside, but I have so far only worn this during the winter so I do not know how this would feel in the summer months with sweat. I gave 4 stars instead of 5 because the velcro backstrap is too secure, Maybe should have a snap buckle instead or have less hook/loop area, because on a few practice draws, the velcro prevented me from quick drawing the gun (I have to pull the velcro off first). I simply taped half the velcro suface over and now I have the perfect amount of retention, yet can rip/draw the gun straight out when needed....With a larger gun, the velcro might be not an issue, because the backstrap will have a longer area to reach around to the mating surface, and thus less hook/loop engagement. For cost of $13, I have zero regrets. Yes this is my first ankle holster, but I did give it to two of my cousins to try, and both said they liked it also. One of the two has an ankle holster by desantis, and he said he hates it, but would consider wearing this one.

My husband received this mini drone as a gift. This is a very nice mini drone for the price. The drone itself appears to be very well made and I like that it comes with some additional blades. The drone came fully assembled, all we had to do was charge the battery and put some batteries in the remote. We are relatively new to drones, however my husband was able to pick up how to fly it relatively quick. I think part of the reason he was able to pick it up quickly is due to the simplicity of the controller. It resembles a video game controller with two toggles and a couple of buttons. Since it is a small drone we are able to easily fly around the house which the kids enough. They get a kick out of watching my husband fly it towards them and then pull it back real fast. We have also had fun using the camera to spy on the kids when they are playing in the other room! This is a great starter drone for anyone who is new and wants to try one out!

If you are a beginner or new to drones then this is a good product for you start with. I got this device for that reason exactly. The drone itself is pretty easy to figure out. When you start flying it, it has a hover mode which is nice, unless you touch any of the controls, it just stays in the same spot in midair. As advertised it has control for all 6 axis. The lights on it help you figure out its orientation when it gets a too far for you to actually see it. It has a camera that can record videos or take snapshots. Unfortunately this all gets saved to a micro-SD that later would need to be downloaded to a second device manually, but really for this price I didn’t have any great expectations. Also comes with some spare blades, but so far I didn’t need to use them. So all in all, good device for beginners and works just as advertised, works very nicely and really for this price works much better than I would expect, so I am giving it 5 stars.

But I screwed it on after. It makes it safe for the propellers anyway, most are just clip one that fall off all the time, one thing I’d like to see for future progress is a better and bigger controller. The controller was great and fly perfect just fits a 5 year olds hands not a grown persons very well. All in all it’s a perfect kids drone and fast enough to call it an adults. I recommend this to anyone reading. By the way the hover mode was flawless I literally flew this with one hand in the video below if that says anything about air control.

review_title: Read the manual. Charge battery first.
review_text: I was very excited to buy a drone, it was my first. It came with a detailed instruction manual which I read. It said, fully charge the battery before first use. I thought that was silly so I put the battery in and the drone lit up like a Christmas tree, so of course it was good to fly! I took it outside and powered up the controller, pressed up on the throttle, and watched as see as it rose into the sky. Now, the reason they say to fully charge the battery, is because the battery only comes with about 10 seconds of fly time. The glorious ascent abruptly halted, and for a moment it seemed that time stood still as well, as the drone hovered in place. Alas, time resumed all too soon and my precious drone plummeted to earth. It did not survive this. So, moral of the story, charge your battery first!

I've had a lot of experience with quadcopters and drones and this is one of those that's perfect for beginners! Even for such a simple quadcopter it was really fun for me to fly! Let me start off by explaining why this is the perfect quadcopter for beginners. First off its size is great as it big enough to fly outdoors against the wind and small enough to fly indoors especially with the prop guards. The technology built into it is definitely for safety reasons as you have to enable the propellers before you take off, and it doesn't let you kill the propellers so you can't drop harshly out of the sky. It also has the prop guards so you don't wreck the blades when learning to fly and hitting things. Even if you break a prop they give you four extras. It also has auto hovering which means that it can hover in a spot using movement sensors to stay still while hovering. Now I've noticed this feature doesn't stay perfectly still while hovering as it;ll bounce up and down, but this a rare feature for smaller drones and it's very helpful for learning to fly and just flying in general. I also haven't been the easiest on this drone as I've had a lot of people who have never flown a quadcopter before try this and it has crashed a lot as you can probably tell by the pictures, but they learned surprisingly quick compared to other quadcopters. it still works great after taking so many hits though! The gyroscope is really nice as you don't need to trim it very much and it helps for when you want to flip it as it stays still. The charger on it is really nice as you remove the battery to charge it and it'll charge in about 45 minutes to fly for about 7 minutes of flight time which is pretty good. I also noticed that the package it came in had a lithium ion warning which indicates that the battery is actually lithium ion which I didn't expect as lithium ion lasts forever compared to other battery chemicals used. Now I did rate this four out of five for a couple of reasons. Since it doesn't have an immediate kill switch meaning you can't shut off the propellers immediately, it causes the props to scrape up if it runs into something, although this feature is nice for beginners, I personally didn't like it as it takes forever to shut off as you have to hold in the right bumper. It also has a lot of trouble binding with the remote for some reason and it may take a few tries to get connected. It also doesn't move the fastest even at high speeds mode, but I really didn't expect it to for the price and with its weight/size disadvantage. I haven't tried the camera yet as I don't have a micro SD card, but I'm sure it's nothing special at 720p resolution, although I have 720p cameras on quadcopters in the past and it's fun to watch from a first person perspective of the drone. Overall this product has a lot of advanced technology and is very durable, but it has some drawbacks and glitches. If you have never flown a quadcopter before, I would definitely recommend this drone to you!

review_text: (SAME REVIEW I POSTED ON THE HOME SECURITY SYSTEM FROM DIGOO BUT ANSWERS ALOT OF CONCERNS AND QUESTIONS) Fairly easy installation if you have some kind of common sense. the PIR has great range! the door sensors stick pretty well. All the sensors came synced with the system already, but I followed instructions anyways and made sure of it. The different settings are nice to have so you can set the PIR to not go off if you use the bathroom but if you leave the house you can set it to sound at any motion. Top left button arms as if youre in the house so the motion sensor wont go off, bottom left is if youre out and want to alert at any motion The app was a little tricky, you may have to create a new email if the email is over 25 characters long(both system and camera), it will register but wont let you log in with it.. wish it would tell you that but it doesnt. Can sync up to 5 phone numbers, so if youre on vacation add someone you trust to get alerts as well incase you dont have cell service. **Even though you set passwords for the unit... anyone who does break in can literally just hit the disarm button on unit and it stops, but it will still alert you thru the app so you will still be informed... if your extra worried, get the wifi speaker to pair with it and put it in your room so you make sure to hear it go off and not assume youll hear your phone. *****!!! I bought the DIgoo wifi camera with it, the camera itself is great! You can move and control it thru either app. Can take still photos or videos up to 3 min intervals, needs an SD card to record or sync to your computer (i didnt do computer, figured SD card was plenty) However i was a little misguided that you can link it to the unit. Somewhat un-true. You can view and control thru the unit app after installing the camera and the camera app seperately. However you can not arm the camera with the house unit itself.... kinda sucks i was hoping it all linked together, but if your alarm goes off and notifies you, then you can switch to your camera thru the house unit app and view it that way. Or arm both seperately, but thats not very convenient. ALL in ALL a great DIY home system compared to spending 40-60 a month on a commercial system. If you just want to use the app and check in every so often, the setup wasn't too bad. That said I couldn't get the "SmartSetup" or whatever to work: you select the wireless access point you want the camera to connect to on your phone, then the ap transmits this data from your phone to the camera via audio. I couldn't get this to work, so I moved on. My intended setup was to use this for logging to a Milestone NVR server. This required the use of the H.264 ONVIF/RSTP from the camera. Admittedly it took me quite a bit of messing around to get this working. To get the cam connected to your wifi: plug in LAN cable, find the IP addressed your DHCP assigns to the camera. Use this info connect to the camera via the app (for the 'device ID', if the app can't find your camera, you can use a PC application called "ONVIF Device Manager" which will show the device ID). Once there, go to the network config section, DON'T chose 'Wifi' right away! Instead choose the access point you want to connect to (must be 2.4Ghz) - it will prompt you for the password, and then of course once you save it looses connection. I had to power cycle the camera to get it to connect. Boot/wifi connect time was about a minute+, so be patient. A few tips: -the "address" that most cam apps ask for can vary in their format. Some must include user/pass, some need to include the ONVIF port (544, default), some the web port (5000), so the info here is really only applicable to Milestone. -if you don't want to use the included PC app, one I found very good was "AnyCam" - this found my camera right away and worked without issue. -in the case of Milestone, I had to use the IP address (only) and port 5000 (default 80) -the username to access these streams is 'admin'. The password is the password mentioned in the user manual. Again for Milestone I had to chose "ONVIF Compliant Camera" as the device. Even when the camera was detected, I still had to change the camera stream protocol to be RTP/UDP. Otherwise it would not display a preview. Once setup it seems to work well - I'll report back long term reliability. Below shows garage at about 7PM with setting sun through man door behind the camera.

review_title: Lacks critical feautres and is flakey
review_text: First off, the design of the camera is pretty cool. Great concept, that's why I ordered them. However the camera lacks critical features that make it worthless. First off, there is no HTTP server built into the camera. The standard operation of setting up an IP cam is to plug it into a wired connection, it DHCP's, you get the IP, and plug it into your browser. Then you can login and change all the setting including adding it to a WiFi network. In this case, with no HTTP server, it doesn't do anything. You NEED the app to set it up. Ok, fair enough I have a few other cameras like that. But one you do get it to setup there is no way to configure the network settings to have a static IP. Meaning this camera will potentially have a different random IP address every time the DHCP lease expires. The manufacturer's response to this is to set this up in your router. Ok... Yes possible based off of the mac but very impracticable for a real installation. Even then I tried to get it to work. It is supposed to be ONVIF compatible so with the user name and password setup at the DHCP address, doesn't work. With all the inherent flaws, it is not worth the time to get it figured out.

review_title: A Decent Stand Alone But Not For Expanding Your System
review_text: I was hoping for a reasonably priced interior camera to add to my camera network. I have a couple of exterior Hikvision cameras running through Blue Iris and wanted to add an interior camera. Saw a few reviews and forum posts that mentioned being able to run this through Blue Iris so I gave it a try. You can get this setup with Blue Iris but it's less than intuitive and there's no documentation from the manufacturer for doing it despite mentioning Blue Iris in the feature list on Amazon. Once connected it's a so-so camera. For the price, image quality and feature set are reasonable but if you're wanting to adjust frame rates, iframe rates, shutter speed, etc... this doesn't give you the option. Setting the camera up on wifi is a bit hit and miss but it works. I've had to do it three times while making other equipment changes on my home network, one time it connected on the first attempt, the other two times it took multiple attempts. I'm 15 feet from the router and running a wifi monitor on a tablet while installing from my phone. Ping time, up and down speeds were good for all connection attempts. If I were looking for a stand alone camera to monitor from my phone at a reasonable price, I think this would do. If I were looking to expand my ip camera network while trying to save money (this was me), I would be making a mistake and should seriously (really should have) consider spending a little more money for a known quality camera.

review_text: My house was robbed last year and the old security camera system was kinda useless because those cameras only recorded and didn't have motion detection and alarming function. Then I found this one that looks really promising and the price is affordable. So I decided to give it a try though I was skeptical at first about functionality and product origin (Made in China). Here are my thoughts: --- Setting up: I had no problem with installing and setting up this device. The manual provided clear instructions and I just followed it step by step. --- View: you can control the view on your phone by simply swiping your finger (see my video). --- Quality: the video quality is amazingly good. I tested the warning alarm and when it went off, the siren was loud enough to ward off any unexpected guest. --- Motion detection: I attached a short video of me testing this function. This function is what I need the most since I cannot stick my eyes on the monitoring screen to guard the house all the time. The motion detection of this camera works perfectly for me. I received notification quickly (or instantly depend on how strong your internet is) so I can react in time if someone breaks into my house. One weakness that I noticed is that this camera depends on electricity and internet to work. So my advice if you want to make this camera your main security system: connect it to a power bank/power storage so that if your house's power goes off, the camera will still be working. review_title: Camera is working well for me
review_text: I received the security camera earlier than expected. It arrived in excellent condition. Set up was super easy, instructions were included. They are also on the sellers product page (on Amazon). Download DigooEye and follow the step by step directions for set up and recording. The camera supports wireless and wired connection and has a lot of great features. Some of the features include Pan/Tilt/Zoom, 1080p Resolution, night vision, motion detection ( it can track a moving object) and video recording. The video can automatically be saved to a SD card (not included). This camera also supports ON IF and fast connection. (You can read more about it online or in the instructions). It also has the capability of 4x Digital zoom. When ideas researching various cameras, there were so many to choose from and I had so many questions that needed answers before making a choice. What wad so helpful on this particular camera was the consumer reviews, as well as, the many questions/answers on the product page. I felt comfortable ordering the DIGOO-M1Z It had all the features that I was looking for in a surveillance camera. Not too mention that it works as described. The quality of the camera and the picture is very good. I was greatly surprised. I would recommend this to others that are looking around at the many surveillance camera available. The first few times that I used the camera, I had a few problems with viewing the picture at night. I have put the camera in a better location and haven't had an further issues. If you have a light on. In the same room, try to make sure there is some lighting behind the camera, not pointed directly at it. My picture was better this way. One other issue was losing connection. I believe that this issue is my internet connection, not the camera. We are in the process of changing carriers and I think this will fix the problem. I will update my review later if needed. My favorite part....checking on the pets when I'm away.

review_title: Good Pic Quality, Lags a Bit
review_text: This is the first security-type camera I've ever owned, so it's a new experience for me. It was extremely easy to set up; I didn't even read the instruction manual. It comes with a pretty long power cord as well. But I'm pretty annoyed at how lazy these companies have become by sending you the USB cord with no adapter. The camera angle is nice and wide. I have a small apartment and I can see the doors in both my living room and kitchen. I attached a picture for reference. The picture quality is VERY good. The image is crisp and clear. I can clearly see the facial features of anyone who is in view of the camera. The app provides a nice experience as well. I really like the walkie talkie feature. I can let my dog hear my voice throughout the day. I also like how you can pan/tilt the camera with a swipe of your finger. But this brings me to what I dislike most about the camera: the delay. Sometimes there's 4 second delay, sometimes there's barely a delay at all. But more often than not, there is a seconds-long delay between real-time and the live stream. I'm not sure if that's normal for all security cameras, but it's something I definitely noticed with this one. Another thing is that the other night, I walked into my kitchen and apparently set off the motion alarm (which I don't remember engaging). It really scared me. The positive side is that it's a very loud police siren alarm which could definitely scare off intruders. So for the affordable price tag, this is a good camera that I would totally recommend. The pros definitely outweigh the cons and I'm pleased!

review_title: I don't like the design; earbuds exact copy of Apple earbuds; charge port broke on second use
review_text: TL;DR: exact copy of Apple earbuds with badly-placed, poor-quality control module - but YMMV. PROS - inexpensive - sound isn't bad - lightweight - comes with cool silicone earbud wraps - if you love Apple earbuds you'll love these CONS - crappy power port - sound isn't great - range is poor - awkward design - if you hate Apple earbuds you'll hate these The control module is at exactly the wrong place for my body shape. If you put the wire behind your neck, the module wants to dangle forwards where it looks stupid, or it wants to dangle backwards where it's hard to reach and ends up pulling the left earbud out of your ear when you turn your head. In either case you have to fumble for the controls becaue you have no idea where they are. And if you put the wire under your chin, the weight of the module pulls on your right ear and eventually dislodges that earbud. (YMMV on all of this because your body probably doesn't match mine.) Sound quality is OK (Bluetooth), but the range is very short with my MacBook Pro. It starts cutting out within ten feet. This won't be a problem if you're using them with your phone, but could be a problem if you want to use them with your computer. There is also a problem with Macs where if you start an app that wants to use the microphone (such as Skype) the audio quality goes straight into the toilet. Not the fault of these earbuds, it happens with any Bluetooth device (well, all of them I've ever tried, anyway). Workaround is to use the Mac's built-in microphone instead of the mic in the Bluetooth device. I was really surprised that the earbuds themselves are IDENTICAL to Apple-branded earbuds. I am guessing that the manufacturer has been buying up returned Apple earbuds (or buying them on the surplus market) and connecting them to their own Bluetooth module. Even the wires are identical. IANAL, but if these weren't actually originally manufactured by Apple, then they're clearly violating Apple's copyright. Note that if you don't like Apple's earbuds, then you won't like these either (and vice versa). Personally I'm kind of middle-of-the-road on the fit. I like Apple's older round style of earbud a lot better than these. One cool feature is that these earbuds ship with silicone wraps for the earbuds that have a little horn that fits into your ear and keeps the earbuds in place. However, I found that this made them a bit more uncomfortable, but it's probably worth it if you plan to go jogging with them. (That was my plan, BTW.) Finally, the charge port felt really cheesy and rough when I first plugged in the included adapter cable, and on the second insertion the port broke off inside the module. It may have something to do with the plug that covers the port - you need to bend it way back to get it out of the way of the plug, and this puts stress on the port. They should redesign this. The product included a card that said I should contact IXIR for support. However, all they have on the website is a web form - no chat or phone number. I didn't try it because Amazon support is better. Personally, I'm returning these to Amazon and purchasing a pair that has the buttons on one of the earbuds. Then you know exactly where the buttons are at all times, and you don't have a dongle bouncing around and bonking you on the collarbone. For example, these by Sbode , or these by HOPDAY , or just search for "bluetooth headphones with mic for running" and pick one you like. Incidentally, Amazon's return policy is that you can't ship a damaged item back to Amazon if it has lithium batteries in it. This item has a polymer lithium battery (the flammable kind), so I called Amazon's customer service and let them know it's against their policy for me to send it back. The rep told me I could keep the item and they'd just refund me. This means I can keep the silicone wraps!

I placed the metal ring that comes with the accessory between the phone and the cover and I have been using the charger in my own car fixed to its base (see my picture) and in my wife's car attached to the air vent. The magnet is strong enough and it is holding the phone pretty tight, and the charger starts charging at your first try (on some wireless chargers you need to move the phone around until it starts working). It is not a slow charger, I am not sure how fast it is, but it is much faster than my other wireless chargers. It looks good, and i love the fact that i can take it out from its base and take it to other cars and attach to the air vent. I haven't tried the charger with iPhone 8 yet, but if it works as good as it does with Samsung phone, it will solve one big problem for me, which is carrying two sets of cables in our cars for my wife and I. review_title: It's OK. Ring fits on iPhone X. Charging speed leaves a lot to be desired.
review_text: UPDATE: I've used it now for a few days under various conditions and have updated my score to reflect how I feel about it. The good: 1. The magnetic mounting (with the metal ring inside my slim case) works well, seems secure enough in the car. It's not as strong of a hold as my non-charging magnetic mount was, but it is sufficient. I don't expect it to go anywhere. 2. It looks nice in the car. 3. The sticky mount feels secure. I don't have a lot of smooth surfaces so I stuck it to the display part of my stock radio. There isn't much on it that I need to see so it worked out OK. The bad: 1. Charging speed - It's not very impressive. In my first test it took 2 hours to take my phone, while I was not using it in any way, from 75% to 100%. While using it with GPS, and with the screen constantly on at about 75% brightness, it basically was only able to keep the phone from draining. After a 40 minute drive the battery was exactly at the same level as when I started. When not using GPS, with the screen off and streaming bluetooth audio, it gave me a bit of a trickle charge up from where I started. 2. The metal ring's sticky side was useless on my iPhone X glass back. I thought maybe using it without the case would help it charge better, but the metal ring popped off seconds after I stick it on. It just didn't work at all, so I am stuck with using my case to hold the ring. FInal thoughts: I considered returning it, but decided to keep it. It's literally the same effort to mount as what I had previously, and I get a small charge, or at least holding the battery even. If needed I can always plug in my lightning cable for a quicker boost. I'll probably keep a lookout for a more powerful version of this type of charger/mount in the future, but this will do for now. INITIAL IMPRESSIONS: I just received this and plan to use it in the car. My biggest worry was that the metal ring (to hold the phone in place via magnets) might be too big either on the phone itself, or to fit inside my Spigen Thin Fit Case Turns out it fits great in both situations! I took some photos showing the ring on the iPhone X. By this weekend I will see how well it charges and how well it mounts in my car. I will update this review with more observations at that time, but so far it looks to be exactly what I was hoping for!

review_title: Love having an inconspicuous mount and no wires to mess with.
review_text: When paired with a solid, strong USB power source, this is a great phone mount. I love the ease of setting your phone against it, but you do have to pay attention to get it properly centered on your charging coil in your phone. It's great that I can easily see the screen without having to fumble to pick up my phone. When I do decide to pick up the phone, grabbing it from the magnetic mount is effortless. If you're running power-hungry navigation apps on your phone, the charger can struggle to keep up if you're not using a good USB source, good cable, or if you simply didn't center the phone on the charging coil. I use an Anker usb charger, Anker USB cables, and have developed a method to ensure my phone (Samsung s6) gets centered on the coil, and don't have problems with the charging. However, it's never a fast charge. I use it for trips where charging speed isn't a requirement. I also keep a 2nd USB cable for passengers/kids or if I need to charge up more quickly. PROS: - Quick, easy placing of phone onto mount - Holds the phone solid (when using the included metal ring) - Is very inconspicuous with or without the phone mounted. - Lets you see your phone easily - Keeps your phone charged without messing with cables. CONS: - The magnetic ring only makes it stick, but doesn't help you properly center your phone. You have to learn to consistently place the phone centered. - Mediocre charging speed. This seems to be more of a limitation of the Qi standard. Using a good power source and USB cord helps this.

review_title: Not A Bad Drill--But Not Great Either
review_text: For those who are thinking you're going to receive a professional quality tool at this price point, think again. This is a $40 cordless drill and is only 12V, so it's not going to keep up with the 18V-20V big boys. However, I knew this going in and wanted something inexpensive and light for general use, so I pulled the trigger. Upon removing the drill from its factory box, I immediately noticed that the storage case the drill comes in was different than the one pictured. The one pictured in the listing clearly shows an orange and white Tacklife logo on the center on the lid, mine was just plain black. Not a big deal at all, but not off to a great start either. Upon deeper inspection of the case I also noticed a dent on one of the corners near the carry handle. It's about the size of a pea and led me to investigate further. It appears to be a solid, well built case in the picture, but it's minimal protection in reality. The case has many hollow chambers due to its blow molded construction and one can put a dent in it with just finger pressure. A drop directly on any corner will likely result in damage. The hinge is just a thin plastic ribbon with no real support either. The clasps are indeed metal as shown in the picture, but they open extremely easy and don't clamp as tight as I would like. Just a drop onto the carpet from arm length and one popped open. One nice surprise though, was that there is space for an additional battery. Of course extra batteries are not available yet, but it's nice to know an extra one fits. Overall, the case is a bummer. While it does offer storage and minimal protection, I don't expect it to last. If you're going to use it everyday, store anything heavy on it, or constantly drag it across rough surfaces, you will not have a case very long. The drill comes with a 1500mAh battery, charger, AC adapter, 6 drill bits, 6 screwdriver bits and a magnetic bit holder. The physical build of the battery and charger seem to be of good build quality, but the drill bits are just standard, cheap bits that you can find anywhere for pennies. The magnetic bit holder is not chrome hardened steel, but seems to be a type of alloy and is not as good as what you would get from Dewalt or other high end drill manufacturer. The drill feels good in the hand, has a hefty weight, is well balanced and has rubberized panels for a firm grip. I actually fell in love with how good it actually felt! The entire rear portion of the drill housing is coated in rubber, which is a plus when needing to give it an extra push through tough materials. The Battery is easy to remove and replace and provides pretty good balance when in use. The forward and reverse selector is placed in the right spot, the trigger is smooth and variable speed works well. Above the trigger is an LED work light, which is nice and bright, but fails to provide any real usable light on the exact work area. It's placed in a bad spot, making the drill head cast a shadow over the work area and unless you're using a long extension, the light is not useful. The closer you are to the work, the less light you get. It puts light everywhere but exactly where you need it...disappointing. The picture posted in the listing clearly shows tons of light on a screw head, which is false and obviously photoshopped. Remaining battery life is shown on the left side of the drill by three, blue LED indicators, which light up anytime the trigger is pressed. This looks cool and gives the drill a futuristic look when in use, but it just eats up valuable battery life. I would prefer to have a button to check battery voltage or a single, LED low voltage indicator instead. Speed of the drill is selected by a sliding button on the top of the drill, which offers a high and low speed. The button is labeled 1 at the top and 2 at the bottom, indicating the selected speed, but they are low in contrast and impossible to read. It's really not necessary to label them anyway, but I thought I would mention it. As far as drill performance goes, it's actually a decent 12V drill. It does not have the high RPM or torque specs of it's competitors, but they are twice the price. This drill has enough torque to actually cause a little wrist flip, which was surprising. I tried to grab the chuck at full speed with my firmest grip in an effort to slow it down. While I could stop it from spinning, it was a painful experience. My biggest complaint with the drill is the dismal battery life. It's only a battery pack consisting of 3 18650 batteries @ 1500mAh (1.5 amp hours), which I would consider very small compared to the 2000mAh of others, but I still expected better performance. I have a 12v drill from Ryobi with a 1500mAh battery and performance is way better on that drill. I don't know if the battery needs to be broken in, but I only had a little over an hour of use before needing to be recharged. This hour was spent drilling about twelve, 2" long, 1/8" holes in a sheet of Poplar, which is a very soft wood. The battery died shortly after when trying to run in 3/16" lag bolts into the holes. Don't expect anything even close to the manufacturer specs for holes/screws drilled...maybe half at best. Another think to consider on any power drill is something called "Concentric Runout". Simply put, this relates to how centered the chuck is and how much it wobbles while in motion. This is a negative of any cordless drill. You will be hard pressed to find a cordless drill without concentric runout. All one needs to do to see how much runout a drill has, is to put in a very long drill bit or extension and pull the trigger. The more the tip of the bit wobbles, the worse the runout. How does this affect performance? Simple, if you're trying to drill a precise hole at a certain size, you will find the finished size is slightly bigger, or out of round. When driving a 4" wood screw, you will notice it's hard to drive the screw in straight. Even high end Dewalts and have wobble...it's just something one needs to be aware of. Some brands have more than others. The Concentric runout on this particular drill is fairly average for it's chuck size and price range. It actually has less than my Ryobi, which is surprising. The listing, and Tacklife's website states a 24 month warranty, but included with the drill is a warranty card that states only 6 months, with a 3 month extension upon registering on their website, for a total of 9 months. Not sure which is accurate, but the lack of accurate information included with the product does not inspire confidence in their warranty. Conclusion: the drill functions and works well for a 12V at a $40 price. It feels good, really good in the hand. It has decent power and torque for a 12V. However, the poor quality of the case, bad LED light placement , dismal battery life and no option to purchase an additional one makes it just an average tool. There are better options out there for just a few bucks more. This will be going back for a return if battery performance does not increase. **** Update **** 1/15/2018 I wanted to like this drill so much that I was willing to accept its caveats. However, the rubber around one of the housing screws began to peel away and I had to return it.

I quote his email here, in case somebody has the same problem, "One thing you can check is the calibration. Place it where you want it to go and turn it on. Let it settle at 0.0 before stepping on to weigh in. Try this a few times and let me know if that helps.".And it totally helped! Now it's precise and not capricious anymore. :).Looks great and works great. Also, it keeps showing your weight after you step off it, so if you have bad eyesight, you can always step off and check (I wear contacts but sometimes I check my weight when my contacts are off and I'm blind'ish, so it's nice that I can just step off and check instead of doing crazy gymnastics while on the scale!).Huge thanks to customers support. review_title: Secure and comfortable & easy to use
review_text: I was looking for a car seat for our yorkie-poo. He loves to go bye bye with us and we take him on trips with us. We were interested in a car seat for our dog because we want to make sure our pet is protected and safe while riding in the car. This pet car seat is great quality and also very cute! The seat has a cute design with paw prints, and comes with a nice soft blanket to lay in the bottom to make more comfortable. Included with the car seat you get a leash and straps to secure the seat to your car. There is a strap to attach to your dogs collar to keep them securely in their seat. I was very happy with this purchase, I received it quickly and it was easy to assemble, lightweight and very easy to use. Our dog seemed to be comfortable and secure and it had helped so much to keep him from climbing on us while driving. This is a great pet car seat, great quality and the perfect size for the dog to have room to be comfortable. I received my order quickly and feel like this was a great choice at a reasonable price!

The concept of this puppy carseat is awesome, but unfortunately the design fell short. As soon as I clicked my puppy into the basket, he immediately wanted out. The sides of the basket collapsed under the weight of my whopping 8 lb puppy attempting to prop his front paws up to see out of the window, which left him continuously falling over and flopping around in the passenger seat.. Even worse, the built in "safety leash," meant to keep puppy in place, actually wrapped around his neck a couple times while I was driving, causing me to panic and pull over to unhook. Honestly, this contraption was more of a hazard for me than help.

Great car seat for our 12 week old Boston Terrier. He doesn't get nervous in the car, but he would always be on my lap in the passenger seat while husband drives. However, we were in need of a car seat to keep him safe when we're driving alone. This car seat works for our pup, but if you're looking for something to RESTRAIN a very agitated dog in the car, maybe this car seat is not ideal. Like other reviews mentioned, the sides are quite flexible and will bend if your dog tries to step on it. Also, the strap that attaches to the harness/collar may be too long. You can tie a knot and make it shorter, but then the dog can't lie down and sleep. But overall for $20 this a really great car seat.

Not sure what some were expecting but for something less than $20, youre getting exactly what you paid for...

It is not sturdy at all, very badly designed. The support poles are on the inside of the seat giving the dog access to chew on them. The strap for my last car seat for my shih tzu broke, so I ordered this one. Big difference, and not in a good way... This car seat is NOT sturdy at ALL!!! The “metal bars” provided are not real metal; they’re flimsy and they bend. I basically took the metal frame from the old car seat, cut holes in the new one, and put it in there. AND, instead of putting the straps around one headrest, I put them around two so she could be higher and actually see out of the window. If I were to use it as pictured, she would only be lifted up a few inches, which defeats the purpose, but this may just be for my car. My dog gets carsick, so this a necessity. review_title: A Lot of Features, Cool Looking, A Bit Flimsy & A Bit Flawed
review_text: This is a really cool light with some nice features, but it has a few drawbacks, one I consider quite important. The Pros: The lights are very bright The laser lane markers are nice There are a number of light settings (steady on, fast strobe, slow strobe, several moving patterns) Turn signals are nice but probably ineffective except at very close range (see Cons, below) Multifunction wireless remote with indicator lights Cool appearance Rechargeable battery (in light, replaceable in remote) The Cons: First, the biggest problem - The light sensor, which is intended to save battery life, prevents the light from being used in daylight. This feature should be programmable. It isn't. I think it is important to be able to use the flashing light feature during the day to attract attention to my existence. No can do with the built-in light sensor. Given that the remote has indicator lights to let you know if the light is on and what it is doing, this sensor is more of a drawback than a plus. Set-up instructions are microscopic but not much help even if readable Light is somewhat flimsy - not sure how much riding shock it can take The light cannot be turned on or off from the remote. There is a separate on/off switch on the light unit, which must be held for a considerable amount of time to either turn the unit on or off. Once it is on, its functions can be controlled from the remote. If this light was somewhat sturdier and had a few design improvements, I would give it 5 stars because it has a lot of cool features and the lights are very noticeable, Too bad it can't be used during daylight.

Nice product. The side laser beams alone are worth the price since it really keeps people and drivers from getting too close, especially at night. This is probably one of the better safety products I've come across to add to my bike. Sadly the product stopped working after a week. The remote would not communicate with the base unit. Before I could remove it or try to fix it, the lithium battery is on the bottom under a cheap cover and it fell out while riding and was lost since I didn't notice right away. Cheap plastic and unreliable electronics have ruined a nicely designed product.

review_title: The instructions SUCK. They might be a great product if you ...
review_text: The instructions SUCK. They might be a great product if you are a mainland Chinese native, however as an educated US citizen they SUCK. This product will go down the tubes in the US if they don't provide a manual that makes sense in clear, concise ENGLISH. The product probably works, however the instructions DOOM the product to the CESSPOOL of a great ideas poorly marketed. My original comments on this product are listed above and were based on the frustration I felt in trying to understand how the product worked. A major contributing problem was the daylight override which would shut the device off after several seconds. It is fairly difficult to figure out a new product in the dark. An e-mail to the manufacturer was promptly answered and daylight override problem was solved with a small piece of aluminum foil tape placed over the light sensor on the bottom of the unit. Having had several days to become familiar with the product, I am now favorably impressed with the product. The vendor has e-mailed me and said that a English friendly version of the instruction is now available. Whether the instructions will include a how to disable the daylight override is unclear. The light is fairly large and prone to shaking and shifting on bumpy rides. I replaced the foam tape provided for the clamp with a foam BMX bar grip on the seat stem. This provides a much better foundation for clamp and reduced the shifting of the light on rough roads. The positioning of the sending unit is limited to one position. Although this is a minor issue, it would be nice if the unit could be rotated 90 degrees (a set of groves on the other two edges of the sending unit would do the trick). Since I will be using the unit primarily during the daylight hours, I don't really have a need for the laser projection option. I haven't used it and don't expect most folks will find it useful. I have replaced the short USB charging cable with a 6 cable so I can charge the unit while on the bike from an outlet in the garage. Overall this is a very nice bike accessory. I would go as far as to say it is required if you value your well being. There are some issues that should be addressed however it is the best turn signal, rear light I have found to date.

So far, I am really liking this light!! It is equal or better in brightness than a 6" oval LED truck light I'd placed on the bike. The mounts were easy to set up, and instructions were in tolerable English. There are a few points that make this light "not perfect" but still valuable. The charging port cover could stand a better fit. It tends to be too loose, and might be dislodged on a bumpy ride. The yellow LED's are far too weak to match the powerful red LED's, even in the turn indicator modes, they tend to get lost. In daytime, the turn signals do not work, as all light functions are filtered through the "energy saving light sensor" which turns the light off when not needed. The mount is a "universal seatpost clamp" , but if you love to carry stuff on a rear rack, the light may be obstructed, a "universal rack" or "build your own" bracket would be awesome so the taillight could be at the back of the rack, out of the way.. The Lane Marking Lasers... I LOVE IT!!!! Best idea in bike lighting since the idea of riding at night! :-) I really do LOVE this light, one of the best lighting solutions I've seen! Winter note, the controller might be hard to work through gloves...... UPDATE: 2-2016: Yes, the charge port covers WILL get lost! The only other notable weakness I see is no side visibility with this light. Awesome rear light though. UPDATE 7-1-2016: The mounts to the bike dont do so well if you have to change it from bike to bike. the plastic band that ratchets through the mount can develop a curve that causes it to snag rather than slide through the mount. The mount is the one weak point to the system. i havent seen replacement mounts for sale, but, with the affordable price, I still like how good the light is.

review_title: Decent for the first 2 months of daily commuting
review_text: The light is nice and bright, but the programming and manufacturing quality are poor. For a light with built in turn signals, the signaling functionality should NOT be tied to a light sensor. If the main light turns off in daylight, the turn signal should reactivate the light when the appropriate button is pressed on the remote. The remote failed on me after only 2 months of use. The buttons don't activate easily and require a very precise press that distracts you while riding. I found myself wondering if the button press happened. I often discovered after getting off the bike that the turn signal was still going from a prior turn, even though I pressed the button to deactivate the signal. The only saving grace is that the middle button cancelled the turn signal. Given that the remote failed, the light now only functions as a standard bright tail light. Like others, I had to cover the light sensor with black electrical tape to disable the auto-off functionality of the light. I will continue use until the light itself fails. Steer clear of this lighting setup for daily use and commuting!

review_title: Very bright and easy to install, turn indicators are a joke. 3.5 stars
review_text: I was excited about getting this wireless bike light for my wife so she could signal turns when riding - she has trouble letting go of one hand to signal a turn the old fashioned way, so this was the perfect solution. We have used it for a few weeks now and the bottom line is this - it is a great product because it allows you to wireless control the light right from the handlebar, it is VERY bright, and the laser lights are a superb added safety feature when riding in low light conditions. However, the light is unreliable in some respects and the turn signals are a joke. Here's a quick rundown. PROs: - VERY bright during day and night times. Keep the rider visible from a distance. - Easy to set up the light (under the seat) and the controller (on handlebar). No need for the adhesive tape, that just creates confusion during the installation process. - Two laser lights that throw light beams on the road behind the bike, making is a lot more visible in the dark (these laser lights are not really visible during the day and they don't need to be). - No cables required to connect controller to light, it's wireless. CONs: - Installation and operation instructions are a joke. Fortunately, the product is fairly straight forward to use. - The turn indicators (the main reason I bought this light) are a joke as well. The actual turn indicator is a small light, but when you signal a turn, the entire main panel light also starts flashing, which makes it impossible for motorists behind you to see that you're signalling a turn. All they'll see are dancing lights under your seat. For me personally, this defeated the whole purpose of buying the light. - The light should have had an option to make it flash, this feature would have been very helpful when riding at dusk when the light is perhaps the least visible and riding conditions are the worst. - Slightly cheap construction. It holds up well, but the light and controller often keep moving around when mounted and need to be adjusted back into position. Overall a good bike light if that's all you're looking for, though there are cheaper battery operated lights that are available for $4-5 that work just fine as a basic bike light, and they also have the flashing lights feature - but they need to be left on at all times. The big benefit of this one is that it is really very bright and can be turned on/off from the controller on the handlebar. 3.5 stars.

review_text: I read a lot of mixed reviews on this item so I decided that I had to buy it to test it for myself. A lot of complaints i read was about how the product stop working or how it would not hold a charge which i thought had happened to me. The next morning I re-charged it and after I turned it back on I realized that the product kept turning off immediately right after i turned it on. I soon realized after waving my hand back and forth over the item that it had a daylight sensor built in it that turns the light off for what I am assuming is power save mode (Which uses your battery even when it is off) when there is light and on when there isn't light. You could easily mistake this for turning the light off during the day time. The product would be better if their was an LED or something to indicate that the light was still on and that it is not just in power save mode. They should at least mention it on the product so that people who buy it would at least know that there is a daylight sensor built into it. PS: To always keep the light on and not stress out if the light is off or in power save mode place some black tape over the day light sensor.

Solid on Turn signals and taillight flashing seperately Turn signals solid with the taillight's light going from the center outward to left and right Side lasers can be odd, solid, or flashing with any mode. The turn signals may as well not exist. They are very small and are unable to effectively communicate that you are going to turn. The taillight goes from left to right or right to left but its not something that makes it obvious. If I saw a bike with this light on and the turn signal on I would not recognize the intent to turn even though I own one. The lasers are pretty cool. They basically create a lane for you which makes you more noticeable and lets drivers know that encroaching into those lines is unsafe. The width of the lane depends on how high up the taillight is. They seem well made and I am really hoping the longevity of these lights is good because it can be a pain to decorate a tree with the copper strand, but it's well worth it. I used 4 33' strands on our Japanese Maple out back and am very satisfied with the results. Decorating took just over an hour. My only issue with the lights is the remote. Unfortunately you must aim the remote directly at the controller as the remote is IR. Depending on where your controller is located, this can be difficult. Overall, I would recommend this product.

Love love LOVE these lights! I recently moved into a condo with a non-functioning wood-burning fire place. Eventually I want to put in an electric firebox, but until then, I wanted some kind of ambience illumination coming from the big black hole in the corner. I purchased two sets of these lights and wove them around a set of fake logs. I put one set to the lowest always-on setting, and the other to the setting where they illuminate slowly from off to fully lit every 10 seconds which creates a little bit more of the fire-place feeling. Pros: *Thin copper wire has a ton of flexibility and easily bends how you want *The length of the wire is long enough to wrap, bend, twist in any configuration *The number of settings and options is AMAZING *One remote will turn the two sets I have off/on simultaneously Cons: *As other reviewers have said, getting them untangled from the box can be an exercise in frustration. Out of the two sets I got, one uncurled easily but the other set took about 10 minutes to untangle. *The sets can not be attached to one another. I plugged them into the same outlet beside the fire place. I can't speak to the longevity of the sets since I've only had them a short while, but since I won't be using them on a daily basis I'm hoping they'll last!! **UPDATE 2/12/18** Since my last review, I've purchased 2 more set of these lights. The fireplace lights are still functioning perfectly! Of the new sets, I use one set in my bedroom filling a glass bowl on my dresser. I set the lights to ON with the remote and then they're on a timer for the morning, to slowly wake me up (simulating the sun rise at 5am). With the copper wire, they look great in the bowl during the day, a nice decoration! They've been going strong for a year with daily use. The third set I put on my headboard, set the lights to ON with the remote, purchased an extension switch, and I use them at night for enough light to see to get into bed, then just reach down and flip them off with the switch. I did try them first with the remote, which worked great, until I dropped the tiny thing behind the bed out of arm's reach, which caused much cursing and unhappiness at having to move my mattress off the bed at 11pm when I just wanted to go to sleep!! The extension switch solved that issue! I'm trying to think of other places I could use these things I love them so much! Picture of the lit lights in the glass bowl and vase was from last week. 2nd picture of unlit lights in the bowl is from today. I just condensed them to one container instead of 2.

review_title: LOVE THESE LIGHTS! VERY BRIGHT AND VERY LONG!
review_text: I have to say, I was VERY PLEASED with these lights! They were much brighter than I expected and the length of the strain of lights is very long! I had some battery operated LED lights, similar to these, however, though they were LED's the batteries would drain quite often, even when not in use. The idea of plugging the lights in was appealing, plus being able to power the lights on and off with the remote was another nice addition to this unit. I also liked that you could dim the lights with the remote as well. I added the lights to the center of my dinning room table. Photos included. Just what I needed!
I put them in a large clear glass lemonade container which sits on top of our kitchen cabinets and they look and work great.

When I first got these I was skeptical about the quality because it is just some really thin copper wires connected to LED lights but I plugged them in and they worked great. The remote did just what it was supposed to do. However, after using them for an actual project I learned a few things. One, the remote has to have a direct line to the sensor or it will not work at all. Also, if the remote doesn't work for some reason, the lights are useless. Second, the wires are as weak as they look. About a week into having them, one of the wires broke or something. I haven't looked into enough. It was at the main connection. It's the one place covered in plastic so I haven't been able to simply reconnect it by twisting them together and tape or solder. I'll have to cut the plastic away to see where it broke. Since it is a simple wire, I should be able to just reconnect it. Hopefully it will work again. But with wire that thin, I don't doubt it will be the last time it breaks. Hopefully I can fix it and it will last long enough for it to be worth it. So, if you are handy with wires and you don't plan to put these in an area they will take any abuse, they will probably be a great buy for you. Good price and they look great, just not durable.

review_title: Best product I've purchased on Amazon
review_text: I absolutely love it. It is exactly how I imagined it would be. My bed is up on a loft so I find it very convinent that I can use the remote to turn off and on the lights

review_title: Not as warm colored as they look
review_text: So these work perfectly fine, but the pictures are a bit deceiving. The lights are much more white than they appear in the pictures. Closer to a bright white. I also made the mistake of assuming that the fade function would work more like a twinkle where the lights fade in and out at a different time as the ones next to it. They all fade on and off at the same time. Also, there's is quite a jump at the lowest part of the fade. It seems to jump from 10% to 0% then back to 10%. I placed these in my fireplace around some logs to try to get a kind of fire look for the summer, but i've only really used the 10% solid dim setting since i don't really like the way the fade works. Also, i also wish that they were a warmer color then a solid function would still somewhat capture the look i want. Like i said at the very beginning, These lights work great, and were super easy to set up. My main reason for only 3 stars is that the description of the product says that they are "warm white-yellow Mini Led Lights" and they are NO WHERE close to yellow. Much closer to bright white or daylight.

I love these little lights! I bought them for my lighted Christmas village. I have them strung around and between the houses and they are just the right size. The copper wire made it easy to string them the way I wanted them. They're bright and they look very festive. So far, they work great. They were just what I was looking for.
These lights are awesome! I almost ordered another set today, but I'm not supposed to be shopping for myself right now.

review_title: Cons The remote control takes some getting used to/is so small that it is easily lost (I used removable stickies to mount it to
review_text: I've had these lights set up for a few weeks and here is what I have to say so far: Cons The remote control takes some getting used to/is so small that it is easily lost (I used removable stickies to mount it to the wall) The fixable nature of the copper wire can be a double-edged sword--it tangles easily/untangles with great difficulty. Therefore, mount/hang/loop it once and leave it as long as possible Pros Everything else. The lights generate no heat, have myriad settings such as dimming in 10% increments/various flashing, strobing, and fading speeds and strengths--learn the remote. They look great in my kitchen wrapped around this odd fence molding (which took 40 minutes to do--see con #2) near the ceiling. They are usually on all the time, though I dim them to their lowest setting as a sort of nightlight. They are barely bright enough for, say, cooking, but their purpose is more ornamental/mood-setting.

review_title: These look great under my dining room table!
review_text: I really love these lights. I bought them to add a touch of ambiance to my picnic-turned-dining table in my second home. The picnic table was a great idea in theory but almost took my dining room too far to the rustic side...but after considering a few options to fancy it up I decided lighting would do the trick. They worked perfect! They are durable and just 1 set was able to wrap the underside of the table multiple times. I love them and have received many compliments on how unique they are in the home. They are not like christmas lights at all...they are much better! I will use these all year round. See pictures... My only slight complaint would be the remote control...I knew I was buying lights with an added IR remote but it really does have to aimed just right to work on the lights and sometimes I find myself unplugging the lights rather than using the remote. The remote is not a big deal at all. I highly recommend these lights!
