review_title: The good: - Excellent materials and construction
review_text: Overall, a little disappointing. The good: - Excellent materials and construction. All toys should be made of nice, solid aluminum. - Relatively quick and mostly easy to assemble. It took my 7 year old about 1 hr with me actively helping. Leave the screws in the labeled bags until you need them. - Scratch style programming interface is easy to get started for those familiar with Scratch. - Great instructions for the mechanical assembly part. The Bad: - No documentation for either app, especially Blockly. There is a half page on Blockly that is mostly just a screen shot. - Blockly is very limited once you start using it. The only sensor that can be accessed from Blockly is "when Tomo senses an obstruction". I thought that there would be light and sound sensors at least, and motion detection. Instead, you can make programs that involve spinning around and making some lights turn on and off. This gets boring quickly. - In Blockly, there are "Detect" and "Event" tabs that are useless and refer functions that are not part of the product or available in the US. They refer to light and sound sensing, PIR (motion) , and even gas detection. The functions don't exist on Tomo - or at least I can't find them. - Bluetooth just dies occasionally and Tomo needs to be reset. - 6 x AA batteries are used instead of a LiPo that could be charged through the micro USB connection (which has no obvious function). Summary: - This feels like a half-finished product. Great construction and mechanical design, but the software team moved on to something else. For the price, I expect more.

I purchased this for my 7 year-old son after a friend of mine whose son has strong science mind highly recommended it. Just like the way I expected, my son had a ton of fun building it. I was a little concerned about the quality but as soon as I got it, I could tell this is a high quality product. Packaging is solid and user manual's easy to follow, even for my 7 year old. I didn't have to build it for him. It is 2 in 1, either Tricycle or Dicycle, and you can control it on smartphone app, which is one of the best features for my son.

Definitely a great deal for what is included. The parts are mostly lightweight aluminum and feel very solid (there is some plastic around the controller board too). The stepper motors don't always move the same amount when programmed to, so the robot usually veers one direction or the other. The app for programming it is pretty good and my 6-year old figured it out pretty quickly. It has a nice "tasks" section that serves as tutorials to teach the basic functions. The kit includes the microcontroller board (with RJ-11 connectors for easy use), an attached LED hat which is programmable, bluetooth interface with phone, an IR sensor for line following (important not to position this too low, it's on sliders so adjustable), and a sonic distance sensor (works so so, about how these distance sensors have always worked for me). review_title: It works and we are pleased with the results for the price.
review_text: Works well and we are pleased for the price. The instructions on use were a little vague but we eventually got it figured out and have made adjustments to sensitivity and correction to fit our dogs behavior. I have a 7 yr old basset hound mix that we keep in the house. He could not control his bark and would get carried away with loud continuous baying regardless of who the person was that he was barking at. We already found the baying very irritating but now we have a new baby in the home and worried about the barking waking the baby and decided to try a bark collar. We started with sound and vibration only which worked well for a while but we eventually had to add the shock, which we keep at a minimal correction level as the collar can inadvertently go off when he shakes his head and ears or if our other dog barks too close. It is not perfect, which is why I have given a four star rating. Adjusting the sensitivity to our dog has seemed to help with most of the inadvertent corrections. The beep tone that sounds when correcting for barking even stops our other dog that does not have a bark collar but is already familiar with remote collar training and knows that the tone is a warning. The battery lasts a long time; we use the collar daily, removing and turning it off nightly to avoid neck irritation and allowing the dogs to bark in defense of their family and home which is rare. I have had the collar nearly a month and have had to recharge the battery only once. Our dog has ceased most barking and will usually only bark once that comes out in a soft woof that will not set off the collar. Our dog has a submissive and sweet temperament and I was worried the collar would cause him to cower or shake with use, but we are relieved to see that is not the case and actually when he hears the collar beep each morning when I turn it on he automatically comes to me to have it put on without me calling him. We pet and praise him each time it is put on. It has made him a more enjoyable dog for everyone. I would not recommend this product for a dog kept outside as I feel you would not be able to monitor the dog close enough and make the necessary adjustments to maintain responsible and humane use of the collar.

review_title: ... the end they turned out to be a big disappointment. The first problem was apparent as soon as ...
review_text: I purchased 2 Digoo DG-ULC Floodlight Outdoor Cameras from Wolifui and I tried as hard as I could to make them work but in the end they turned out to be a big disappointment. The first problem was apparent as soon as I opened the boxes. The mount that encloses the camera and holds the wall lantern have two 1-inch deep holes machined through the solid aluminum mount for mounting screws to pass through. However, one of the cameras I received did not have one of the holes machined through. (See attached photos) I thought I could possibly drill it out myself but there were more problems. Read on. The Digoo U-Cam app is required to to configure the WiFi settings so the camera can connect to a wireless network. The app requires a Digoo account to be set up before a camera can be configured and the configuration process apparently uses Bluetooth to connect to the camera for configuration. The setup process failed over and over until I discovered that the camera could only connect to wireless networks that use WPA/WPA2 encryption and mine used WEP. The skimpy documentation that comes along with the camera doesn't mention any of this and neither does the U-Cam app. It just prompts for a password and them fails WiFi setup after about a minute. After finally getting the camera on my wireless network using WPA2 I could view video through the U-Cam app. Next I wanted to connect the camera to my Synology Surveillance Station DVR along with the other IP cameras in my security system. The Digoo camera is supposed to be ONVIF compatible so I expected this to be easy. It turned out not to be possible because Digoo doesn't appear to conform to the ONVIF standard ports and only the raw RTSP H.265 video stream is available without audio. H.265 is pretty new and my DVR doesn't support it yet. (By the way, neither does the latest version of VideoLAN VLC.) In case anyone is interested, the RTSP H.265 video stream can be accessed with the following URL: rtsp://admin:20160404@[IP ADDRESS]:554 There is also a built-in web portal in the camera but about all it's good for is viewing the video stream and it requires an ActiveX control to be installed before you can log in. Only the H.265 main-stream is available, there is no sub-stream. Any changes to settings have no effect and revert back to their defaults. The username and password is "admin" and "20160404". I also noticed a very disturbing delay in the video, about 24 seconds. In other words, motion in front of the camera took 24 seconds before it was seen on the app. This made no sense until I remembered reading about Chinese IP cameras being very "chatty". I tried blocking all Internet access from the camera with a firewall rule and power-cycled the camera. It still responded to pings on my local network afterwards but the built-in web portal was down and so was the RTSP video stream. After disabling the firewall rule both the web portal and video steam started to work again. Why would a local IP camera need Internet access to supply a local video stream? The only explanation I could come up with is that this model of camera is primarily intended as a cloud device to be viewed anywhere through the Digoo U-Cam app. The local video feed (supposedly ONVIF compatible) is coming from the cloud and being served by the camera. This would also account for the delay in the video stream while it made the round trip. A trace of the traffic from the camera over about 2 minutes showed the following outside IP addresses being contacted. 110.75.186.247 110.75.186.248 110.75.186.249 110.75.190.198 115.28.122.198 120.25.108.11 123.204.45.116 182.92.12.11 202.108.6.95 202.112.29.82 202.112.31.197 202.118.1.130 202.120.2.101 This camera is *very* chatty with servers in China! And if the camera does not have Internet access it cannot be used as a stand-alone IP camera. This last revelation was a deal breaker for me. I had high hopes that these cameras would serve as a not-too-noticeable doorway camera as well as a decorative wall lantern holder *and* be part of my existing security system. They pretty much met the first two criteria but they can never be part of a serious security system if they cannot be secured themselves. I'd rather have my security cameras not sending their video who-knows-where without my knowledge. Summary: Great product idea, poor execution. Digoo should consider a firmware replacement for these cameras that allows them to be used as a stand-alone IP camera. Until then, I'm returning these.

review_title: Great semi hidden Wall Lantern camera
review_text: This is an outdoor camera that hides inside your outside wall lantern. It replaces your base wall lantern and uses the same lamp fixture. The base has a small camera that will record anything in front of it. It has 1080p resolution, motion detection and audio recording. You connect to it via Wifi connection and an app for iOS or Android. The lamp will also automatically turn on at night and turn off during the day. ❤ LIKES: Hidden camera design Easy do it yourself install Can use existing lantern bulb Motion Detection Audio recording Automatic Light on at dusk and off during day 💔 DISLIKES: SD Card not included Night vision is poor No method to download video on iOS No fast forward feature for motion detected videos Phone notification does not seem to work on iOS

Where do I start? This would have been a great concept: an almost hidden camera that can be placed where it puts out its own light. First, it says it's 1080 but if you go into the web GUI 720 is the maximum resolution. I thought it looked soft. Speaking of soft: the picture is sharp around the edges and blurry in the middle. ONVIF doesn't work though it is advertised. It says it supports mSD 64GB cards but the instructions say the card has to be preformatted in FAT32 which only supports 32GB capacity. The web interface is very primitive and many of the options have not effect at all. Email to tech support went unanswered. It looked good. A criminal wouldn't even notice it if they walked past it and the camera is aimable. Assembling the lamp was kind of a pain because the best way to get an outdoor lantern is to buy a similar one and disassemble it. That's OK. The other issues are unforgivable. Buy an Amazon, Nest or or Ring. You will have a much better experience.

This is a great product as long as you are aware of what you are getting. This is only a camera and not a light. It is a camera that is in a housing that can be attached to the side of your house or garage, just like any wall mounted fixture. But please understand that this product is not something you just buy and screw in a light bulb. It comes with two sets of wires on the back, one to hardwire the fixture and one to use for a light. So you need an entire light fixture that you will then mount and wire yourself through the arm of this fixture. I used an outdoor light that is meant to mount to a wall or ceiling and my husband, who is very handy with this stuff, adapted it for me to use with this fixture. So once the light was all attached and the wires were connected, we mounted the unit on the side of our garage. I love the way it looks and I don't think anyone will even realize that there is a camera in there. It looks just like a normal wall light fixture with a dusk to dawn sensor on it. The app for this camera/light is very easy to download and set up. Through the app, I can use the camera remotely, take snapshots and video manually, set it to record when movement is detected, turn the light on and off or set the light to automatically turn on at night and turn off during the day. You have the option to install an SD card to record video and if you are going to do that you really should do it before you install the fixture because you have to take off the back panel to access the SD card slot. Overall I am extremely happy with this camera/light holder fixture. It was much less expensive than anything else I found for this purpose so I was fine with the little bit of wiring that had to be done.

review_title: A Nifty Little Tuner! Don't Spend More For Less.
review_text: There are literally hundreds of small clip-on tuners for stringed instruments available today - many of them, here on Amazon. There are two major variables to consider when choosing which one would be best suited to your needs: These are 1) the ease of use (flexibility of positioning, strength of the clip and clarity of the readout), as well as the function (accuracy of readings and adaptability to different instruments.); and 2) the price. This clip-on from Aniler gets high marks in all areas. Offering five instrument modes (guitar, violin. uke, bass and chromatic) with a set (standard) 440Hz pitch, I have used it easily and more than satisfactorily with both 6 and 12 string guitars, ukuleles, a fiddle and - using the chromatic mode - my banjo! (I also tuned a mandolin which, though not specifically included, is tuned to the same notes as is the violin/fiddle.) No problems to note anywhere. Its accuracy was confirmed using several true online digital tone readers. The readout is bright and clear - even a person who has trouble distinguishing colors would be able to easily read the large note letters from the distance of the tuning end of the instrument. THe clip holds the tuner firmly in place - ordinarily on the headstock of the instrument. I was especially delighted to find that this tuner worked equally well with my electric guitar - something I had questions about. As it turns out, it can 'feel' the vibrations up the neck on an electric (turned on or off) as it can for an acoustic instrument. This tuner meets all of my needs and I expect others will find it completely satisfying as well. The attached photo shows it at work on my Epiphone Les Paul Special II electric guitar. It does all of what I need and does it well - for a price that is hard to dicker about. You can spend a lot more and get a lot less.

What I like: One control - a small 'chicklet' button on the back where it's easy to operate one-handed. 'Boot time' is fast - hold the button for a quick 2 seconds and within another 2 the screen is up with a brief graphical flourish - too many tuners waste seconds on what they think are fancy welcomes and shutdowns that are nothing but time-wasters to me. Mode selection is simple: single-click while powered on toggles instrument/chromatic modes. The last tuning mode selected (uke, guitar, violin, bass, chromatic) is restored on next startup. The 360 swivel is tight and easy for a lefty to position - you'd be surprised how many tuner designs are righty-biased. Power off is same as on - 2 seconds and a quick shutdown. No remembering when to double-click, etc. What I don't like: The yellow 'almost in tune' color is too close to the 'in tune' green to easily distinguish. People with certain forms of color blindness may find this frustrating. While I don't care for fancy startup/shutdown graphics that waste my time, I do appreciate attractive and effective graphics that enhance functionality. The monochrome display on this tuner reminds me is slightly dizzying to read and a dated look by today's standards. The tuner's response is also a bit 'hot' for my taste, meaning I have to adjust string pitch slowly in very fine increments. Other tuners that I have feel more natural to use - I can adjust pitch at a pace I might do while tuning by ear. Bottom Line: Functional and fast operating, if not especially attractive.

Besides, in the old days, many connections had to be made for some devices while power is off -- luckily we have come quite far in technology (in some areas) ;) Overall - love it - super useful at to the reason we purchased it. review_title: Update: VERY prompt customer service, waiting to see build quality of new batch...
review_text: Update: I received an email from MillSO Customer Service the day after leaving my original review. They said the factory was made aware of the issue and has extended the length of the "split" piece to fully contain both cables. I'll update the review when I see how the new part looks... stay tuned! Original review: [Shielding exposed, I question how long it will last...] Ignoring the one issue I have with this product, it seems to be a very built unit. The cables are thick yet flexible, and both male and female ends seem to be well built. The female ends have a good positive feeling when inserting a pair of headphones. The issue I have is with the rubber part where the "split" happens. The "seam" on the stock product photos is a separate part that slides up and down the "female" cables, presumably to keep the two ends closer together (a common feature on earbuds). However, moving the sliding part reveals the two female cables are not fully molded into the "split" piece. Shielding can be seen in the attached picture. I will likely use some glue to fasten the sliding part to the "split" piece and to fasten the female cables within the sliding part. I question how long this splitter will last without some sort of modification to better secure the two female cables to the rubber "split" piece. Also, I haven't used this device with microphones yet, but it appears to split audio as expected.

Is it hot in here or is it just me? On a roundabout of medication this is my most asked question. My husband mentioned as a joke that we could get a thermometer for inside the house, and the idea kind of stuck with me. Now I know I’m not crazy, it is hot in here. AND my husband knows he’s making me late for work with all of the little adjustable alarms! Nice try! I received two of these. One sent first with a bit of a malfunction. I’m chocking that up to USPS since they tend to think “4K tv” around here means “4 kicks.” The second one works just fine. The battery compartment requires 3 AAA batteries, or if you’re constantly worried about battery life you can just plug it in and let it be. The letters can be dimmed, and the power saving mode can be shut off easily enough. The instructions are clear and concise, not hard at all to follow. I had it set up and running within 20 minutes. There’s a small data-keeping battery in the unit as well, so if you decide it’s just not working aesthetically where you set it down, you can move it to a different spot. That’s great, because I’m a bit picky and have already moved it 4 times to different places around the house. Usually where my husband is to remind him we have to go. review_title: Very nice, viewable in daylight, but loud
review_text: Purchased this from another site (just as a full disclaimer). I bought this to replace a green LED alarm clock I had because I didn't like green (or red or blue) LEDs at night, and didn't want something that I had to touch to get a backlight or had constantly glowing. I love this clock. I have the LEDs set at their brightest, which is not too bright in a dark room. I could probably go to the L2 setting for a little less, but I like the brightness, especially during the day. In fact, the day is most useful because unlike most alarm clocks with a glass or plastic screen, this one does not produce glare. Yep, direct sunlight or pitch black room, you can easily see the time. Three alarms are nice, and you can turn them all on or off as you see fit. The alarms are either on or off, no picking days. That's a bummer. However, being able to have 3 different alarms is real convenient. The temperature is one of those "cool" features that isn't exactly useful but is cool. I mean, truly, do you really need to know the temperature inside or do you just need to know that you're hot, cold, or just right? Still, it's neat. The switching of the display from date+year to temperature+time is also "cool," but I find it distracting, especially if you look to get the time and are greeted with the date, then have to stare at it for 10 seconds before you get your time. I would give this 5 stars except for one thing. This thing is loud. For the alarm, you can understand it (when I'm really tired I've been known to sleep through soft alarms), but the darn thing beeps every time you push a button. Need to set the time? BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP, etc. Need to turn off the alarm? BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP, etc. Did I mention it was loud? Yeah, as in your neighbors know you're setting your alarm clock. And if you live in a condo or apartment, they'll know when you're waking up too. If you can avoid changing settings too often (or don't live with musicians), you will love this little gem of a clock. I'm pleased with it, but I would be VERY pleased if the settings didn't BEEP.

review_title: Lets me listen to TV audio over Bluetooth, and for a great price
review_text: I first found this product because of noise levels late at night when watching a movie or show would jump from rather quiet to very loud in an instant. Especially with scenes where music starts playing. So what does this product to do exactly? I use it to transmit audio from TV to a pair of Bluetooth headphones for silent listening in the evening time. It seems there is an option to also use this as a receiver, for example if you had two of these one could transmit the audio from the TV, over Bluetooth, to be received by the second of these devices configured appropriately. While the product comes with a multi step instruction manual, I think it might be helpful to illustrate how I connected mine. In the pictures I show the following setup: 1) TV outputs audio through red/white RCA to a Digital/Analog converter. 2) DIgital/Analog converter outputs 3.5mm audio plug, normally going to the sound bar but I move it to the transmit plug on this device. 3) I press the middle button until the device turns on, ensure transmit is illuminated, and keep it held until the lights start flashing for pairing mode. 4) Next I have the Bluetooth headphones nearby and hold the power button on those until they enter pairing mode also. 5) With both in pairing mode I press the middle button of the transmit device every few seconds to change channels until the light slows demonstrating it is connected to the headphones. The device appears to turn itself off after about 10 minutes of inactivity (no audio activity). When in use, the device has taken around 5 hours to run out of battery and needs to be charged. I have found I can still use it normally while it is charging, however once the battery finishes charging if I keep it plugged to power there is a distracting buzzing sound sent to the headphones. This sounds like a “feature” because I have read the same thing happening in others’ reviews on Amazon. Personally I use an Amazon fire TV stick for watching movies. Based on my experience I would think this product would help anyone using regular TV, Apple TV, Chromecast or other alternatives.

I didn't have a flat fix kit in the car, and since I was within a mile of a rest area, I decided to risk driving on it — an expensive mistake. The biggest problem with most tire pluggers and strings is getting them through the tread, especially if it's a steel belted radial. This kit is compact — always important to a motorcycle traveller — and looks like it should work. I really like the concept, but since I have not yet put it to the test, I'm giving it 4 stars. review_text: Amazing quality and crisp sound, I charged quick and lasted a long time. I am really impressed with the finishing and durability of it, it also connected to both of my Android and iPhone phones right away. It has a silicone shell with a sealable usb port to protect it from water. It has a large suction cup on the back which allows you to stick it to your shower wall. The best thing for us is that we can use it on our boat and it won’t go sliding around when doing watersports. It sticks pretty firmly and you have to pry the edge up in order to get it to loosen its suction. Only time will tell how well the suction cup will last. I’m anticipating that as the material ages, it’ll probably lose some of its suctionability. I’m hoping it’ll be years down the road. I love being able to swap back and forth between bluetooth mode and FM radio! One thing I do dislike about the radio mode is I am unable to tell what station I am on. I still like it though because it's nice to still listen to music without draining my phone battery. It also connected to Bluetooth instantaneously and the sound quality/loudness is excellent. On top of that it is super simple to operate and I enjoy how it lights up and changes colors! The battery life is also great and I love that I just plug it in via USB to charge it back up. This little speaker will be used way more than just in the shower for us. Some speakers don’t allow you to go back to the previous song (although you can skip forward) but this speaker allows you the option to do that. It was easy to pair up with my phone. The speaker plays at greater than the 33 ft distance quoted for this product. It comes with a mini-usb plug. Another fun feature is the led lights on the speaker. A medium-weight cardigan sweater for Fall, Winter, Spring in the North. I am happy to report that this is somewhat warm -- not the warmest possible sweater, but not bad. When I first read the online description of the fiber -- a blend of cotton, viscose rayon, and a little nylon, I thought this likely to be one of those extremely thin, lightweight knit cardigans -- the type that is thinner than T-shirt fabric, for summer only. That is not the case here. The red-black marl pattern is pretty, but a little different than an old-fashioned marl sweater. The difference seems to be that the Lucky manufacturers put the traditional marl pattern on the inner side, while the outside texture of this sweater would have been on the inner side of an old-fashioned marl sweater. I think the inside is prettier, and looks more durable. For a moment, I wondered if I could reverse this and wear it inside-out, but that didn't look right; the inside seams were too bulky to be showing on the outside. This is is an open style with no buttons, no snaps. The front pockets are neat, streamlined, so they do not look bulky, at least when empty. Unlike some sweaters, this does not have dropped shoulders, which is good. The length, when I measured along the center back, is about 34 inches. It appears 1-2 inches longer in front, but that may depend on one's figure. It may stretch a bit, during a long day.

review_title: This little speaker is FANTASTIC! Works as soon as you plug it in
review_text: This little speaker is FANTASTIC! Works as soon as you plug it in, no difficulty in figuring out how it works. I've purchased 5 different portable speakers for use around the house and for my kids but this one is by far the most superior of all and I intend to buy a few more. The volume is pretty loud, I use it with my laptop in the kitchen while listening to music and I can still hear it in the garage and in the upstairs bedroom if I leave my bedroom door open. The sound is clear and and crisp. What a quality product for a fraction of the price.

Features This small compact speaker have 4 great modes 1: Handsfree call speaker 2: MP3 Player 3: Bluetooth Speaker 4: FM radio Design Easily one of the best speakers for its size! Here is why, it is made from a smooth matte plastic which has a great feel to it. It also has 4 little rubber feet 3 of which also works as buttons, these 3 are, go back a track, pause/play and go forward a track. Whilst the speaker is on a flat surface, pressing one of these buttons on top will do what the button says. Very clever design. FM radio The speaker will automatically search through the different frequencies and will find stations. You can use the next and back track buttons to go onto the next radio. Very easy to use. Signal is great in the right positions. Speaker quality The speaker quality is amazing, very loud and the volume is great in small and big rooms. The speaker is very bass heavy. The bass is so boosted that it makes things move and will rattle most moveable surfaces. MP3 Player This works once a Micro SD card is inserted into the TF card slot. Works greatly, very responsive and great audio too. Voice There is a Siri-like female voice that tells you what mode the speaker is in, when the device needs charging it also tells you when a Bluetooth device has connected/disconnected. When you turn on the speaker, a pre-made message in a robotic voice says ""This is your iPhone 4 Bluetooth speaker, I am now in control, you cannot resist my command"" after this a voice says ""Bluetooth mode, the Bluetooth device is connected successfully"" Summary This is a great compact little speaker with great looks, great sound quality and a load of cool features. review_title: I mean, it works, but this is a "NOPE"
review_text: Well, I'll start off by saying that I would NEVER recommend this product to ANYONE. It's not the quality I would hope to expect from a $20+ speaker. There are plenty of better quality speakers out there for the same price or a few bucks more. Even better, if you have a few extra bucks to spend, there are really high quality speakers out there for $50-$80. I would argue that this one has very little going for it to make it worth over $16. cons: - the stupid start up voice! it's obnoxious and unnecessary. If you want to keep this ridiculous intro in the device, add a volume button on the box so I don't have to hear it every time I boot the speaker up! - the low battery voice! yeah, this has a low battery warning that is really annoying. plus, the voice says something to the extent of "please provide power before battery is destroyed" and then immediately dies.... like WHYYY????!!!?!?!! Just turn off and die! - short battery life. this thing only lasted me about 2-3 hours continuously. I mean, I'm only asking for like 5 hours at least. I don't want to have to charge this thing every time I use it or keep it plugged in constantly. - average speaker quality. no better. very cheap. pros: - the lights are pretty. (that's why I bought it) - it technically works... - the bass is more pronounced and higher quality than the overall sound quality. -it's a cube... and that's... different, i guess. Look, if this speaker cost me between 10 and 15 dollars and didn't have an intro and low battery warning that annoyed the living bejesus out of me, it would get a 4 star; however, I guarantee that if the lights hadn't caught my attention, I would have gotten a $30 or $40 device from another company that would have blown this one out of the water. look elsewhere for your own sake.

Absolutely incredibly little speaker! Design By far the best looking mini speaker on the market. It is constructed from a matte plastic which has a good feel to it. There are 4 rubber feet on the bottom which grip well. Three of these feet also act as buttons. So then the speaker is on a flat surface, pressing a button on the top will depress the corresponding rubber foot. A neat and intuitive set of controls! Features This speaker shines in the features department too with 4 modes 1. Bluetooth Speaker 2. Handsfree conference call speaker 3. MP3 Player 4. FM radio Speaker Quality/Tone This is a very bass heavy speaker! It can genuinely shake the surface it rests upon. Those that like bass heavy music will find this very impressive! Overall there is passable sound quality and amazing volume for the size! Bluetooth quality is top notch and the range is also good. FM radio The speaker automatically searches through the frequencies to find stations. You then use the next and back track buttons to quickly skip through stations. Very easy to control with just the three buttons available! The signal can be patchy but works well in the right position. MP3 Player Works when a microsd card is inserted into the slot labeled TF Card. Works well, nice and fast track switching. Good audio quality. Voice feedback There is a quirky female voice which tells you what mode the speaker is in, when you need to charge and that a Bluetooth device has connected/disconnected. When you first turn the speaker on, you will be presented with a lengthy message with sound effects “This is your iphone 4 bluetooth speaker, I am now in control, you cannot resist my command” Before the voice feedback kicks in and says ”Bluetooth mode, the Bluetooth device is-a connected successfully” Conclusion Very well made speaker with great looks, good sound quality and a host of features. Lots of bang for your buck! Recommended!

review_title: I love the RECHARGEABLE Dog Training Collar, it will pay for itself fast. I now do not have to buy new expensive batteries!
review_text: The Dog Training Collar, Digoo-PPT1 Rechargeable, Beep, Vibration and Stimulation Electronic Collar, Fit for All Size Dogs (10Lbs - 150Lbs) arrived on time in a package showing no signs of damage. In the past I have purchaseds 2 shock collars for my dogs but they came with batteries that had a short life and replacing the batteries was very expensive. This dog collar will pay for itself in a short time due to the fact it is easily recharged. As soon as it arrived I charged the Electronic Collar and the hand held remote. Much to my surprise the charge took a very short amount of time. Reading the manual is a must for this electronic stimulation collar. In the past I had no choice but to shock my dogs, with this collar I have 4 training mode choices, Shock, Vibration, Light or Sound. We decided on a low vibration mode for our small dogs. The setting is from 1-100, so if a low setting does not work we can set the level higher. Also, there are choices of metal posts to touch the dogs skin, big dog you use the shorter metal prong, smaller dog like we have, we used the longer metal prong. Once the collar was on our dog and he began running for his doggie door to run outside barking at someone walking behind our fence, I pressed the vibration button and he stopped barking immediately. I am so happy that I do not have to shock him anymore, the vibration mode seems to be a much wiser way to control his barking. Paring the Remote and the Receiver was very easy, just reading the instruction and we had the pairing taken care of in seconds. The charging hole was found immediately on the receiver, it is located under a small rubber flap, just plug in the double wired USB adapter. There is a plug for the receiver and a plug for the adapter. Our settings were set on high at the factory, so check the settings before using the collar, I had to go from 100 down to 01 before we began using the vibration mode. The receiver is water proof, no worries about it getting wet, a relief to us living in the Pacific North West of the US where we can get more than our share of rain and snow. Installing the receiver to the nylon belt collar was extremely easy to do and adjusting was a breeze. I love this new RECHARGEABLE Dog Training Collar.

The range of the shock collar is great! Your dog can get quite far and still correct behavior. The voltage is also quite good. It goes up to 100 and my dog is a very energetic 75# boxer/Australian shepherd mix. So when his behavior was corrected set only at 20 I was quite pleased. The sound is different than other shock collars and this one seems to make my dog more nervous, which is good because I can warn him properly before I have to actually shock him. I think the remote could be a little more sturdy, it feels pretty cheap, but still functions appropriately. The collar itself is nice and fits much better than "belt buckle" style collars and doesn't have excess material hanging off for him to chew on. Overall I am pleased with the product and would recommend to family and friends.

The instructions have not been translated by a native English speaker and so are rather poor. I started my pug off at home and he didn't seem to be affected at all by either vibration or beeping. I thought it wasn't going to work and was not going to bother with it any more when we went on a walk and he was particularly bad with joggers and cyclists and cars and my sister persuaded me to have another go. With the vibration on full, it seemed to have an effect. After he had done his brainless attempt at intimidating a cyclist he stopped and looked puzzled. Things progressed somewhat from there. If he has already gone 'off his head', the collar will not stop him but if I catch him at the right moment, just as he is about to 'go' then it does stop him and increasingly he is leaving cyclists and joggers alone. (I haven't tried it with cars as yet.) I don't always put the collar on him, only when I think we will encounter triggers so he is still a bit naughty at times but then when I put the collar on him - without using it otherwise - his behaviour improves noticably all round. The behaviour of my sister's 'poo-eater' has also been improved. We have only used it on him twice so far and didn't try it at home first, just on walks. The first walk he tried, probably 15 to 20 times to eat poo and reacted visibly when buzzed. (I haven't found the beeping affects either dog at this stage.) The last time I used the collar on that walk he spat out what he had picked up and it turned out to be a piece off a rubber ball, so we are all glad that he didn't eat that. The following walk he only made two attempts to eat poo. So again, work-in-progress but the collar does seem to be improving the 'poo-eating' situation. The set included two collars, the hand-set controller and a charging plug/lead. The instructions say that only the supplied charging equipment should be used. I have only charged the collars and hand-set up once so far and we have walked for several hours and I used the pug-collar over Christmas when we had visitors. The handset has a battery power-level indicator, which I find useful. I think the buttons on the hand-set are reasonably intuitive to use, although I just have the vibration on max as the dogs don't seem to notice it otherwise. I might try to use the beeper as the dogs start to be better behaved over time. The lights on the collars don't seem to me to be about controlling the dog as might be indicated in the product description; they are more about knowing that the collar is switched on -- and they only stay on if the handset is also powered on. Overall, I think the collars have been worth purchasing (I hesitated for months before spending the money). I am not sure yet if either dog will be fully habilitated but I am pleased with the results achieved so far.

review_title: Reasonable Price But With a Significant Drawback
review_text: I'm leaving a quick review to add my experience to the mix. About a year ago, I bought a Plantronics-style knockoff and it lasted about 8 months. As many people like to say, "I babied the headset and it just broke!!". It's true, I didn't even rotate the boom mic to the "closed" position because my original Plantronics headset broke after a year. Fast-forwarding, I was very pleased with the Plantronics replacement but the company wasn't selling them anyone and I found this model, again same profile design as the Plantronics model. Given the reviews, I decided it was wise to buy something at 1/4th the cost. However, I am disappointed. While it had an "enhanced" feature of extending the earpiece lower, the distance between the back of the headset and the speaker is MUCH smaller. It's not comfortable at all. In fact, it pinches my ear that I can't "go all day without even noticing I'm wearing it". Maybe I have big ears but I think the bend is at more of an angle. Presumably to keep it snug but it's painful so I find I only wear it when on the phone, whereas my older model with the exact same design, could be worn for 5 hours (from Dallas to Houston) without any discomfort.

I'm giving this 1 star only because it amplifies background noise to piercing levels. The reason I purchased this is for work, when I'm on a call I want to be able to multi task. Even typing at my computer has been compared to bombs dropping and I'm not heavy handed on the keyboard. This headset is useless unless you're in an absolutely quiet area. Update - I had previously been using this headset with the Samsung Galaxy 8, and it was aweful. I recently switched to the Iphone 8 and used the headset, funny because it works perfect with the Apple. I love this headset now. I wouldn't think the brand of phone would matter but it does.

review_title: Everything you need for handsfree driving
review_text: I ride a motorcycle a LOT. In my travels, I am astounded at how many people still play with their phone, or hold their phone while talking on speaker (I call it the Pop-Tart Pose - holding it horizontally). With something as simple as this earbud, you can easily chat away while driving, doing chores around the house, even while you work at your desk. - It's comfortable. Fits over the left or right ear. - It sounds great - plenty of volume (I'm half-deaf) and voice quality is wonderful. People can hear YOU without a lot of interfering background noise. - Great battery life, easy to answer and hang up without touching your phone. charges quickly using Micro-USB adapter. There are a LOT of styles - products that go from $15 all the way up through $200. While I admit the expensive earbuds have fancier software (directive noise canceling and equalization) this simple unit does 99% of the others without breaking the bank. You're not out a TON of money when your dog uses it as a chew toy. I honestly wish more drivers had one of these. Motorcycle riders would feel a bit safer.

This is the fourth bluetooth earpiece that I have used. The 3 prior have all been Plantronics, which were great units, but they just seem overpriced. This one was definitely a mix of good and bad. First, the good. Pairing was quick and easy. It only took a couple of minutes to set it up and start using it. Sound quality was generally good. I never had any issues with anybody hearing me, and to my understanding, there was minimal background noise. Sound quality on my end was good, but only if you were able to get the earpiece seated correctly. Now the bad. First, the unit is quite rigid which leads to problems getting it on and getting it to fit correctly once on. The rigidity also kept me from being able to seat the eartip correctly so I lost quite a bit of volume. But the worst part was that it was assembled incorrectly and the rotation stops were in the wrong places. In my right ear, the mic was pressed up against my cheek and there was a very uncomfortable pressure in my ear. In my left ear, it fit fine most of the time, but had a tendency to pivot away from my cheek. As far as overall comfort, if you can get it to fit correctly, it is ok. But if you can't, it can be quite uncomfortable, even painful. The Plantronics definitely fit better and were much more comfortable, but were similar on sound quality. I am going to try it for a few more days, but will likely return it. If the stops were in the right place I would probably be keeping it as I could wear it in my right ear which is my preference, but cannot currently do.

This unit never had that problem even though others (as well as my car) have. Seems to use the latest and greatest technology. The bad - If you are expecting consistent crisp sound quality because you have used other headsets before, you will be disappointed. While the sound quality is good, it's crackled and fuzzy at times. I typically test this by calling our home number and leaving a message. The fuzz made some of my words unintelligible and it sounded like a rumpling piece of wrapping paper in the background. Not consistently, but enough to make it annoying. I additionally had business associates tell me that they could hear the difference and would ask me to repeat things occasionally. - The grip on my ear is a little snug, and at the end of the day it hurts a little. I am hoping that over time this relaxes, and just for the sake of the obvious - not everyone's ears are going to be the same size. Overall it's not a bad product. It sure beats the $100+ you'll pay for a Jabra or Plantronics unit but it comes at a little bit of a cost you should probably consider if you use it for business/business travel. 2017-03-21 Update: As I said above, the customer service seemed outstanding but now I can confirm that they really are. I was contacted and asked if I would like a replacement without having asked for it. They said that the sound issues are rare, but they have seen it a few times. Sellers that pay attention to customer feedback and respond are really valuable and show they really believe and care about the quality and reputation of their product.

review_text: I purchased 2 pairs of these - one for home and one for work - so I wouldn't have to remember to throw it into my bag every day. Unfortunately, I had a consistently poor experience with each: COMFORT: I could never get these to fit comfortably. After just a few minutes, they started hurting my ear in a couple of places. I tried different size inserts, different positioning, and different ears. None of them rested well for me. I've noticed that lower-cost headsets often cause me discomfort. If you've never had a problem with headset comfort, then these may not be a problem for you. Otherwise, I can't recommend them. NOISE-CANCELING: While talking to someone else, I walked into a moderately noisy room. She immediately said that she couldn't hear me anymore. PAIRING: One reason I liked these was that I could pair them with two devices. I'm constantly having to toggle between my mobile phone and my laptop for making and receiving calls. So I followed the instructions and paired with both devices. However, I constantly get a "beep beep ... connected" message now, even when I'm on calls. I don't see others complaining about that issue, so I assume it has to do with being paired with multiple devices. So I wouldn't recommend getting these if you want to pair with 2 devices that are always in the same area at the same time. SOUND QUALITY: It may be related to the above pairing issue, but I constantly heard static in the background when using one of these headsets. Too bad - I was hoping these would work out. I'll be going back to a more expensive option.

Like most of these products, it's made of hard, non flexible plastic. So either the speaker finds your ear, or like me, it doesn't. There is a small (Very small) range of adjustment built-in, but it comes up short -literally. I have to force the speaker bud into my ear hole to hear it, where it inevitably pops back out. Here's a message to consumers and manufacturers out there. These types of items need to have a flexible section over the top of the ear, so that a greater number of wearers will find comfort and satisfaction. review_text: I've owned this bluetooth ear piece for just over 3 months and would not recommend it at all. Full disclosure, I use this headset on an office phone with bluetooth, not with a cell phone, so I don't know if that's why i'm having these problems or not. Problem #1: It has no deadening noise feature for surrounding noise. I work in an office, so when my co-worker is talking on another line, the person I am talking to can hear their conversation loud and clear. Also, things like shuffling papers and using a stapler are very loud both to my ear, and to the person I'm talking to. Problem #2: It loses its bluetooth connection at random times. Not when I'm on the phone, but if I don't make or receive a call for a while, the phone will ring in my ear, I will hit the button to answer the call, and I will get a message that says "Connected" as if it were disconnected and then will proceed to not answer the call. I then have to pick up my office phone. These problems didn't seem to happen when I purchased the product, but seem to be happening more and more. If these problems had been more prevalent earlier, I would have returned it. I would still love to return it, but sometimes you get what you pay for, and this was a very cheap headset.

Due to the issues of connectivity, I contacted Lebowex customer support and they were incredibly helpful and supportive. This receiver is very capable for such a tiny device. It powers my earphones up to high levels and it sounds good to my old ears. The controls are simple and logical. The little LED in the center button shows on, off, and connected status; that's hard to see while you're pushing the button, though, so it has voice prompts to tell you things like power on and off and when it connects. It connected quickly and easily to my phone. Once in a while it will momentarily lose contact with my phone when I change the playing track the first time, but it immediately recovers and that may be a reflection of the sometimes-sketchy Bluetooth on my 3-year old phone. The very compact design and button arrangement does affect one situation, though it's a design choice and not a fault of this useful little gadget. I have a ski helmet with headphones and I like to be able to answer my phone while on the slopes. The compact button arrangement makes it tricky to answer the phone while I am wearing ski gloves and not looking at the unit. Once connected, it works well for phone calls so I don't have to dig my phone out of my parka. I don't list to music on the slopes, so in my phone's Bluetooth settings I disabled the "media player" function for this device and that minimized accidental button pushes with gloves.

I also wanted something sturdy that wouldn't break or wear out after a few months of use. The BASEUS Phone Ring stand is just what I had in mind. It's made of sturdy, polished metal with a well-engineered look and feel. So far the base of the Phone Ring strongly adheres to the rubberized Diztronic TPU cover I keep on my Note 4. I was concerned that my Note 4 with the Phone Ring attached would not easily fit in the Bomea pouch case I use, but the Phone Ring adds only about 1/8" to the thickness of the phone and cover, so it easily fits in the pouch case and is also easy to pull out of the case. Update 7/8/17 I've been using this for about a week now. When I first wrote my review I had only checked that the ring/metal stuck to my car mount, but I hadn't tried I after it was installed because I wanted to give the adhesive time to set. This has to be one of the worst design flaws I've seen. As far as a ring/stand for your phone, it's perfect. It even rotates which happens to be the downfall. The reason I purchased this was because it's advertised that it can be used with your car mount. The point of a magnetic car mount is that you don't have to have something that holds the phone in place by grabbing it, you can just toss it on there and it sticks. Not this. Because it rotates the phone will not stay straight on the mount at all. Every time you make a turn, the phone flips around in a circle. It's quite annoying and could be fixed by having a "lock" or something on the ring. I gave 2 stars because the ring comes in handy as long as I'm not driving. I thought it might loosen with a bit of use, but 4 days after installing, if anything, it's worse than it was at first. The tape is still very sticky, and so long as I don't try and open the ring, it still sticks to my phone, but the force required to use the ring is more than the tape can handle, and off it comes. Amazon won't let me return it, so I guess I should have just bought another one in the store. At least I could take it back if it didn't work. One other complaint: This is much "fatter" than the specs indicated. Maybe the ring itself is technically only 3mm, but it sticks off of the phone more like 5mm. Doesn't sound like much, but when phones are only 7-8mm thick to begin with, a 2mm difference feels huge. Phone doesn't fit in my car cradle with this ring attached.

As somebody who considers himself a techie, a gamer, and a gadget-lover, I'm a little embarrassed to admit that until now, I haven't had any experience into the world of VR, despite having been really interested in it for some time. I recently experienced a full VR gaming experience at a neighbor's home, and was blown away by how far gaming technology has come. He recommended I "dip my feet in the water" with an inexpensive Google Cardboard-style headset, that uses a mobile phone as a dedicated screen. So I found this headset, and it seemed to have everything I would have expected in a VR headset. I downloaded some VR apps, loaded my phone into the unit, and started tinkering. I was really surprised at how quickly time vanished. I spent a few hours playing games, watching videos, and exploring curated VR content. A lot of VR apps actually come with a built in QR code scanner, which you can use to scan the QR code on the handbook that comes with the device, and it will automatically configure the app's settings to give an optimal view, which is really nice. As far as actual product specifics, the device was comfortable, and I was able to wear it for several hours without really thinking about it. The headphones use a standard headphone jack, which my iPhone 7 Plus doesn't support, but I was able to use a lightning adapter, and it worked just fine. review_title: Lots of Features Packed With Great Price

It thus sometimes get into the way of the headset and the eye padding. The eye padding gets loose twice because of this, though it's pretty easy to push them back in place. A few tips: * Make sure you clean you phone screen well. I thought my headset lens is bad cause it shows a big black dot when I first tried. It turns out to be my dirty phone screen. * You need to find those SBS (Side By Side) videos. review_text: I am always looking for new bluetooth headphones since they seem to be getting better all the time. The included grip cover prevents the headphones from falling out from the weight of the control board. Don't get me wrong you still feel the weight of the board but I was quickly able to adapt to it and no longer notice the weight. The sound quality was really nice and was able to play music from 3 rooms away before experiencing poor connection. The battery was also able to last me most of the day with normal use. Another downside is that I found the power led to be too bright. I would have rather not having the led flashing every couple of seconds. I ended up placing a small piece of electrical tape over it. I have come to like this headphone despite its flaws. I’m not sure if it’s for everyone but I would suggest giving it a try, just remember amazon has a return service.

This is an entirely different form factor from other ear bud options, but it is one that still certainly has its benefits. And while many will find the retractable cord design cumbersome, some will appreciate the around the neck style, and the novelty of the retractable earbuds. The somewhat flexible band stays snugly around your neck, and you can simply retract the buds back into the unit when not in use, which allows you to turn them on and off quickly. One downside to this is that the earpiece wire is very thin, and can be damaged easily.This is surely a best sounding series, offering both aptX codec support and a Harman Kardon branded Signature Sound. The audio is well-rounded with a solid bass sound, but all in all does lack the clarity of high-end headphones.For average listening, it will be just fine, as content still sounds clear and balanced and there are EQ settings to help dial in the ideal sound. Because the headphones only include two sets of ear tips, it can be a bit harder to get the proper seal for a good sound. The controls are well-spaced and easy to access, and some have extra uses that can be quite handy. For instance, the speakerphone call button allows you to use services like Siri, Google Now, or Cortana to make a call without getting your phone out. The Tone & Talk Android app can even read you text messages, making this a useful device in the office. Combine all of this with a 14 hour battery life and you have a truly versatile pair of headphones. They would certainly be a better value if they were more waterproof, but considering that you can get them for under $100, these earbuds are definitely a viable option for portable audio. Pros: 14 hour battery life Tone & Talk app can make phone calls and messages Cons: Earphone wire is dangerously thin Not waterproof

Bluetooth headphones are awesome things to have. This allows you to listen to audio from your phone or other bluetooth capable device without having to worry about wires tethered to your device. This way, you can do things such as housework or working out at the gym without having to have a wire that could get tangled up or snagged on something, causing you to drop your phone or damage your headphones. I typically listen to things with only one earbud in so that I can hear what's going on around me. For that reason, I really like that these have retractable wires on the buds on both sides, so when I'm not using one, it stays neatly up close to the base. Also, the sides of the unit fold down for easy storage. I also like that these charge using a the industry standard micro-USB cable. I have tons of these around in car chargers and in multi-port chargers that I have in multiple rooms of my house plus on my desk at work. That way I'm always able to charge these when I need to, without having to carry around a special cord for charging. However, charging isn't that big of a deal because I've been very surprised about the battery life I get from this unit. Typically, units like this will only get about 4 hours of battery life on a single charge, but I've managed to get over 8 hours out of the package without even having to charge the first time.

We got this bluetooth headset for my son who loves the Apple EarPods (wired) for compact size to take to school for his down time, but wanted a set of bluetooth headset. My initial impression was how this could sound good, looking like a knock-off of EarPods. I test every thing we buy. And while I personally dislike the Apple's EarPods for it's shape not staying in my ears, this Bluetooth headset came with the silicone adapter to keep the ear piece in the ear just right. The fit and quality is pretty nice, the center remote control body has shiny clear coat to the touch and doesn't feel cheapie made like some of the other headphones I have had in the past. I felt that the remote control body is a bit on the heavy side so it may bounce around if you intend to use this for running. But, it comes with a clip to secure the cable near this remote control body on your collar to help secure it. The cables that connect the 2 ear pieces and remote control unit is the popular white rubber jacket flat cable. It comes with intuitive instruction manual in English(!), though, it is very easy to use, even a 5year-old could easily figure out the 3 buttons with multi functions. Compared to the Apple EarPods, the only thing that is missing is the silicone cover where the wire goes into the earpiece. Sound quality is subjective, but based on my experience, this is surprisingly well. With any earphones with small size speaker drivers, you tend to lose the base. And while this Bluetooth headset is in no exception to the rule, I was amazed by the amicable balance of high frequency and base. It's not Beats. But for this tiny earpiece, it has a very good sound. When you pause the music, there is no hissing (electrical) noise, typical to economical headsets out there. I then tested the mic by calling via my iPhone. The person on the other side of the call said it sounded very clearly. I was talking right next to my TV with basketball game going on so it was rather noisy. But the other side of the call did not hear any noise that would interfere the conversation. So it has some level of noise cancelling feature I came to like so much. I have not tested the battery life but the manual claims 3 hours of music listening. From the size of the remote control body that houses the rechargeable battery, I thought it would be a bit longer than that. Stand-by time however, is an impressive 100hours, and 3.5 hours of talk time. I have not tested the recharging time either, but from my experience with other bluetooth headsets, I expect it to be very subtle. Overall, the quality level of fit and sound, this is a very good headset which is a nice and rare bargain to this price range headphone, I might steal it from my son, or get another set for myself.

review_title: Nice little BT earphone with some advanced features
review_text: This is the first of its kind in the Bluetooth earphone product that offers truly handsfree voice command on incoming calls. When a call comes in you can either answer answer yes or no and the call will go through or go to voicemail automatically which is nice feature. The headphone build quality is very good. The box contains the Micro USB cable and two sets of extra earpads for different fitting requirements, and a clip to tie the headphone wire to your shirt, etc. There are 3 buttons on the control pod including volume up, down, and a multi-function button. The microphone is located on the bottom of the control unit (through a tiny circular hole). Pairing was easy and quick. The range was good (probably due to Bluetooth 4.1). The earpod has an opening that allows a little extra bass to pass through. In term of audio quality, it's very good from a cost standpoint. Bass was good and the high sounds were crisp. In terms of general usability, note that this does NOT have an over-the-ear clip (like some other offering) so it will not stay put as tight if you're doing some strenuous exercises... but the benefit is your ear lobe does not hurt in extended listening. Secondly, I think the control unit is a little too close to the earpiece and the weight can drag it down a little (if it's in hanging position). The cable has a certain stiffness (or flex) in it so it cannot be bent easily which is good. This headphone is less expensive than the name brand ones so it would be unfair to compare between those. All in all, this is a nice design, good quality, excellent sound, and true handsfree communication capabilities. One thing that would be nice to include would be a small carrying case to store the charging cable and the ear buds.

The charge on these has been decent too, I used them for 3 days without having to charge them up. The battery was about halfway empty when I charged them up for the first time. A charging cord is included in the box. I was very impressed by these headphones, I am making the switch from my Apple ones to these to go cordless.

i purchased these headphones for my husband, as he had a pair that recently stopped working. Here is his review: Overall I like the look and fit of these headphones. They are well packaged and contain a nice case for storage. They pair easily to my iPhone7 and iWatch 2nd gen. Unfortunately, they can only pair to one device at at time, so in order to switch from the phone to the watch, or vice versa, it requires me to go into the other device and click "forget" on the headphones, then power cycle the headphones and repair. It doesn't take long, but it's an added step in comparison to other Bluetooth headphones I've owned that can pair to multiple devices at a time. The headphones are quite loud and very clear. Sounds of various ranges/pitches play well. The battery life is great. I've been able to work in the yard for several hours while streaming at medium volume without running the battery dead. I was also able to go for a 12 mile run after a full charge streaming podcasts without a low battery warning. The biggest con I have is wind noise. While running outdoors into a steady breeze the wind noise in the headphones made the podcast I was listening to was completely drowned out. This could potentially be remedied by wearing bigger ear pieces, but I was wearing the most comfortable of the three options that came with the headphones when I battled the wind noise. Overall, I'd recommend these headphones for someone looking for an entry level Bluetooth model. Pros: Comfort Volume/clarity Battery life Cons: Wind noise Pairs to only one device

review_title: INNLIFE makes a "Wonderful noise" with these Bluetooth ear pieces!
review_text: Great Bluetooth earpieces that deliver excellent, crisp sound. These look & feel identical to the Apple wired ear pieces provided with the iPhones. INNLIFE has included an adjustable clip on the left side of the ear piece which can slide up or down to suit your preference. Clip keeps these firmly in place & also helps keep them from falling to the ground if they should slip out of your ears for whatever reason. Comes with a one foot charging cord (USB connection for the charging needed), directions (needed a magnifying glass to read, but once that was done, directions easy & straight forward to follow), extra ear bud pads to fit your comfort, and the Bluetooth Earpieces. They call this a headphone, but my old fashioned self thinks of headphones as the bulky set you put over your head and has the padded cups that fit over your ears. Those are another category than these. The setup is simple & paired quickly with my iPhone 7. Full charge took about 45 minutes but I suspect a bit longer for next charge as this was my initial charge straight from the box. It likely had a small charge already on it which lessened the initial charging time. Play time on one charge is yet to be determined as I'm still using the initial charge. Will update if the play time is different than seller's description. The volume level is excellent if you like your music loud. One exception was using these for trying to relax at night. The lowest volume setting was still a tad too loud. Would like to have one click lower to be 'just right," Overall, this is a super item and an excellent buy for the price! I purchased these without any discount or free offers. (How do so many people get those free items?) Please click yes or no if this review was helpful. Thank you!

First off let me just say the sound is great on these. They sound crystal clear and not tinny like some others I have owned in this price range. They come with little rubber sleeves to go over the earpieces. I find the covers help them stay in your ear and are more comfortable so that’s how I use them. As far as Bluetooth goes they come with as much features as you are probably used to. The main button controls a lot of functions like answering a call, summoning Siri, play pause music, and making or ignoring calls. You can navigate your songs with the volume buttons. Overall this is a great Bluetooth headset and for the price I don’t have to worry about damaging it during workouts.

review_title: Battery life is excellent. The Bluetooth signal strength/clarity are fantastic
review_text: I purchased these headphones to wear during workouts and outdoor excursions. The build quality is solid. Battery life is excellent. The Bluetooth signal strength/clarity are fantastic, easily beating my much pricier LG HBS-1100 set that I use for work. The sound quality is good, but a bit lacking in bass. One concern is the earbud size, they are on the larger side of earbuds that I have used. While they work well in my ears, my wife could not get them to seat properly in hers.

review_title: Great wireless headphones! Worth the price.. Doesn't fall out!
review_text: Everyone else in my household has Apple AirPods, and I personally didn't want to spend that kind of money on headphones. I figured I give these a try because they look similar to the original design of Apple heaphones. They stay perfectly in my ears, and I don't have to adjust them. It comes with a clip to hook onto your shirt which makes all the difference. The clip is strong, so you don't have worry about the headphones flying out of your ears and dropping to the floor. It has a control panel that allows you to turn it on and sync and turn the volume higher or lower. When you receive a phone call a female voice tells you the number of who's calling.The only issue I have with these is that once I received a phone call it kept disconnecting from the headphones and switching to my phone.

review_title: If you like Apple earbuds, this is the bargain Bluetooth headset for you.
review_text: Wow. These are actually good! I’ve never said that about any Bluetooth headset ever. I was attracted to these because of the similarity to the new style Apple earbuds that came with my IPhone 8 Plus. I’m impressed by the comfort and audio quality, especially in phone calls in comparison to the wired buds that came with the phone. Keeping them in place without the included silicone earpieces is an excercize in futility. They are similar to, but not exactly identical to the Apple earbuds. They’re a little tiniest bit thicker. It makes them not stay in as good. For audio quality, I added the silicone earpiece adapter things. It comes with two sets, which is great because they enhance the function of the Apple headset as well. Keeps them in place better and improves audio. Audio is definitely better on the wired headphones, but the audio of this $20 Bluetooth is pretty passable. There’s bass, but not as much. There’s treble, but there’s a lot of it. These work great for phone calls while doing housework, deskwork or driving. They’re adequate for listening to music. I’ve never been happier with a Bluetooth headset in 10 years of owning every other primitive generation of Bt headsets.

review_title: This one is the BEST one I have had
review_text: INNLIFE Wireless Headphones V4.1 Stereo Earphones Noise Cancelling Earbuds is my fifth Bluetooth earbuds. This one is the BEST one I have had. Design: Resembles me of another famous brand earbud because they both look almost same. Overall, these earbuds are awesome, you can use them while doing hiking, cycling, exercising, walking, working, studying ,etc. Anywhere!!

review_title: FINALY! Good wireless headphones at an affordable price.
review_text: I've been through a few different style headsets and if you have an iphone and are used to these earbuds...they are the best! They fit just like the iphone standard ones, but also come with clear/opaque earcovers (which helps keep the buds clean). The sound is great! So far the best of all the lower priced earbuds out there. The only reason these didn't get 5 stars is that the control piece is a little bigger than most brands out there and the battery only lasts about 3 - 3.5 hours. For such a bulky piece, seems like they can have a better battery inside. I might buy a second pair because I'm so happy I found a pair that fit AND have good sound.

review_title: I was really impressed at first , BUTT THEN...
review_text: I purchased these as a gift, i received a pretty good price and they seemed to be a quality item. the person i gave them to really liked the design and the sound quality, i also tried them out and the comfort , sound quality, and battery life are impressive BUT THERE IS A PROBLEM the person i gifted them to has been using them regularly and the plastic or outer surface of the plastic is peeling off and leaving black residue on his skin. My son broke my designer earphones and my life has not been the same since 😕 however, I don’t have 100+ to drop on big brand right now. I’ve been trying a whole lot of Bluetooth earphones lately and these are the best! Pros- -“pod” design of earphone, it just works! These beat any other design by miles. The pod is somewhat conical shaped so fits well in pretty much any ear canal. They sit well and stay in, and beat out custom sized inserts, premium foams, etc. and you don’t even feel ‘em. -building on the previous comment, I love that these stay put throughout vigorous exercise and running. They stay in and need minimum adjustment. -although not super-premium sound, they sound great for the price point! -intuitive and easily accessed controls -great talk /listen time at 7-8 hours for me. These earbuds are made to look a lot like the Apple earpods. What I like about them is that they include a plastic piece that can go over the bud and helps it stay in your ear. The regular earpods from Apple won't stay in my ear well, but this set with it's added piece stays in with no problem. Also, there is a plastic clip on the line which will let it clip to your shirt. I bought this headset for my wife who runs all the time but using it now myself most of the time. These are my new workout ear phones. They come with silicone earbud covers that hold them in securely. A clip on the cord holds them securely to your shirt in the event both earbuds fall out together. After initial setup, they connect very quickly. Turn them on and they connect within 2 seconds. review_title: if not better than the typical apple earpods that usually come in ...
review_text: These pair of earbuds are very decent for the price. The pairing process is very simple and intuitive. This pair comes with three different buttons with a load of functionalities.First off you can control the volume using the volume buttons, and you can use the multi-functional button to power on and power off the device, as well as make phone calls! I would really recommend these to anyone looking for a reliable pair of earbuds for use in or outside the GYM, or even for any sports related activity for that matter. The sound coming out of these is very clear, although I would have loved a little more power behind the bass.

UPDATE: After a little over 3 months of using them, they stopped working. I was in the middle of my workout and the song I was listening to started breaking up. A moment later the song just stopped. I tried turning the earbuds off and back on, but nothing. There wasn't an issue with the bluetooth connection or the battery. They are broken. I didn't expect to get a lifetime of use out of them, but I did expect more than 3 months. Very disappointed. Initial Review: They work very well and are good quality. My only issue is the little control box thingy is heavy (relative to the bud) and will cause my bud to fall out when I'm working out. review_title: I love music and headphones are my reprieve from background "noise" ...
review_text: Updated review: downgrade to 3 stars. After using for a short period, maybe 30 hours total, the headset constantly interrupts music as if you were pressing the home button on iPhone to engage Siri - which I am not. I have even disabled Siri, but the headset still plays about 10-15 seconds, then beep-beep, silence and after about 7 seconds, returns to the music, already in progress. This obviously makes them completely unusable. I have found that turning them off-on usually fixes the issue for a time, but it is annoying. Original review: 5 stars I just received this item, so this review is based on my initial impression. I will update over time if my opinion changes. For context, let me say that in general, if you see me day or night, I will have headphones on. I love music and headphones are my reprieve from background "noise" like airport crowds, crying babies, chatty passengers in the next seat over, and mundane political discussions in public places. :-) I have bought and used most of the $100+ brands at one time or another, including Bose, Beatsx, Tone LG Ultimate, etc., but I purchased these on a lightning deal, specifically to see if Bluetooth speaker technology has become mainstream enough for cheap-chinese-knock-offs to be "good" - and you know what? They ARE! The sound quality is comparable to the LG Tone, and better than the BeatsX (of which I am not a fan). The Bluetooth range is the same as the other brands, about 35 ft inside the house. the battery life is good, I have had them powered on for the past 15-hours between listening and standby mode, with about 5 hours of play time. Pairing to my iPhone7 was easy. The around-the-neck-fit is not as comfortable or natural as the LG Tone, but comparable with the BeatsX. The ear-fit is exactly the same as apple's ear-pods, or air-pods. The volume range is loud enough that in normal listening, I find max volume too loud, which is not true of the BeatsX. I wouldn't call these premium headphones, clearly, but I gave 5-stars because of the fact that you could buy 4, or maybe 5 pairs of these for the price of the BeatsX and the are equal or better in every regard - so I would say these are a tremendous value, and pretty decent headphones for everyday use at a price-point that is affordable by just about everyone.

I transcribe for a living and wanted something cordless so I wasn't being constantly tied down to the computer if I needed to walk away for a second. These are exactly what I needed. They were easy to connect to my PC and I can switch between it and my phone with ease, I even figured out how to connect both at the same time weirdly enough. It was more noticeable when I dropped below 9 minutes per mile or during speed workouts. However, for the price this is not a concern. Previously, I ran with $150 Beats X. The Beats are definitely a better product, BUT not $130 better. Therefore, I'd recommend this product. You have to use the clip when running if you don't want the cord to bounce as much. This took some getting used to but it works well. Highly recommend.
