review_title: Good value but bass-happy and odd controls
review_text: Summary: Functional and inexpensive. Works to make calls. Retractors and folding features are nice. Helpful and responsive customer service. But... sound is all boom with minimal midrange or treble. Buttons and feedback all minimal design. Compared to the LG Tone Pro, these come up far short. A few details: I'm a semi-pro vocalist and guitarist. I've been making music my whole life. For $34 I didn't expect perfection. I have LG Tone Pro HBS770 that I enjoy, but often misplace. Thought these might be a suitable spare for a bit less $$, and the retracting and folding features seemed nice improvements. First impression was that these are huge (more than double volume and weight of LGs). Looked like something out of 50s sci fi movie. Retractors work fine, though instructions warn you must gently guide buds into docks with your hands for longer life. Folding feature is nice to save space. Buds fit my ears fine with stock tips, making good comfortable seal. But the sound is oppressive. No, I don't mean impressive. Boomy bass is it. Maybe OK for head-banger rock, but for acoustic, orchestral, jazz or vocals this is not the droid I was looking for. Very low score for musical accuracy or enjoyment for what I like to listen to. Controls are minimal with exactly three buttons: +, -, and Phone. Eventually you might get used to the long-press and multi-taps needed for common functions, but I prefer a few more controls, like individual volume up/down, track up/down, and pause. Voice prompts clear enough, but no battery level spoken or visible. May tell you when battery gets low, but I can't listen that long. Mid- and higher-frequencies are so muddy, it throws off balance and ability to pick out individual instruments. Imaging inconsistent. Seal, Kiss From a Rose sounds like totally different song, and not for the better. So... if you like bass, bass, and more bass, and higher volume than other headsets for same level setting, don't mind missing mids and distorted treble, you may like this. I don't.

I bought this pair because I lost my wired iPhone 7 headset, so I decided to take the plunge and get the AirPods, but apparently they were impossible to find. These are decent for the price, but I have my complaints. Pros Good battery life. While I haven't timed a full charge to compare with the advertised Fast charging Can charge and use simultaneously Cons Not super-comfortable. If you put the cord around the back of your neck, it pulls the buds back at an awkward angle that causes discomfort, so I usually wear them with the cored dangling down in front of my. However, this isn't a perfect solution. For one, it's a little annoying having the cord dangling. Two, the batter/control module is located on the right side, causing extra pull on my right ear, and that also causes discomfort. For prolonged usage, I end up having to switch back and forth between positions to stave of discomfort. Mind you it's not agonizing; it's just annoying. I've never had great luck with Bluetooth devices and reliability concerning connections. Granted, I've only had experience with a few devices, but they're connectivity seems a little random. Like, it sometimes connects automatically when I don't want them to, and not connect when I want them to. This one is no different. So it's usually a necessity to be fiddling around in the Bluetooth settings whenever I use the headset. I sometimes have issues whole talking on the phone. It cuts in and out occasionally. It's not frequent enough for serious concern, but it's annoying when it happens. Although, it doesn't happen as frequently with my phone as my laptop. The weight imbalance of the set (the battery and controls being on one side) makes it so they don't reliably stay around my neck when not in use, so I have to stick them in my pocket if I want to take them with me. Lastly, there are little LEDs on the battery to indicate certain functions. Like when it's turning on/off, connecting and charging. That's all fine, but it periodically blinks when in use, and it's quite bright. I don't notice it most of the time, but if I'm laying in bed at night it's really annoying. I can't imagine why this would be a feature. I guess so that you can see if it's on at a glance, but for one, you have to look at it for sever seconds in order to determine that, and there's no reason why it has to be so bright. It could have been a steady-on dim light. Two, they could have simply had an auto shutoff function after a few minutes of no use or something. I don't understand. Final notes While I'm no audiophile, the sound doesn't seem terrible, but it's noticeably worse than the Apple earphones. It's totally fine for podcasts/audiobooks (which is mostly what I listen to), but music sound seems to be lacking. Overall, they're not bad for the price, and they serve my needs until I can get something better. My advice would be to spend a few extra dollars on something else if you want a quality headset. I gave three stars instead of two because of the low price. Had I paid much more, it would have received a lower rating. Ultimately, it's functional and inexpensive, so if that's all you're looking for, then by all means.

review_title: Feature count and style over sound quality.
review_text: Quite a snazzy-looking set. The LEDs are a nice touch. In-line microphone enable/disable and volume control is nice, and the chunkiness of the control module is great for when I'm sitting at my computer - very easy to grab without looking. The length of the cord is perfect. The sound isolation is great - my girlfriend is watching Harry Potter 6 feet away and I can barely hear it. I haven't tested the microphone yet, but when I played a few songs through the speakers, it was like hearing them through a thick towel. I'm not sure whether this is just the quality of the speakers, or maybe the padding, but typically even an extended burn-in period doesn't help when the speakers are this "fuzzy". I have tested 30+ sets of earbuds, on-ear and over-ear headsets, and this sound quality is easily in the bottom 5. There is no bass. There is no crisp treble. The midrange is staticky instead of smooth and strong. Adjusting the volume higher exacerbates these problems instead of hiding them. Still, I tend to spend quite a lot of money on headphones. Comparing these to my $150 set of Audio-Technica ATH-M50x is not a fair comparison. For the $25 price tag, it's actually not a bad set. Definitely a feature quantity-over-quality set, but still not bad. If the audio were even just a little bit crisper at the top end, I'd give it a full 5 - even ignoring the lack of bass and midrange clarity.

review_title: Best gaming headset for the price!

They fit comfortably on my somewhat small head. I thought they were plastic but was pleasantly surprised when I the sides had metal on the inside. The headset feels stable and doesn't move at all when it's on my head. Even when I dance and listen to music this headset stays on my head pretty well! The blue LED lights are not super bright but give off a nice futuristic looking glow. What I loved most were the plugs that this headphone had. It'll basically work on any platform. It came with a normal USB connection, PC audio in/audio out (red+green) plug. It also came with a converter so you can use these with your phone or any other device that has a standard 3.5mm audio jack. Everything except an Iphone 7. I tried it with my Samsung phone and it worked really well just like any other headphones would! The mic is good and it transmits my voice clearly (according to my teammates). It's very comparable to my Plantronics headset. Very clear and it really helped decrease any background noises like typing. What was also nice was the ability to 'flip' my mic up and out of my face so I could use the headset without having a mic in my face always. Overall I'm really glad I purchased these. I think I'll keep using them even after I get my normal Plantronics back just because they fit my head so much better and feel much more comfortable. At less than $30 this is the best thing I've bought all year!

review_title: New twist and functionality to the selfie stick!
review_text: We all have selfie sticks and they're pretty straight forward. This new version of the selfie stick adds a lot more functionality. First of all, this came very well packaged and certainly can be given as a gift. It has a nice carrying case as well. Ok, so what sets this selfie stick apart from the others? It certainly feels solid and not flimsy. The spring is tight and your phone won't fall out, nor will the angle of the bracket change (it's pretty tight) The best part is the base of the selfie stick also turns it into a tripod! Sometimes you want to get a shot and the selfie stick isn't long enough, or you want to get more of your body in the shot other than your face. With the detachable bluetooth remote (which conveniently clicks back into the selfie stick), you can set the tripod up, click the remote, and you have a picture that no other selfie stick is able to capture. The remote is rechargeable with a standard micro USB port and it comes with a charging cable.

This is a great product that is steady and portable if you're just looking for a good simple to use selfie stick. Here are some points to keep in mind: 1. The bottom of the stick where you hold can expand out to make it a mini tripod. It should not be assumed that this is the perfect tripod you can use. The higher you extend the stick the more unsteady it will become. The big positive is having that expandable/collapsable in a good selfie stick as this would enable you to take great videos such as personal interviews and some great photos IF the stick is placed on a table with minimum extension to the stick itself. 2. Portable and compact. This can literally fit in a regular men's jeans pocket. So compact like a small flashlight. 3. The extension pole/boom is one of the best I have seen in the compact line. Smooth expand/collapse motion. The phone mount is steady and does NOT slip like many selfie stick Ive seen. 4. Very important to know that you can charge the battery of that allows to power the bluetooth. You can easily locate the battery clip by looking at the blue power light. Hold the button down till the blue light is off. Then with your thumb held down just push that upward (that is the battery clip compartment) till it slides up just a bit then you can pull it out slowly. DONT OPEN THE CLIP as the battery may fall out. Locate one end of the clip where the port Is locate. That is the charge port where you plug in the charger cord. I don't recommend to charge it all the time unless the blue light is low and that you will take a long trip without charging. 5. Perhaps my only disappointment with this product its not its performance and overall usability BUT just that I WISH THE PHONE MOUNT/CLIP is one that you and twist and dismount from the stick so you can screw it on a regular heavy duty tripod made for cameras and video cams. I missed checking that part before the purchase. I needed an easy selfie with good performance with a clip that I can dismount and mount it on my heavy duty tripod. I ended up going to Target to buy another selfie stick with that versatility. I compared the two and this Hummix product scores high in my scale minus that dismount ability. So If you're looking for quick, reliable bluetooth, on the go stick this is a great buy.

It does have its good and bad points, but for my uses it's almost perfect and I am soooooooooo relieved not to have to sort through the morass of tripods and such. I have an EYN (Everything You Need) case on my cell. It's thick, having a compartment on it. I have to remove it from the case to use with my tripod, and I hate that. I love the case, I've had it for 3 phones about 5 years, and I don't want to wear it out taking it on and off. This unit's phone holder holds my phone WITH the case on. Securely and carefully. I had sworn I’d never own a selfie stick, but this thing made me change my mind – somewhat. That is mostly because it combines selfie-stick with rudimentary functionalities of an old-fashioned tripod and a remote controlled camera (not included, of course). First you need to find the remote control. As there are no instructions whatsoever I thought for a while I was missing it. But it finally dawned on me that it was hidden snuggled up in the handle piece of the thingamajig. Even with that hint it might take you a bit to find it. It’s that little piece that has the name of the maker (Humixx) on it. It slides out. After you charge it, go to town on the stick. It’s a bit more solid than some might have you think – though the tripod is awfully small. The handle folds outwards into three legs. It probably can accommodate a wide range of cameras and phones. It even comes with a gray nylon carrying case. Not bad.

Having the remote attach to the tripod is the best feature this stick has going for it. It works well and is priced just a bit higher than similar items. The remote pairs quickly to my iPhone X. I then can attach my X relatively easy to the clamp-just a little tight but the spring on the clamp is built well so far. It pivots for both landscape and portrait shots and the tripod is rigid not overly flexible-a good thing. When not in use, the top of the tripod folds over the bottom, making it portable and easy to transport. This tripod is not built for a heavy small camera. I have a Sony RX 100VI and its size makes it work well for the selfie stick, but the legs on the tripod need to be extended just right for the tripod to safely balance the camera.

Let's set some realistic expectations about this Monocular. #1 The accessories (tripod and phone holder) are of very cheap build quality. You will be nervous about over tightening things. They're plastic and thin metal. Using the tripod on a height setting other than the lowest setting when your phone is in landscape will require you to use a step for the flexible phone tripod. I used a scrape piece of 2x4. #2 The instructions are written so if you are a visual learner you will need to refer to the pictures from Amazon on how to assemble, but everything is pretty straightforward. #3 If you've never used a magnified tool before, keep in mind all of your movements will also be magnified. 1cm here is a foot there. Move slow, and make minute adjustments. Your FOV (field of view) will be restricted. #4 The surfer I snapped was at most 200 yards away, and I used my phone's digital magnification to aid in getting a better image. #5 You will LOVE the remote. Once you set the lens to where you want to shoot you will get some great shots. Pairing the remote is as simple as any other bluetooth item. #6 This is NOT a mid range or even high-entry level optic. Its bottom of the barrel, but worth the money if you want to get your feet wet and learn basic settings and techniques for long range photography. This is going in my hiking back and I am spending more money on a higher level optic. Bottom Line: if you're on the fence, buy it. The remote alone is worth $10 or so and you can bring it with you if you upgrade optics.

review_title: Very versatile but you need a separate power supply
review_text: It's a little misleading to call this device a 'charging hub' although it does have charging capabilities. I'll explain later. The packaging for this item was very nice, in fact very clever and not at all wasteful. The box contains the hub and a soft carrying case, in which the hub fits very tightly indeed. There is a pencil-holder sort of tube on the side of the pouch. I guess you put the cord in there but it's not so clear. In any event, you plug this into the USB-C port of your tablet, phone, what-have-you. The hub provides 3 USB 3.0 ports, for things such as a keyboard, mouse, thumb drive, etc. There is one USB-C port which I haven't found a use for. There is also a functional HDMI port, and slots for both SD and micro-SD cards. All of these work as expected, making the hub remarkably versatile. There is also an ethernet port. Your mileage will vary here; some devices work with this and some don't. I've not been able to get it to work on either my Pixel XL or my ASUS tablet, but that's not the hub's fault. And ... there is a 2 amp USB 3.0 charging port. However, the poorly-written instruction sheet tells you to "promise" to connect AC power in the USB C port intended for that purpose. You need to supply your own cable and power source (your phone charger will do fine for this). In fact, there's a limit to how much power you can (or should, or want to) draw from your tablet or phone, so if you're going to use many peripherals at the same time, especially hungry ones, you'll need external power (and at some point you'll face bandwidth limitations). I'll give this four stars for versatility in a compact, lightweight, and highly portable package. One star off for the need to provide your own power source.

review_title: Works great but a little larger and heavier than some
review_text: I've recently evaluated half a dozen USB-C / Thunderbolt "docks" or "hubs" or "dongles" (whatever you want to call them), across almost as many brands. And while I've never heard of this brand or used its products before, it seems of high quality and worked perfectly. • It has a fairly thick and stiff USC-C cable built in that’s about 6" long • It has a small form factor (about 4.3"L x 2.25"W x 0.6"H), and solid and precise full aluminum construction and all the ports are well labeled (engraved). • All the ports work as one would expect, at the speeds one would expect, and no additional drivers were required to get it to work on the two machines I tried it on (Lenovo Yoga C930 and Microsoft Surface Go) • It has a great set of ports (particularly for its size) - The main USB-C built in cable, a USB-C power delivery port that lets you connect a charger while using your device), 3 USB-A 3.0 ports, 1 HDMI 1.2 port (up to 4K @ 30hz), High speed Ethernet port, and SD and Micro SD card slots. The only slightly negative things are its not the smallest, or lightest, and the HDMI port is only 1.2 and not 2.0 so you can't drive a 4K monitor at 60hz. That said, all of the portable docks I've tried that had an HDMI port shared that issue. Only ones that included a display port would drive 4K @ 60, and then (likely because of bandwidth issues) that dropped the USB-A ports down to 2.0 So this is a solid option, and a good buy, but there are smaller and lighter options out there at a similar price point.

review_title: A life-saver, especially if you have a MacBook laptop
review_text: At the place where I work, every four years we are provided a new computer. For the past 8 years I've used an Apple iMac. However, due to policy changes, that version was no longer available, so this time I was provided a MacBook laptop. I thought this would work just fine, but once I had it in hand I knew I had a problem. The MacBook comes with only 2 Type-C ports and that's it. What was Apple thinking!? There are no USB ports, etc. So, I had to figure out a way to connect a network cable, external monitor, external hard drive, charging cable, and scanner to this device using only two ports. Thank the Maker for the Humixx 9-in-1 hub!!!!! After attaching all of those cables to the port, which uses only one of the laptop's two Type-C ports, I still have one available Type-C port on my computer, plus a charging USB port on the dock, plus two data card ports. I LOVE it! Enough said. 5 stars!!!!

I seem to be accumulating a fair number of USB-C hubs due to the number of MacBooks I have in the house, and I'm currently loving the Vava USB-C hub that's an 8 in 1 (this Humiix hub has an extra USB 3.0 port) but supports Power Delivery, which is something that this one doesn't. They are priced the same, and function exactly the same (I had no problems connecting this and pushing out 4k to the TV, nor did it choke when I plugged it into the home router.) It got a little warm when plugged in, but it's the same as every other USB-C hub. Overall this is a great hub, although it feels like there's way too many of them to make a definitive judgement as to the best on the market. Power Delivery is something to look for, but only if you plan on plugging in your power adapter into the hub instead of another port on the computer. It's priced competitively at $62.

I'm using this on a 2018 MacBook Pro (TouchBar model). It's working just fine for me so far. I've used an SD card with it, and right now I have my HDMI monitor plugged in and it also works fine. I also use a USB mouse on this hub, and that's working well. It is truly 'plug and play' - there was no setting up at all. It worked the second I plugged it in. You can plug your power cord into this hub, and it will charge the battery of your laptop. However, I don't plug power into since I'd rather have the Apple charger go directly to my MacBookPro. Finally, it does get a little warm when using, but nothing that I'm concerned about. My only complaint is very minor: the case that comes with it is such a tight fit that it's a pain to put it in. review_title: Works, but thawing time is nearly double of higher-quality trays.
review_text: I previously purchased a similar tray from VonShef, which unfortunately during a trip it got banged up, and some of powder coating chipped off. When I went to buy a new one, they were out of stock, so I found this one. It looked good, and almost identical in size and design. But honestly, by far not even close. First, you have to understand that a heat-sync (the property that makes these things work) only works when it can make the sync itself work. It works by being able to utilize the room-temperature air to keep the tray warmer than the expanding cold from the food sitting on it. Thereby, causing a rapid, exponential thawing effect. In order to have the heat sync work, it must have as much tray hitting room-temperature air as the item it's thawing. Because of this, if the grooves in your tray are not deep enough, you will thaw much, much slower. Compared to other trays I have seen, the grooves in this tray are very shallow. While it did work, when I put it up against my (damaged) VonShef tray, the thawing time was still nearly double. My old tray, even with the damage, thawed a 1" T-Bone to room temp in under 1 hour. This tray after 1 hour was still frozen solid in the middle. This was a side-by-side test to make sure I was not giving it an unfair review. I'm sure that those who have used it are impressed with how well it thaws, especially if they are comparing it to refrigerator or even room-temp thawing. That said, spend the extra money, get a tray with deep grooves (the VonShef tray the same size is now back in-stock) and you'll be much happier in the end.

review_title: More than just a chair mat ... FYI, it's RECTANGULAR, not square.
review_text: I like that this mat is perfectly rectangular (NOT SQUARE, with rounded corners) and no protruding portion that goes under the desk. This mat is heavier than some of the chair mats and the bottom has ample and long enough studs to hold it in place on low-pile carpet. I am actually using the mat over our low-pile carpet in front of the sliding glass door in our basement to protect the carpet from rain and snow as people (and animals) track in and out during this very wet season. It is the PERFECT size and shape for this. It can sometimes get a little slick if people track in too much water or snow, but other than that, it is doing a good job of containing the water (so that it can easily be wiped up with towels). It arrives rolled tightly with the top on the outside. Because it was so cold here, it was a little bit of a bear to unroll ... not impossible though. Warmth and sun help it flatten out. Also placing heavy objects around the edges help keep it flattened initially. It is still really cold in my basement (and it's by the door) so it still is curling a little around the ends. It does have a plastic-y smell, but nothing overly noxious, and nothing different than what I've smelled on similar plastic mats. Overall, this seems like a good-quality and durable mat. Definitely for use on low-pile carpets only.

review_title: ONLY for use on low profile rugs or carpeting
review_text: This BRONZEMAN BB0688 Desk Chair Mat for Carpet is ONLY for use on low profile rugs and carpeting but it works very well under those circumstances. I also used a hairdryer on high heat on it and it helped it flatten quickly and completely. This is a transparent mat and it has little plastic cleats all over the bottom side so it cannot be used on hard flooring. But the biggest thing to remember is that it is only for low profile rugs and carpeting - like berber or industrial carpeting. Even a medium pile carpet will prevent your chair from rolling properly on this mat. If you have any question whether your rug pile is low enough, it probably isn't. It does off gas pretty badly when you first open the box so I laid it on the front porch with the books on the corners for a day and the smell was gone. Still, it works great for me and I am pleased with it.

This Duvet cover set is advertised as 100% Egyptian cotton, but the retail packaging only indicates cotton. I think that's an indication that this Duvet set may not be genuine Egyptian cotton. There was a small sticker bar code label that indicated Egyptian, but it could have easily been added at anytime. Generally, Egyptian cotton is a description that indicates a better, if not one of the best grades of cotton. Also, there have been several articles published within the last year that indicate the US market is flooded with fake Egyptian cotton products. For a product to be genuine Egyptian cotton, the cotton must be cultivated and sourced from Egypt. A major source of fake Egyptian cotton is China. This Duvet set has all the characteristics of Chinese manufacture and if so, it's likely made from Chinese cotton marketed as genuine Egyptian cotton. Dazzfond's retail packaging offers no proof that this Duvet set is genuine Egyptian cotton. This will be a one star review until the seller can prove the product matches the advertising.

This Duvet cover set is advertised as 100% Egyptian cotton, but the retail packaging only indicates cotton. I think that's an indication that this Duvet set may not be genuine Egyptian cotton. There was a small sticker bar code label that indicated Egyptian, but it could have easily been added at anytime. Generally, Egyptian cotton is a description that indicates a better, if not one of the best grades of cotton. Also, there have been several articles published within the last year that indicate the US market is flooded with fake Egyptian cotton products. For a product to be genuine Egyptian cotton, the cotton must be cultivated and sourced from Egypt. A major source of fake Egyptian cotton is China. This Duvet set has all the characteristics of Chinese manufacture and if so, it's likely made from Chinese cotton marketed as genuine Egyptian cotton. Dazzfond's retail packaging offers no proof that this Duvet set is genuine Egyptian cotton. This will be a one star review until the seller can prove the product matches the advertising.

The Snore Eliminator PRO is the second chip strap I have purchased to help stop my snoring. The first chip strap (from another company) described the product as “Soft, flexible fabric won't irritate the face.” However, the material did not ‘breathe’ and I woke with my face sweating where the straps touched my cheeks and chin. The Velcro fasteners on the first strap were are smaller and had less ‘grip area.’ Having a smaller head, I found it difficult to fasten so it would remain in place. By contrast, the material in the Snore Eliminator Pro is a soft, non-itchy material that breathes! I sleep comfortably and don’t wake with a damp face! The Velcro straps on the Snore Eliminator PRO are longer than my previous chin strap and better designed. The Velcro straps are incredibly flexible in how you can fasten them. The Snore Eliminator Pro fits my small head and should fit pretty much everyone. After using the Snore Eliminator PRO for a few weeks, I have discovered an unexpected benefit, too! Because the chin strap stops me from breathing through my mouth while asleep, I’ve found my nose is no longer clogged with a bunch of ‘stuff’ and, I no longer experience ‘dry mouth' each morning. I also feel like I’m getting a better night’s sleep because of the strap. I recommend it to anyone who has been told they snore. If you’ve not tried a chin strap before, be aware it may take a bit to become accustomed to wearing. The first night, I took it off about half-way through the night. I honestly made this purchase on a whim. I was looking into purchasing false lashes but I am so tired of the glue and cleaning them and replacing them, so I decided to try magnetic lashes. I always scour Amazon reviews before I buy anything, because I like to see what "real" people have to say about the product. I was about to settle on a different pair of lashes because they had a better overall star rating when I suddenly realized that all of the "reviews" were posted by the same exact "person" on the same exact day, leading me to believe that they were falsified by the seller to achieve a better rating. That being said, I was drawn to these ARVESA lashes because it was very clear that they were fairly popular among the common public. Well, to say I was satisfied is an understatement. The lashes came perfectly packaged and none of them were damaged. They are easy to apply once you get the hang of it (practice before you plan to wear them out!), the e-book directions are very clear/helpful, and they add a ton of volume and length without looking too obviously fake. Lastly, the customer service has been outstanding. The owner of the business has e-mailed me frequently since my purchase to just ensure that I am completely satisfied, and that speaks volumes to me. I guess my only "complaint" (which is not even a complaint at all) is that they are a little long for my personal preference, I think I'm just going to trim them a bit. So if you're looking to try out good quality magnetic lashes without spending a ton, I would highly suggest starting with these!

review_title: Easy to apply and look good
review_text: I’ve bought and tried several magnetic lashes after developing skin sensitivity to mascara in the last few months and these have proven to be the best, by far. Until trying this brand, magnetic lashes were just frustrating. Some took 20 minutes to apply, because they just weren’t shaping to my almond-shaped eyes. Others just looked strange or wouldn’t stay put, and some had magnets on each outer end, so they couldn’t be trimmed. These are narrower, but that makes them much easier to apply and they blend in perfectly with my natural lashes, adding a subtle, beautiful lash thickness and length. The best part is that these take less than a minute to apply and stay on for the whole day (unless I rub my eyes). When I do rub my eyes and the lashes move to a less natural looking spot, it’s a second to remove and easy enough to apply on the go using my phone camera as a mirror.

I am a total amateur at applying false lashes, but these made it so easy!! At first I had a bit of a hard time, but once I figured out to apply the bottom one first & close my eye go hold it, it was a breeze. But before I figured that out I had to pull them off and apart several times. They held up to all of that not so gentle tugging. They are comfortable, I actually forget that I have them on after about thirty mins or so. I would definitely recommend for beginners to experts!

review_title: These are literally the most affordable and most natural looking lashes I've ever owned.
review_text: I didn't have any dislikes about the lashes. They came in this gorgeous case with these cute pink eyelash applicatiors ❤️😊! The thing I love most about these magnetic lashes is that they're affordable! I've tried so many different big brands for these specific magnetic lashes and Arvesa has been hands down the absolute best. The eye lashes are so easy to apply and they actually stay on all day 😍. I haven't had any problems with thinning or fall-out which is incredible 🙌🏾! And the eyelashes definitely look natural! I'll be ordering more products from Arvesa in the near future.

I really dig these! I bought them to fill out my cart, and I wasn't expecting much. I was very pleasantly surprised though! I don't like wearing false lashes because I'm paranoid the glue will rip out my actual lashes, and it just doesn't feel sanitary enough without buying new lashes every time (I know that's probably weird). These are great, though. Takes a little effort to figure out how to use rhem, but honestly not more than it takes to figure out glue-on lashes. And the nice thing is that as you figure it out, if you make a mistake and place it wrong or something, you can easily just take them off and move them. I actually ended up having an easier time using my fingers to apply them than the little tool it comes with, but to each their own. Overall extremely pleased with these!

review_title: Would not buy again, but still better than glue
review_text: I don’t hate them entirely but they are difficult to apply and they don’t not look natural in any sense. I won’t return them cause it’s not worth the hassle considering these were less than $15 but I’m pretty sure I won’t get much use from them. The magnets are meant to be easy to apply but they stick to each other before you can even align them correctly so that creates a problems. They do stay on once they’re applied though and I do like avoiding the mess of glue.

I had never owned a pair of magnetic lashes before. I was reading reviews on magnetic lashes online. Another person he recommended them. I found these on Amazon so I bought them. The company emailed me to let me know they will be coming in the mail and also attached instructions. I was impressed. Then, I received them and received another email from them. Wow, you just don’t find that anymore. It does require practice to put them on and I am still learning, but I love them. It took me a while when I received them to get them on. I loved the way they looked. They are easy to take off when you don’t have them right,too. I am a lash person. I have spent thousands of dollars on mascara. These lashes will boost your lashes to the next level. You will have to practice with them if you are not use to magnetic lashes, like me BUT the results are worth it.

I really like these Lashes. They are easy to use and mess free because you don't have to worry about the glue. I cut them in half because each band has two magnets and it makes them look more natural. They're a good lenght. I'd recommend wearing them with eyeliner to conceal the magnets. The case makes it easy to store them and keeps them safe because it's magnetic too. I really liked that it came with a brush and applicator. Will definitely buy again for the price and quality.

review_title: Great magnetic eyelashes at an amazing price!
review_text: I normally don’t write reviews but I had to come here to recommend these magnetic lashes. First they’re very inexpensive so of course one will be skeptical...but they really work great & look great! They arrived promptly & seller contacted me several times via email to make sure everything arrived well. I honestly didn’t respond because I hadn’t tried them yet. I had seen videos & tutorials on best way to put them on & I knew they would be a little tricky at first so I didn’t wanna be rushed while putting them on for the first time. Yes, they’re tricky, but if you’re patient & practice a few times you’ll be fine. Definitely curl your eyelashes & put on mascara beforehand. That’s a must do tip. These pictures are from tonight, the 2nd time I wear them. Took me a few tries, but I love the outcome & it’s worth the little extra time. I had fake eyelashes put on at a salon & loved the look, but didn’t want to be a slave to it. Plus the glue bugged me after awhile. This product gives me the look without the commitment. Highly recommend!

I've bought these twice now. Easier to use because they are only two magnets and they look natural. I've bought others that made me look like a drag queen lol. These are great. I wouldn't buy any other kind.

review_title: I wanted to love these, but not so much
review_text: After lots of practice at getting these on right, I just don't like them. It looks fake. The lashes are about half the length of my eye, so to the outside corner they are very full and overly-long, while the inside is dramatically less so. My lower lashes look disproportionately skimpy. If you use these, it is a must to set them all of the way to the outside corner of your eye. Otherwise they look, as someone else commented, like a big lump of lash. Really bad. I was excited about the possibility that my lashes would look fuller --all day, even after my mascara wore off -- and that prep time would be shorter. Maybe these other reviewers who love them just look better with them on that do I.

review_title: Don’t let the 4 and 5 stars fool you
review_text: I was eager to get these based on the 4 and 5 star reviews. I’m no stranger to magnetic lashes and got these to replace the ones I’ve had for the last 7 months. The applicator is not easy to use and, in my opinion, makes it harder to apply these lashes. It took servers attempts for me to get these on close to my lash line. When I finally got them on as close as I could get them, they still didn’t look right. They were straight vs curved and unlike my other magnetic lashes, there is no right eye or left eye...so there really is no rhyme or reason on applying these. The quality of the actual lashes seems nice, which is why this review is 2 stars and not 1. I’m honestly super disappointed with these and am wishing I’d just repurchased the lashes I had prior...guess I’ll venture over and order those now. I’d recommend skipping these - there are better lashes on the market that are much easier to apply, are more natural looking, and give a proper curve for your right and your left eye.
These are just the TIPS.. not one full set of lashes. I thought these were a full lash not lash pieces. Over all comfortable, just wish I knew they were not a full lash. Received them fairly quickly!
I found them much easier to use than other falsies have tried in the past. Super cute!

These lashes look great. I've only put them on twice and they ARE difficult to use, but with practice I'm sure it'll be easier every time. The magnets are very strong! The lashes don't move once you have them on properly. They are handmade from silk so they are easy to disfigure. A brush is included, which I used to brush them back into shape. I will probably buy them again since they are not overly long, but long enough to enhance the eye.

I absolutely love these magnetic lashes. I have never tried false eyelashes because my eyelashes used to be quite full. Now that I'm 46, I have noticed my eyelashes are thinner, shorter and my eyes no longer look as bright as they once did. Once I learned how to put the eyelashes on; they look absolutely amazing. It will take time for me getting used to wearing them, but even my sons say I look different; what did I do different......lol........they can't figure it out and I'm not going to tell my secret. Thank you for creating a fantastic product!! They are very inexpensive and truly look like the real deal. I'm ecstatic with the magnetics!!! Thank you, thank you, thank you.

Finally took some time to play with them today. Unfortunately I wish they were a bit longer. My lashes are extremely thin and straight and even after curling them and applying mascara, these look like I only have eyelashes on 1/2 of my eyelid. It looks very unnatural. If they would be just a bit longer I would be happier with this purchase. Also you can see the glue from the magnets on some of the lashes. I love the case and application tool that is included and I did receive a few emails from the seller confirming delivery and asking how I liked them. I would not recommend or purchase these again.

It took me a few tries to get the hang of using magnetic lashes, but I love how they look! They’re saving me lots of money since I used to get my lash extensions done every 2 weeks! They have amazing volume and easy to use once you get the hang of it!

review_title: These fake lashes are way too Narrow and difficult to get apart when you pull them off
review_text: The plastic tweezers are way too sloppy, they don't close evenly and they can easily twist where they don't touch at all! The fake lashes are too narrow, about 5/8" wide and the lashes are too long, they touch the glasses on the inside - they protrude out too far. A nice touch with the set is they have a small red dot on the magnet that matches the other side so you know which sides go together, but when they are together, it is difficult to get them apart safely. I used two pair of needle nose tweezers to pick each side apart. Another nice design idea they have is the case that they come in has 8 separate areas that are metallic so the fake lashes will stick to the area where you put them, so you can keep the upper and lower pieces in sets inside the case. I wish they were longer (covered more of the natural eyelash) and had shorter lashes.

review_title: I found solution to my post chemo lashes!
review_text: These lashes are the answer to my prayers! I went through chemo and my lashes have never been the same. I'm so excited to have full and thick lashes again.

review_title: Trying these on short Asian lashes is Purgatory.
review_text: Unless you already have super long eyelashes, good luck getting these on. These were a complete waste of time and money. If you have short, Asian eyelashes, do not buy these. These would be good for slowly and methodically torturing someone in Dante’s Inferno. It sucks because you have to open the package and try them on to truly appreciate the sadism. By that time, they are used and therefore unreturnable.

Absolutely love this product! Very easy application. Great instruction manual and wonderful packaging! I have wore magnetic eyelashes since they first came out and I have to say these are fabulous and at a great cost!

review_title: DO NOT PASS THESE BY! BUY THESE!
review_text: This is my second time purchasing a set of these! I am in love! By far my favorite magnetic lashes and so easy to put on. Also, I love the upgraded case!

These lashes have been great so far. The applicator is helpful, though I use my hand to put the lashes on most of the time. It takes a few tries to get it down, but that’s the case with all magnetic lashes. These are great for everyday use and can be easily trimmed if you feel they’re too long. I don’t have to worry about them falling off throughout the day. Would highly recommend!

review_title: Lashes are great quality and beautifully natural looking.
review_text: The case works great, and the addition of the applicator tweezers was a nice touch. These are exactly the right length to look stunning without being over-the-top.

I don’t know if maybe it was the lashes I received but the magnets were visible on the lash. So if someone was standing over me, they would be able to see the magnets. Sending them back. There were nothing to distinguish between the top and bottom lashes.

review_title: Instant Beautiful Lashes that Stay Put!
review_text: This is a pleasant surprise. The first set of magnetic lashes were awkward to get on-especially using a regular pair of metal tweezers. Everything was sticking together. After trying for an hour, I Decided to err on the side of caution & not risk putting an eye out. I did more research and found this set, made by Arvesa. These avoid the dangers & inconvenience of metal applicators by including a little plastic pink applicator. After a few minutes, I’d applied a pair of lashes to both eyes in about 10 minutes. I've cut that time in half after a little practice. The case that holds lashes & tools has a magnetic back, so supplies & extra lashes aren’t sliding all over. They are very comfortable, & don’t get in the way of my contact lenses. Not sure if the hair used is real or synthetic, but they’re very soft. I can see myself buying another set when needed.

I was happy that my eyelashes arrived in time for New Years. I had to look at the videos to make sure how to put them on (which was great that they were available). I was a little nervous at first because with other fake lashes I had not had to put on mascara, that said since they are only for half of your eyelashes it definitely helps them blend. The only thing that I have noticed after wearing them for a while is that they had moved down on my eyelash. It was easy to just push them back (see the photo where it looks like they slid and then with a quick push they were fine). That said some tips I learned is that the side with the red dots is the lower lash, putting the lash closest to the edge of your lash can be tough but wait about a minute after you have put on the mascara so that you don’t get too much mascara on your finger. I am sure as I use them more I will get more used to them.

Really loving these! It took me a couple tries but I found it easiest if you put the top layer on and hold it to your lashes (with mascara on) and pull your lid out slightly from your eye so you can then place the lower layer of lashes on more easily. It will take some getting used to the feeling of the extra weight on my lashes but they look great!

This was my first time using magnetic eyelashes and I didn’t want to spend a fortune nor did I want to completely cheap out either. I figured these would be the best options. They feel like good quality eyelashes and the come in a case so they will last much longer. I attempted a few times to put them on with no luck. I ended up looking for a YouTube video to help me. I was able to get them on with a few tips. The easiest way to put them on is to curl your natural eyelash, apply your mascara, grab the top fake lash with you fingers and place as close to your eyelid as possible. Grab the bottom fake lash with the pink tweezers that come with your magnetic lashes and place underneath your real lash. After I got them on I really like the way they look. I know some ppl said they didn’t like the way they lay but I actually bent mine a little bit to fit my eyelid so that helps. They are not the most natural looking but for 15 they look good. I only gave 3 stars because how long it took me to be able to put them on and the box they come in was not labeled left lid or right lid. They are not bad for the price, especially after you figure out how to put them on.
I received wonderful instructions from this company on how to apply these lashes. Now that I know how to properly apply them, I LOVE the way they look!!

I have worn these lashes everyday since I've received them in my order, and though it hasn't been that long I'm already loving these lashes. I have been wearing eyelash extensions for almost a year prior and I wanted to hold off on getting extensions in again so that my natural lashes can heal. I decided to try magnetic lashes because I don't like how glue feels on my lids. These lashes are not like a full set, more like a natural cat eye kind of set where they are ideally placed at the outer edges of your eyes. It's a pretty nice natural look. I liked the length as well, but not sure if it may be too long for some. The packaging is nice and it comes with a little note from the seller and instructions on how to put them on. I did have some difficulty at first but when I read the instructions, it all came to me so easily. The trick is to apply the bottom lashes first, align them to where you would like, and close your eye. Then apply the top set as close to the lid as possible. After a day it took me not more than 15 seconds to apply them on one eye. I did do it on bare lashes, but it would probably look better with mascara and some curling. They are relatively easy to clean as I've been just swishing it in cleansing water makeup remover, and pat drying it. I see these lasting a long time, since there are 2 sets for each eye per order. I'll most likely be using these as daily lashes. All in all this is worth it for the low price.

review_title: oh I am in love with this shop and the owner!
review_text: Wonderful lady! she made my mother (Amanda) very happy today and me as well. Nice personality, great product. We will buy more from her!

I was looking for a middle ground between glued fake lashes & lash extensions. Unfortunately, there's nothing I loved about these lashes. They don't look natural and application is difficult, even when using the applicator. I wouldn't mind this much if they looked good but the only way in which they would look acceptable is if people were looking at you by standing right in front of you the whole time. If someone looks at you from the side, or if you blink or look down (aka any natural position), the magnets are EXTREMELY VISIBLE! There's no way they can be concealed on your lashline. I'll be returning this product ASAP.

I was a little skeptical about buying, because of some of the reviews. Ive actually tried other magnetic, and these are the best. Easy to apply after learning to how do it a couple times. After a couple hours they slip off, but super easy to get back on and to be expected (walking around/moving and such.) They look like if you were to get eyelash extensions, and make you look like, for lack of a better word a “bad b**ch.” Will be getting again. Also, the case it comes in is magetic, so that’s really nice too!!

I was so bummed because I have my first interview in like 8 years and I was super sad because I got fake lashes with glue, the glue was super harmful to me and it tore of my lashes and some lid it hurt real bad! I was sad on how I would look but these lashes are beautiful and made me look so good I feel confident and will treat my eyelashes with oils in the meantime in hopes of growth. I'm great full and happy I had this as an option. Also happy that it's a family owned business and I got an email from them it was nice to know they care for each of us.

review_title: Hopefully I can make them work
review_text: The lashes are only half length which is disappointing because they are entirely too long to look okay they must be cut in half. I haven’t actually gotten them put on in a satisfying way yet I hope if I keep at it I can figure it out it’s partly due because I have thick long lashes so I have to get through tangled lashes (my bottom constantly get tangled with top). The instructions are completely wrong. They stated to put the bottom lashes on the bottom lash line and top on top lash line. Completely wrong. Your supposed to put the bottom lashes underneath your top lash line and top lash connecting the lashes into a essentially a lash sandwich on your top lash line only. Nothing goes into bottom lashes and I had to watch a video on YouTube to instantly understand the instructions were way wrong. I do not recommend this brand
They are life ! I love my set ! Wear them all the time!!

review_title: As good as it gets without extensions
review_text: These are amazing… I was looking for an alternative to the expense of extensions because I do BJJ and after one or two rolls they are all ripped out. These are great because I can take them off and just go to class without long lashes and then put them back on whenever I want. As another review were noted yes, once you get close it is more obvious but again people getting that close to my face already know. Be careful when you put them on initially they don’t curve like your normal eyes so definitely align the outer, I emphasize outer, one first list nap and then do the inner one I scratched my cornea once or twice trying to get them on, (but I also have a more sensitive cornea due to eye surgery) regardless follow the instructions and get ready to bat those lashes!!!

I enjoy these lashes. First off, the face the correct direction, meaning the lower lash magnets face up and the upper lash magnets face down. I cannot tell you how many times the cheaper magnetic lashes have magnets all facing the same direction, mostly down. They still work, but in terms of them blending into you natural lashes it looks awful. These lashes have the magnets where they should be and that's fantastic. I trim mine down a little - both in length of the 'hair' and the length of the strip - to make them blend with my natural lashes better. Overall, great lashes.

Takes some practice to get the application down, but that goes with with all magnetic lashes I suppose. Once on, they look great and light weight enough to be comfortable. I haven’t work them out for the day yet, but they feel secure enough to stay out so far. Would recommend and buy again.

This is the first pair I've been able to put on relatively easily! It's because they only go on the ends, so I don't poke my eye when I hold the bottom lashes. They look great in photos. Since they give you an extra pair I could experiment with trimming them. I'm using them for a cosplay.

review_title: Far too thick, poor quality product
review_text: Bottom-line up front: I am experienced with magnetic lashes. The quality of the product is inconsistent and does not look attractive when worn. Several months ago, I received my first pair of magnetic eyelashes as a gift. I instantly became a believer! When I decided to replace the old pair with the ARVESA 8x False Magnetic Eyelashes, I was excited to find what appeared to be a quality product for a good price. However, I was sorely disappointed. The thickness, styling, and length of each individual lash varies widely, making them hard to match as a pair for each eye. Additionally, once doubled up, they are far too thick and are clearly seen when worn. I attempted to mix, match, and trim eyelashes to improve their appearance, but I will not be wearing these lashes in the future and regret my purchase.

review_title: Step by step instruction as to how to apply these amazing lashes?!?!
review_text: I was skeptical when ordering these, due to ordering other magnetic lashes and feeling highly disappointed when they wouldn’t go on.... if they did, they didn’t stay on!!! The Arvesa brand are AMAZING!! It comes with a tool to help apply them!! So easy and so very BEAUTIFUL!!! I can’t wait to order again!!! Thanks ARVESA.... my being skeptical was short lived!!! Full of excitement!!!

review_title: Great Accent lashes and Even Better Customer Service
review_text: Ok so I am sick of spending so much time on my mascara every morning that I have tried eye lash extensions, which are nice but honestly a really big hassle and expense! So now I am on to magnectic lashes, I have bought who knows how many different kinds and either they look horrible or a real pain to get on or heavy. I almost gave up on buying anymore of those and went back to the extensions, thay is until I ordered these! They look and feel nice and super easy to put on. Remember though they are an accent lash and not a full lash(which in my opinion look better and more natural than the full magnectic lashes). I have not been disappointed. Now on to customer service, I have never seen an owner who has personally sent emails to make sure that you are happy with your purchase, but that's what Harsh(the owner of Arvesa) does, that tells me she really cares about the quality of her product and hapiness of her clients, how many companies or people can you honestly think of that do? I recommend you try these and if you are unhappy she will make sure that you will be. This is just my opinion

I'm so disappointed with these. Unless you already have really long lashes, these will look unnatural. I noticed this in one of the pictures in a review, but she said they looked natural in real life. They don't. I need lashes that will cover my whole lid, and that have a shorter lash length.
Trimmed the length a bit to get them exactly like i wanted them. SO pleased with this product!

I was a bit worried to try magnetic lashes because I wear contacts and one of the strip goes underneath the lash line, but it hasn’t irritated my eyes at all. Just like with strip lashes, these do take a bit of practice. I would recommend putting on a couple of coats of mascara so the top lashes have something to adhere to. And make sure to hold the bottom lashes so you don’t have to look down while the top lashes are on. This prevents them from slipping off.

Was very skeptical about these but they’re awesome ! It takes a little bit to get used to them though .. putting them on was hard the first few times but you figure it out quick. My suggestion is closing one eye, putting the lash underneath with your eye shut and then connecting the second eyelash from the top. High quality, comes in a cute protective hard carrying case so you won’t lose them.

The lashes are of 'Just OK' looking quality, the strands at the ends are sometimes splayed everywhere. The magnets themselves are fine, and they do stay in place. They're also not quite long enough to blend in properly with regular eyelashes, there's an obvious 'line' where you can tell where the magnetic lashes start and your real ones end, even when brushed out. Overall, though, these are decent lashes-- but not the best.

I wanted to like these, I have tried the ones with the single magnet and thought I would like a double magnet better. I think I’m going back to try the single. These are actually too strong… Once I get them attached, it’s very difficult to get them off to adjust them, and you never get it on right the first time. At least I don’t.

First time using false lashes. Pretty easy to apply (I didn't even need the applicator tool.) Stayed in place. A little on the long side, but Blended well with my natural lashes after adding extra mascara.

review_title: I CAN'T BELIEVE THESE ACTUALLY WORK!
review_text: I'm totally stoked that these magnetic eyelashes actually work. They totally put the cherry on top to my makeup look! It took a few tries to get them on, but once you get the hang of it, they're pretty easy to use. They don't feel heavy or itchy. I hardly even notice I'm wearing them. It's important to note that these are accent eyelashes, not a full strip.

I had to trim the very last hair on several because they were strangely too long. The tweezer really is worthless. The Ardell one is much better. Hairs should be more crossed. One of the eyelasses had some glossy glue by the magnet which I don't know how to remove but is quite visible.

I really like this lashes, it's bit tricky to put them on but once you got the hang of it, is a piece of cake it'll just take practice. This lashes are super economic and are great. I'm still getting the hang of these but they are gorgeous and look super naturals and the PRICE!!! WORTH. IT. *You can notice the difference on the first pic: one eye with magnetic lashes the other without. Second pic: both lashes ON.

review_title: Definitely need to practice putting these on..
review_text: Love the concept! I've always loved false lashes, but never liked/have been good with the glue. It does take some practice to get used to applying, but still easier than glue for me. I like that they're partial lashes, but since my natural lashes are short & thin, it looks weird in me if I don't add eyeshadow or eyeliner as well. (I may trim one set to see if that works too) Overall, I like these lashes & will keep an eye out for other lashes from this company.

Never used magnetic lashes before kind of bought them on a whim they had pretty good reviews so I will see if I can make them work and well Force comes to worse I can always return them. However came in a nice bubble envelope in a plastic sealed package and they're very very pretty looking

My girlfriend was interested in trying these since she is sensitive to glue near her eye. The results were spectacular! Not only were these high quality lashes, but the magnetic closure was ingenious and offered her a perfect way to use false eyelashes without irritating her eyes. Highly recommend!

review_title: The eye lashes are Perfect, good size
review_text: The eye lashes are Perfect, good size... i like the case with the magnet... only I have to try the applicator, i don't know how to use... thanks. Shipping on time

review_title: Easy to apply and stay on!
review_text: I love these lashes and am so happy I bought them. I have been using glue lashes for years and hate they leave glue in my lashes, have to wait til they dry right or reapply, and sometimes they peel off during the day. These have stay put! I applied them quickly with my bare hands. Unlike the directions, I placed a top lash on top of mine first, and then pushed it as far against the lash line as possible paying attention to each end. I then held them in place and lifted them up, punching them with my natural lashes, while I clicked the bottom set it into place underneath. I look forward to more magnetic styles coming out!

I gave up!!! I did everything they said to do. Too hard as the top one does not sit properly on the lash line. You cannot adjust it after you put the bottom one one. Also, it looks too fake. They need to fuse the upper and lower lashes together so we can slide it in between our own lashes. Figure out how not to have the magnets together until it is lined up properly!
These are great! A little difficult to master the technique of getting them on just right, but they look great once you do!

review_title: Tough little light with some neat features
review_text: We have a lot of lanterns of various sizes that we use for tent lights, for car lights, and sometimes just as a nightlight. This one is pretty good. The amber almost makes it seem like a candle and its a nice mode for all through the night when you wake up in the middle of the night and don't want your night vision too messed up. You can even pretend its a candle if you really squint. The only real big issue is the elegance of it. I know thats silly but when you're comparing it to other products, like a Snow Peak lantern or traditional gas powered lantern its just a little too function. Its a little big for its throw and the orange/black/white isn't the most attractive color scheme. So id say this is more geared to be an emergency light than a camping but only slightly.

review_title: An Efficient, Well Designed, And Effective Lamp
review_text: I wish that we would have had six of these when Hurricane Irma knocked out our power for six days. They are compact, cast enough light to read by in total darkness, and function perfectly as a night light for those quiet evenings when you're trying to get your mind around what just happened. The second of the three intensities is almost as bright as the highest setting and would be suitable for just about anything short of reading. Just make sure to have a bunch of AA batteries handy. Compact battery powered LED lanterns are safer , much easier to use, and cast more light than any candle. When you have children around you looking for some safety at night, this pleasant little lamp generates a nice little circle of security and comfort. My only quibble is the price. It would seem to be priced more realisticly at around $10.00.

review_title: Not happy w/using batteries, & glow in the dark not so glowy, but otherwise quite decent
review_text: Aside from a couple of minor issues, I'm liking this a lot. The bright setting is quite decent for a camping/emergency situation. It'll fill up a tent well, or a canopy-covered area just fine. The medium and nite light settings could be useful in plenty of situations. Its compact-ness is quite decent. The listing pix show it well enough, so I won't duplicate, but you can see it packs down quite well. No glass to break - always a plus in camping. The hook is a useful touch. The 2 issues that, combined, I'm taking 1 star off for are: 1. It needs batteries. Maybe we'll forever be tied to them, but I'd really rather see emergency/camping gear move to solar or electric charge-able. Batteries add an unreliable factor, and also substantial weight (relatively). 2. The glow in the dark thing was way over hyped. It's like any other glow in the dark thing - it needs to be charged. I tried gradually increasing times, but even after leaving the light on high for 30 mins I got only 4 mins of glow in the dark for it. Not a useful function, for me. Other than those 2 issues, I really do like this. I'll update if any durability issues pop up, but otherwise it's quite decent.

Let's face it, there's a lot of gimmicky LED lights out there. They mostly make bold, wild, unfounded claims. This UST Spright lantern is surprisingly very good. It uses 3-AA batteries and measures 4.75 x 3.5 x 3.5 inches (HxWxD) expanded, 2.75 x 3.5 x 3.5 when collapsed. The weight is 7 ounces with batteries. The diameter is very similar to a hockey puck. There's an integrated hook for hanging from a branch, tent pole, camper support...you name it. It does have a nice glow when first started in high mode. I couldn't tell much of a difference between high and medium modes. The nightlight mode reminds me of a candle. Very subtle light, but adequate once your eyes are adjusted for night vision. The glow in the dark feature is awesome as well and lasts about 10 minutes. Just enough to tell monster stories before falling asleep at camp. The batteries are supposed to last 30 hours on high and 5 days on low. Very impressive stats. All-in-all, it's a nifty LED lantern for camping or other outdoor activities. I will use my lantern for emergency power outages, mostly from hurricanes. Not bad for 14 bucks.

review_title: Outstanding little lantern! Many great features!
review_text: This is an excellent portable lamp. It has several features that I really like. First, the collapsible silicone shade is very easy to use and easily pops in and out of position as needed. Second, the lantern is very light, making it easy to carry around. Third, the lantern is relatively small, making it easy to pack. Fourth, my oversized 2800mAh rechargeable AA batteries fit easily into the battery slots and actually work (I can't say that for many of the other portable lanterns I own that use AA batteries as sometimes even though the larger, 2800 mAh AA battery will still fit in the battery space, for some reason they will not work). Fifth, the lantern puts out a lot of light and the light is not glaring or too bright. The silicone portion does absorb light and will emit a light, greenish glow when the lantern is turned off but this effect is not permanent and only lasts several hours if there is little or no other ambient light for the silicone to absorb.

review_title: Handy if you want to be seen in the dark
review_text: This light will come in handy if you're an early or late walker, jogger or bicyclist and need to be seen by motorists. There's a clip on it so you can hang the light from a belt, backback, bike rack or the toggle of a walking stick. It's light weight, with the most weight coming from the 3 AA batteries. The white silicon top collapses and raises easily. When on it lights up bright, softly and with an amber glow. When off it glows a soft green in the dark. The soft lighting isn't going to allow you to see anything, but it'll tell others you're there. At the brightest setting it's good for seeing a small space. If you need to dig around in your trunk after dark this will light up the area surrounding the light. It doesn't give off enough light to shine in front of you to see where you're walking like a flashlight does. But, unlike a flashlight you can set this down and get light without blinding everyone around.

review_title: Lightweight, It Folds and It puts out a Decent Amount of Light
review_text: Lightweight and the white part folds up into the base so it takes up very little room in your bags. It puts out a moderate amount of light. Certainly enough to see to get undressed and into bed. I like that it has a built in hanger and the white part glows after shutting out the main light. I'd rather have just a bit of ambient light in the tent for awhile when camping since otherwise it's just pitch black and if I should have to get up to use the bathroom, I can see without stepping all over stuff and it's much less jarring that flipping on the flashlight. I would recommend this little light. Thank you to Amazon and the Maker/Vendor for letting me give this a try.

review_title: Handy and convenient for camping and other activities
review_text: My wife had earlier bought a two-pack of collapsible LED lanterns from LL Bean and it turns out that these were also made by UST and are still smaller versions of this Spright model. The Spright takes three AA batteries (the LL Bean version uses AAA cells) and is quite bright on even the medium setting. My wife says that the "candle" mode was perfect when she was tenting with her sister - it's not just dimmer, but also yellow. Unlike the LL Bean model, though, the Spright's candle mode doesn't flicker (like a real candle) and the Spright also lacks the ridiculous color changing "party mode" of its smaller sibling. The glowing shell is great after you turn out the lights.

We didn't expect much if this light, to be honest but found it quite useful and even charming in an odd way. The collapsible silicone is a useful concept for packing this in a backpack or even storing in a glove box. It is much lighter and smaller than the LED lanterns we normally use. The clip on the bottom is also more versatile than other lanterns we own. I'm afraid this is going to end up in the hubby's kayak gear which means I will be buying more. The three light levels are handy, too. I am thinking this would be great for an emergency preparedness kit, too, with it's compact versatility.

review_title: Great light for our Hurricane supply kit
review_text: We juse got through Hurricane Irma in Florida and the pre-hurricane planning involved making sure our emergency supplies were on hand. Among those emergency supplies are various lanterns and flashlights. Among the bunch is this one. This is a space-saving collapsible lantern with a expandable silicone top. The silicone actually glows in the dark if the light has been on a while. It is about the size of two stacked hockey pucks when collapsed. There is a hook / handle on the bottom that is helpful for carrying and hanging. Functional lantern that gives off nice light and has multiple settings.

review_title: Bright, compact, and easy to pack!
review_text: A very cute and effective lantern! Collapsed it's about the size of a hockey puck. When you pop it up, and power it on, it provides an ample amount of light for a medium-sized room or tent, or varying degrees of lesser light to work as anything down to a child's nightlight. It's versatile, too! It can hang easily with integrated hook, and packs up quickly unlike old fashioned lanterns with fixed domes. A must-have for any camper, or just for keeping in your car for emergencies. Five stars. There's nothing to dislike here.

review_title: This camping lantern comes in very handy when going out ...
review_text: This camping lantern comes in very handy when going out into the woods or just using it to light up underneath your desk to fix something. The lantern has 3 modes, high, low and amber night light. The high is what you want to use for normal work, low is for just before bed time and the amber night light is just that, barely enough light to let you see the shapes around you. This conveniently takes 3 AAs and lasts for many hours before needed a recharge. It collapses into a small puck and is light enough to take on every trip.

I purchased this locally, but wanted to review it. It's a great light. Lots of light, two settings and it glows in the dark which is a cool plus. I love the silicone "globe" that pulls out to give it more of an area light feel versus a flashlight. I paid $14.99 and it's worth twice that when compared to what other lights sell for in the backpacking/camping game. Lanterns/lights/flashlights for whatever reason are typically overpriced and can sometimes under-deliver. Not this one. It's underpriced and OVER-delivers. Buy one and you won't regret it.

I got this for my son who is a Scout and camps once a month. It's lightweight, collapsible, sturdy and bright. All the requisites of a "must have" piece of equipment. His complaint was that it was so bright the senior patrol leader saw it from several meters away and told them to go to bed. So not much of a complaint when you put it into context.

review_title: Collapsible Lantern Great for Power Outages
review_text: The UST Spright Collapsible LED Lantern was designed for camping as it is battery operated and will provide bright lighting for up to 30 hours. We are not campers, though, but acquired this product for emergency use in case of power failure and after testing it I am persuaded it will work quite well. I took it into our guest room during evening hours with shade drawn and door shut. When you click the lantern on by default the first position is bright. The illumination from this small lantern was sufficient that I could see everything in the room and could function quite well for 30 hours without power. Besides bright, the lantern has two other modes (low and amber nightlight) and can operate on three AA batteries for up to five days on nightlight. It glows in the dark when shut off so we will be able to find it easy on our small desk when the power goes out. For those who use the lantern for camping, it is water resistant and has a hook to hang from the top of the tent for maximum illumination. The illumination ability is 100 lumens at high mode, 50 lumens at low, and 10 lumens at amber nightlight. Ultimate Survival Technologies (UST) has been making camping equipment for more than 80 years.

review_title: Great Oil Mister/Sprayer to use less oil in your cooking
review_text: I decided to purchase this as we are trying to use less oil in our cooking. I have some really nice Circulon pans and had been using PAM cooking spray on them. What I found was that the PAM was gunking up the pans after a while leaving a residue and messing up the non-stick properties. Seems there is more than just oil on those cans. When I got around to looking at the instructions on one of my Circulon pans it specifically stated not to use sprays like PAM on them. This little beauty of a device can spray a pretty fine mist of pure cooking oil (we are using canola) on the bottom of a pan which coats it just enough to help with browning of meats & veggies but without using very much oil at all. I've cooked salmon, chicken and veggies so far with great results. I spay the bottom of the pan before putting it on the heat, then maybe spray a little more on top of the protein or veggies to coat. This is an aerosol device, not a 'pump' type sprayer (think spray paint -vs- windex). You have to 'pump' up some air pressure into the sprayer using the top cover then just press the button to spray the contents. You have to pump it up every time you use it and I typically give it a good 8 to 10 pumps. Overall I'm very satisfied with this Oil Mister from MB Lifestyle. It looks good sitting next to my stove top and works great.

The product arrived, looked fantastic and I was super excited to use it. Put the oil in and it would only bubble out. I submitted a return request for a defective product and they sent me a new one.
